title: Report Codex Desktop read state to the shared owner
body:
## Outcome

When you read a finished Codex Desktop task in Codex, consumers that honor read evidence stop showing it as unread. Legacy Nanoleaf did this, and shared mode lost it. The owner reports the state as `read.observed`. Notices and acknowledgments do not change.

## Why

[Nanoleaf #74](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/74) traced the wall's growing unread count to this gap. #195 expires sessions after 24 hours without activity, which stops the growth. But a task you have already read in Codex still shows unread until you acknowledge it or it expires.

## Source (checked September 23, 2026)

- Codex Desktop uses the Windows Codex home, `C:\Users\<user>\.codex` (`/mnt/c/Users/<user>/.codex` from WSL), not WSL `~/.codex`.
- In `.codex-global-state.json`, `electron-thread-read-state-v1.unreadByIdentity` holds one list of unread thread IDs, nested under a host key and a `local:` key. The IDs match Desktop session IDs.
- The list names only unread sessions. Nothing lists read ones.
- The older key that legacy Nanoleaf reads, `electron-persisted-atom-state.unread-thread-ids-by-host-v1`, no longer exists. The format can change again.
- No hook reports reads, and a Linux file watcher on `/mnt/c` receives no events. The poller therefore checks the file's modification time and size every few seconds and parses the file (about 3 MB) only when they change.

## Scope

- [ ] Add a read-only poller to the owner for Codex Desktop sessions (`provider: codex`, `client: desktop`) and a configured file path.
- [ ] A listed session is `unread`. A session missing from a successfully parsed list is `read` if it was listed earlier or its latest turn ended at least 5 seconds ago. Desktop sets the flag shortly after Stop, and legacy Nanoleaf used the same 5-second wait.
- [ ] A missing, unreadable or unexpectedly shaped file produces no events. If the format changes again, the poller goes quiet instead of guessing.
- [ ] Emit only when a session's state changes. This keeps the journal small and does not keep sessions alive under #195.
- [ ] Never touch sessions from other clients or providers. Only `read` or `unread` for known sessions leaves the poller.
- [ ] Record the source and the read rule in [docs/provider-qualification.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/provider-qualification.md).

The owner already stores `read.observed` ([reducer.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/reducer.ts#L160)). After a new completion, Desktop lists the session again and it returns to unread, so no reducer change is expected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fixture tests cover:
  - a listed session
  - an unlisted session after the wait
  - an unlisted session within the wait that was never listed
  - a missing or malformed file
  - an unchanged file
  - a new completion after read
  - a non-Desktop session
- [ ] Live: read a finished task in Codex Desktop and see Nanoleaf's unread indicator clear. One closing comment records it.

## Dependencies

None. Nanoleaf already hides its unread indicator for `read: read`. #218 uses the same configured Codex home.

## Not included

Changes to notice retention, clearing notices by age (#195 covers expiry), bulk acknowledgment, Claude read evidence, consumer-side provider logic and writing Codex state.

## Readiness

Complexity small. Uncertainty low. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Expire monitoring sessions after 24 hours without activity
body:
## Outcome

The shared owner forgets any session that has had no new agent evidence for 24 hours. That frees owner capacity, which fixes the capacity failure blocking [Tidbyt #21](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/21). It also clears stale rows from the wall, Tidbyt, Pixoo and the dashboard. New activity later creates a fresh entry.

Removing archived Codex tasks sooner is split out to #218.

## Owner policy (September 23, 2026)

- The full session identity stays the monitoring key. Subagents remain separate records.
- Expiry forgets monitoring state. It does not acknowledge, mark read, complete or cancel anything. It applies to sessions with open notices or attention too.
- Expiry may drop task labels, manual task-project associations, Line placement and animation state. Global projects, colors, reservations, scenes, device settings and agent conversations stay.
- New activity after expiry creates a record with defaults. Old effects are not replayed.
- The 128-record limit stays. It counts children.

## Design

The owner already has most of what this needs:

- **Clock.** Use each session's `lastEvidenceAtMs`. It is saved with the session and set only when an event is applied ([reducer.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/reducer.ts#L172)). Duplicates, labels and acknowledgments do not change it, and a restart does not reset it.
- **Timing.** Expire alongside the existing 24-hour journal pruning ([index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L59)), at startup, and before rejecting a new identity at capacity. Real rejections still count as loss.
- **Late events.** `runtime.ended` never creates a record, and the owner drops events observed before the 24-hour cutoff. Old events therefore cannot refill freed slots.
- **Children.** Each record expires on its own clock, with no cascade. Child counts are derived from the records present ([children.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/children.ts)), so a missing parent or child does not break the snapshot.
- **Consumers.** The snapshot format does not change; expired sessions just disappear. Nanoleaf deletes a missing task's rows, which this policy accepts. The existing resync resets of animations are also accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fake-clock test fills the owner to 128, expires old records, admits new identities and continues past 128 lifetime identities.
- [ ] Tests cover:
  - just before and at 24 hours
  - renewal by a new event
  - no renewal from labels or acknowledgments
  - a restart that keeps the window
- [ ] `runtime.ended` for an unknown identity creates nothing. Events older than the cutoff are dropped. A new start after expiry creates a fresh record.
- [ ] Expired notices and attention disappear without an acknowledgment. Other sessions and global settings are unchanged.
- [ ] Nanoleaf and the dashboard handle a child whose parent expired.
- [ ] Installed: back up the owner database, update the service, and confirm that old sessions leave and `lossCount` stops rising. Then finish the #21 display checks. One comment records this.

## Related work

#191 (read evidence) and #218 (archive removal) are independent follow-ups. [Nanoleaf #80](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/80) groups children for display but frees no capacity. The UI work in Nanoleaf [#75](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/75), [#76](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/76) and [#77](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/77) can proceed on its own. #123, #138 and #139 keep their separate scopes.

## Not included

Archive removal, changes to the per-session notice limit, a cleanup UI, restoring expired tasks, synthetic lifecycle events and a live database reset.

## Readiness

Complexity small to medium: an owner change plus tests. Uncertainty low. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Prepare Codex and Claude task briefs from the mobile work guide
body:
Owner: Hub guide source.

Outcome: open any issue in the guide on a phone or desktop, pick an action and copy a short prompt that starts that work in an existing Codex or Claude app. Plan starts the `plan-work` skill; Implement starts `deliver-work`.

## Scope

- Selecting an issue badge (`a.issue[data-issue]`) opens one native `<dialog>` with the repository, number, title, a GitHub link and four actions: Explain, Plan, Implement and Review. Each action shows its prompt in a read-only textarea with a Copy button. Update the search hint that says issue links open GitHub.
- Build prompts in the browser from the badge's existing key, URL and title. Reference the full issue URL and embed no snapshot context: the agent reads the live issue and the repository's AGENTS.md.
- Prompt templates. Delivery may tune the wording but keeps the skill names and scope limits:
  - Explain: `Explain <issue URL> ("<title>"). Read the issue and the repository's AGENTS.md first. Read-only: don't change files, branches or GitHub.`
  - Plan: `Use the plan-work skill for <issue URL>. Planning only: return proposals and don't change the tracker until I approve. If plan-work isn't available here, say so and stop.`
  - Implement: `Use the deliver-work skill to deliver <issue URL>. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.`
  - Review: `Review the open pull request for <issue URL>. If there isn't exactly one, ask me which revision to review. Read-only: report findings without changing files or GitHub.`
- Expose `openBrief(key)` so [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201) can open the same dialog.

Implement uses the deliver-work default finish line (merged PR and closed issue). Edit the pasted prompt to set a narrower limit.

## Acceptance

1. Selecting a Hub, Nanoleaf or Pixoo badge opens the dialog with the correct repository, number, title and URL, and the GitHub link still works. Escape and Close dismiss the dialog and return focus to the badge. At 390 px the page does not overflow.
2. Each prompt uses the full issue URL. Explain and Review state read-only scope; Plan names `plan-work` and planning-only scope; Implement names `deliver-work`. Titles render as text, not markup.
3. Copy writes the prompt to the clipboard. If the Clipboard API is denied or unavailable, including when the guide is opened from `file://`, the textarea text is selected for manual copying.

Evidence: one new `check_guide.cjs` case covering these criteria at 390 px, plus the existing `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py` and `check_guide.cjs` runs. No live agent or device test.

## Delivery

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md) and the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). All changes stay under `docs/work-guide/`, so the guide-only CI exception applies and no human UI approval is needed. No product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change.

Uses current guide styles; [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) and [#86](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/86) do not block it. [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197) is independent. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result.

Out of scope: embedded outcome, acceptance, dependency or atlas context; Codex/Claude destination labels; user-entered notes; deep links; app launch URLs; GitHub writes. This issue does not verify that a given app session can load `plan-work` or `deliver-work`; that depends on the user's agent setup.

Assessment: complexity low, uncertainty low, impact low (client-side copy only). Ready for source delivery.

title: Show current public GitHub status in the dated guide
body:
Owner: Hub guide source.

Outcome: when the guide opens, its issue badges show current status read directly from GitHub, with one line saying when that status was read. If GitHub can't be reached, the guide keeps its snapshot status and says so.

## Scope

- On page load, send anonymous GitHub REST requests for `agent-device-hub`, `codex-nanoleaf` and `divoom-app-upgrade`:
  - open issues: `/repos/jimmie-potts/<repo>/issues?state=open&per_page=100`
  - issues closed since the snapshot: `/repos/jimmie-potts/<repo>/issues?state=closed&since=<snapshot refreshedAt>&per_page=100`

  Follow `Link` pagination and skip pull requests. All three repositories are public, and the API allows browser requests without sign-in (`access-control-allow-origin: *`, 60 requests an hour per IP). Checked on September 23, 2026.
- Port the `guide_status.py` rules to the page:
  - closed with `state_reason` `completed` → Completed; other closures → Closed
  - `status:review` → In review; `status:in-progress` → In progress
  - `blocked` label or `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0` → Blocked. `blocked_by` counts open blockers only; `total_blocked_by` also counts closed ones.

  Update each badge's symbol, status text, `data-state`, `data-status`, `title` and `aria-label`.
- Add one freshness line, for example "Status from GitHub at 14:32. Guide text and counts from the 23 Sep snapshot." or "GitHub unavailable; showing 23 Sep snapshot status."
- Update the guide intro sentence that says the guide loads nothing remote.
- No refresh button: reloading the page refreshes status.

## Acceptance

1. When every read succeeds, each badge shows the status the ported rules give for the live data, and the freshness line shows the read time. Guide prose, counts and "Waiting for" text keep their snapshot values, and the page labels them as snapshot values.
2. Missing data never changes a status. If any read for a repository fails, including 403 or 429 rate limiting, that repository's badges keep snapshot status and the freshness line names the repository. An issue absent from both reads keeps its snapshot status.
3. The page renders completely without the requests. Offline and `file://` use fall back to snapshot status without console errors. Values from GitHub are written as text, not markup.

Evidence: `check_guide.cjs` cases with routed fake API responses covering a closed issue, a newly blocked issue, an issue in review, a second results page and one failed repository, plus the existing `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py` and `check_guide.cjs` runs. Update the check's external-request expectation to allow only GET requests to `api.github.com`.

## Delivery

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md) and the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). All changes stay under `docs/work-guide/`, so the guide-only CI exception applies and no human UI approval is needed. No product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change.

Independent of [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85), [#86](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/86) and [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196). [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201) can read the updated badge `data-status` values. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result.

Out of scope: a collector or export command, a status schema or published status file, status in the atlas, pull request, review or check summaries, recounting guide totals, scheduled refresh ([#200](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/200) is closed as not planned), authenticated requests, and new issues that the guide doesn't already list.

title: Replay recorded delivery history without inventing system state
body:
Owner: Hub guide history/timeline.

Outcome: scrub through verified delivery milestones with brief neon highlights and direct links to their evidence.

Acceptance and planned evidence:

1. Use recorded timestamps/revisions and the existing history inputs. Selecting a date shows the milestones known at that point; timestamp ties have deterministic ordering. Distinguish source merge, installation, and physical acceptance where evidence exists. Fixture checks cover out-of-order, missing, and simultaneous events.
2. A milestone card links its source. Do not reconstruct historical dependency topology from today's graph or infer a component existed at a date without records. Missing topology becomes a milestone-only timeline, not guessed assembly animation.
3. Play, pause, step, and scrub stay synchronized, work with keyboard/touch, and respect reduced motion, offscreen suspension, and print. Browser tests cover boundary dates and no-history cases.
4. Retain snapshot date and uncertainty labels; measure mobile interaction before publication. Exclude achievement scores, productivity comparisons, live telemetry, and automatically treating every guide-only merge as a product milestone.

Locations: `work/history/github-history.json`, `timeline.py`, guide browser checks. Required data already exists; validate coverage during delivery. [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) supplies preferred visual consistency but is not a semantic blocker for an existing-style timeline. Coordinate shared timeline edits with [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201). This is a deferred optional release, not part of the first public milestone.

Assessment: complexity medium; uncertainty medium (historical coverage); impact low. Ready for later refinement after the core public journey; no full historical architecture reconstruction is promised.

## Delivery and evidence boundary

Planning baseline: September 23, 2026; Hub `600d9055dacaa242cc188cf5cbca19c04f08f484`, public guide `6f2289cf3ca743abe2f13add88be2d58446953e7`. Reasoning setting: unknown. All implementation, browser, performance, deployment, and installed-client checks described here are planned, not executed.

Follow the current [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/600d9055dacaa242cc188cf5cbca19c04f08f484/docs/sdlc.md), [owning development checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/600d9055dacaa242cc188cf5cbca19c04f08f484/docs/development.md), and [guide/export procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/600d9055dacaa242cc188cf5cbca19c04f08f484/docs/work-guide/README.md). Use one coordinating writer and an isolated delivery worktree, independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed base/head, applicable current-head and merged-main CI, and guarded merge. Atlas/application UI requires current-candidate human approval; guide/viewer-only UI does not. The guide-only CI exception needs its exact path/filter/local-check evidence.

For guide changes, plan `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, and `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`. Atlas changes additionally use `python3 docs/system-design/build.py`, its `--check` mode, `python3 docs/system-design/check.py`, and `node docs/system-design/check.cjs`. Workflow/OpenSpec changes use Node 24, `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow`, and `npm run test:workflow`. Product changes add the issue-appropriate executable validation to development guidance/CI and an issue-linked OpenSpec change as required; documentation presentation records its no-product-contract-change rationale. Run owning hub/dashboard/MCP/shared checks when those packages change.

Public data and command contracts receive independent security/concurrency inspection before dependent work consumes them. Rich motion includes accessibility and actual-phone performance evidence. Refresh the assessment when scope, source inputs, API support, or failure findings change.

This publication authorizes tracker definitions and dependency links only. It does not start implementation, modify repository visibility, install credentials/hooks/services, launch agents, activate schedules, contact devices, or publish a website. Guide-source synchronization, public publication, and real-phone/installed acceptance remain separate future effects. Private task records and conversations never enter the public feed or the existing metadata-only monitoring service.

title: Qualify phone-to-native-app handoff options for Codex and Claude
body:
Owner: Hub development integration research.

Outcome: establish which supported paths can actually reach the user's existing Codex and Claude applications, and what a future connector may claim.

Acceptance and planned evidence:

1. Inventory the actual named app/client versions, phone access method, and Windows/WSL ownership when authorized. Record unknowns rather than assuming that mobile chat, CLI, Desktop, SDK, and app-server sessions are interchangeable.
2. Produce a per-client matrix for opening a project, opening an existing session, preparing/sending a brief, steering a running turn, receiving questions, answering, interruption, and observing delivery. Each cell names official support and separately observed behavior or explicitly says unsupported/unknown.
3. Compare copy/manual routes with documented deep links and supported local interfaces. MCP tool access alone is not evidence of external session wake-up or message delivery. Preserve existing apps and their permissions; do not read or mutate private session databases as an integration shortcut.
4. Identify supported authentication and subscription/API billing paths. Do not assume SDK/custom-client usage shares the current app subscription or reaches current app sessions. Record the documented constraints and remaining account-specific checks.
5. Use fake adapters or isolated tests for development. Any actual session launch, credential setup, app installation, or private-data inspection needs the named owner's separate operational request. Report documentation-only findings separately from installed qualification.
6. Recommend the smallest supported first adapter and copy/manual fallbacks for the other paths, or return a documented no-go. body:

1. Compare a private-network-only route with a small authenticated HTTPS service and outbound PC connector for the actual phone workflow. Do not conflate notice dismissal, message delivery, agent receipt, and successful implementation.
5. Locate responsibilities in existing apps/hub and apps/dashboard where appropriate. If internet reachability requires a separate small relay, name its narrow ownership and justify it. Do not expose the loopback device-control listener or create a second agent-state owner.
6. Record the decision through the repository's ADR/OpenSpec conventions and refine [#204](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/204)/[#205](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/205) into exact contracts and checks. title: Clean up delivered worktrees and scratch after merge
body:
## Outcome

Deliveries clean up after themselves. After a PR merges and main CI passes, the coordinator removes its own worktree and scratch files, so finished work stops piling up on the host.

On 2026-09-23 the WSL host's `/tmp` (a 7.6 GB RAM-backed tmpfs shared by all agent sessions) filled completely. Most of it was finished per-issue checkouts, each with its own `node_modules`, left behind after their PRs merged. There were also 48 stale worktree registrations across four repositories. No repository rule said when a delivery should clean up, and the shared deliver-work skill keeps artifacts when no retention rule exists. Host-level storage guidance (large work goes under `.local/`, not `/tmp`) now lives in the global agent instructions; this issue adds the repository-level retention rule.

## Scope

- `docs/sdlc.md`: add a cleanup step after the main-CI readback. The coordinator removes its own clean worktree with `git worktree remove` (never forced) and deletes its own `.local/scratch/<task>` folder, after confirming that required evidence is in the PR, the issue or the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`. Because this repository squash-merges, delivery is judged by the PR's merged state, not commit ancestry. Failed or abandoned work is kept until the user decides. Other sessions' worktrees, branches and scratch stay untouched.
- `docs/development.md`: when the default `node` is not 24, run commands through `fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --` and reuse one shared Node 24 installation instead of installing Node per task.

Out of scope: host-level storage rules, removing existing worktrees under `.local/worktrees`, and CI changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/sdlc.md` contains the cleanup step with the conditions above.
- `docs/development.md` contains the fnm note.
- `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` exit zero, and every configured Depot job succeeds on the PR head and the merged main revision.

## Dependencies

None. The same retention rule is proposed for codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade in linked issues.

## Verification

Local workflow checks, Depot CI, and independent Standards and Specification reviews.

## Delivery target

Merged to `main`.

title: Make the work guide clipboard-fallback check pass in Depot CI
body:
## Outcome

The work guide's browser check passes in Depot CI again, so main's Work guide job is green and deliveries blocked on merged-main evidence can close.

## Problem

`docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs:214` asserts that a denied clipboard makes the task brief select its prompt for manual copying (`A denied clipboard selects the prompt`). The test gets its "denied" case by calling `clearPermissions()` and relying on headless Chromium to reject `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. Main's Work guide job on `a19a62eb673fd17a5aecdb1db6b5575947e2feb7` failed on this assertion twice: check runs 107425147844 and 107426083706, Depot attempts `4z0gb8j2xf` and `cbcfp3cqdr`. The assertion arrived in #209 (Refs #196). That was a guide-only change, so Depot never ran it before merge.

## Scope

- Reproduce the failure with CI's browser (Playwright 1.63.0 and its headless Chromium shell).
- Make the denied and missing clipboard cases deterministic, so they no longer depend on the browser's default permission. Keep the real granted-clipboard copy check.
- Change the guide's copy behavior only if the reproduction shows a product defect rather than a test-environment assumption.

Out of scope: guide content or snapshot refreshes, and other guide checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Work guide job passes on Depot for the candidate: a `depot ci run` of `.depot/workflows/work-guide.yml` with the change, plus main's Work guide job after merge (the next non-guide merge runs it).
- Locally: `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py` and `check_guide.cjs` pass, and `git diff --exit-code -- docs/work-guide/outputs` shows no drift.

## Dependencies

Regression from #196 (#209). Blocks closure of #207.

## Verification

A red/green reproduction with CI's browser, a Depot run of the Work guide workflow, local guide checks, and independent Standards and Specification reviews.

## Delivery target

Merged to `main`, with main's Work guide job green.

title: Use shared npm and Playwright caches in setup guidance
body:
## Outcome

Setup guidance keeps npm and Playwright caches in their shared default locations instead of a temporary cache.

On 2026-09-23 the WSL host's `/tmp`, a 7.6 GB RAM-backed tmpfs shared by all agent sessions, filled completely. Part of the cause was guidance that sends caches or per-task installs into `/tmp`. The Codex local-development sandbox profile now allows writes to `~/.npm` and `~/.cache/ms-playwright`, so the read-only-cache workaround is no longer needed.

## Scope

Out of scope: examples that write a single small report file under `/tmp`, other documentation, CI and tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` exit zero, and every configured Depot job succeeds on the PR head and the merged main revision.

## Dependencies

After #210 merges, so this PR's Work guide job runs with the fixed browser check. Its merged-main Depot run is also the main evidence #210 and #207 need.

title: Clear Codex Desktop tasks and Line assignments when sessions end
body:
## Outcome

Retire an ended Codex Desktop session and its known descendants from the shared owner in one durable update. Existing consumers remove the task: Nanoleaf releases its Line assignments, Tidbyt and Pixoo update their monitoring displays, and the dashboard removes its row.

The owner retires within seconds of accepting `runtime.ended`. Displays follow their existing polling, write cadence and transport availability; this is not a promise that all physical devices clear simultaneously.

Scope simplified with the user on September 24, 2026. The agreed retirement behavior and safeguards remain.

## Policy

The [Codex hook reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#sessionend) documents `SessionEnd` for archive/delete of an open conversation, normal shutdown, and a conversation idle and unopened in any connected client for 30 minutes. The existing normalizer maps these to the same `runtime.ended` event; its reason is currently `"other"`. No new idle timer or cause detection is needed.

- Apply retirement to `provider: codex`, `client: desktop`. Keep other provider/client policies unchanged in this delivery; [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) extends the same owner rule to Codex CLI and Claude Code afterward.
- Remove the parent and descendants linked by known parent identities together. Do not guess relationships or terminate agents.
- Use [#195's forgetting policy](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195): notices, attention, task labels, task-project overrides, Line placement and animation state may be discarded. This is not acknowledgment, readership, success or cancellation. Preserve unrelated sessions, global projects, colors, reservations, scenes, settings and conversations.
- Ordinary turn completion, waiting for input, read/acknowledgment changes and five-minute freshness uncertainty do not retire sessions. A turn exceeding 30 minutes does not trigger cleanup just because of its duration.
- Keep the 24-hour evidence expiry as the fallback for absent/lost ends, with each record's existing expiry clock.
- Eligible new work after resume or unarchive creates a fresh monitoring record with defaults, without old-effect replay. Retain protection against recognizable delayed events and document unknown-ordering limits.

## Bounded implementation

1. Extend the owner's existing atomic session-removal path from #195 and publish the normal snapshot revision. No new cleanup service or physical writer. The explicitly approved local presentation control below is a separate Nanoleaf operation.
2. Reuse consumer reconciliation. Add focused checks for Nanoleaf, Tidbyt, Pixoo and the dashboard; change a consumer only where a check demonstrates a gap. Retain device queues, native modes, scene restoration, cadence and resynchronization behavior. Report unrelated existing animation limitations separately.
3. Keep archive lookup out of retirement. Cleanup works without Codex-home configuration or a readable archive folder. Retain read-only archive evidence solely as an admission safeguard against archived tasks returning through delayed events, using [#191's configuration](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/191). Missing/unreadable files supply no evidence; never write or move Codex files.
4. Keep retirement/resume handling bounded and durable across restart. Resolve the case where a consumer misses retirement and sees the same conversation identity recreated at its next read. Preserve fresh-record semantics without assuming every intermediate snapshot was observed.
5. Update the issue-linked OpenSpec change, affected lifecycle/state contract and guide, compatibility assessment and required checks. Use the smallest change demonstrated necessary by the focused scenarios below.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] One normalized `runtime.ended` scenario verifies atomic parent/known-descendant retirement, capacity release and one published revision. Retain provider-mapping coverage; do not duplicate identical unit tests for the four documented end causes.
- [x] Unknown/repeated ends create nothing. Unrelated sessions and global settings survive.
- [x] Ordinary completion, waiting, read/acknowledgment changes, freshness uncertainty and a turn lasting over 30 minutes retain the session; fake-clock coverage preserves the separate 24-hour fallback.
- [x] Archive admission tests cover available archive evidence, absent configuration, missing/unreadable folders, delayed events and new work after unarchive.
- [x] Focused tests cover recognizable delayed events, same-identity resume, a recognizable old end after resume, owner restart and a consumer missing the entire retirement between reads. New monitoring records start fresh and old effects do not replay.
- [x] Cover child events after parent retirement and state the admission rule and limits of missing identity/order evidence.
- [x] Existing-consumer checks verify Nanoleaf assignment release, Tidbyt/Pixoo monitoring updates and dashboard removal, including reconnect. If nothing remains to display, preserve each consumer's existing idle behavior. Fix change-caused regressions without redesigning unrelated effects.
- [x] Qualify the separately authorized installed archive-end path with a throwaway conversation. Record accepted owner retirement, dashboard removal and visible Nanoleaf Line release separately from source checks; preserve the timing evidence. Other consumer checks do not repeat complete hardware qualification.

The user approved moving the remaining native non-archive end, reopen-without-prompt and live-resume qualification to [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253). The idle/shutdown trials did not establish reliable end emission. That investigation is not a blocker for this accepted-end retirement delivery; no automatic cleanup on quit or after thirty minutes is claimed. Source-level fresh-resume and read-only admission safeguards remain required and verified above.

## Dependencies and boundaries

[#195](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195) is complete. [#191](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/191) supplies the archive safeguard's Codex-home context, not a prerequisite for receiving ends.

[Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) follows this delivery and generalizes accepted-end retirement across the supported providers. It is not a blocker for #218 and does not expand #218's active PRs or acceptance scope.

[Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) is a downstream consumer of authoritative session presence/removal, with #241 as an additional prerequisite for consistent provider behavior. It owns automatic Work/Free switching and manual override; this issue issues no mode commands. An unavailable feed must not be represented as a healthy empty snapshot.

No archive polling, App Server client, Windows watcher, archive browser, restoration history, new dashboard feature, Claude/CLI policy change or future LIFX/PC-lighting integration. Those future consumers do not block delivery. This issue does not block completed [Tidbyt #21](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/21).

## Installed-trial presentation expansion

The user approved these additions on September 24 after observing the installed wall:

- [x] Shared completed/read tasks retain both their wall row and assigned Line until authoritative removal or explicit eviction. Reading ends the unread pulse; idle is steady blue. Preserve legacy input and orphan-child behavior.
- [x] The selected wall task offers **Evict** for the current Nanoleaf device. Remove its local row, allocation and task effects without changing the conversation, shared owner, other devices, global preferences or mode. Keep it suppressed through polling, read/acknowledgment changes and restart. An identifiable new turn or generation may appear again; reject controls from an older turn/generation/source selection.
- [x] Verify the new UI in isolated browser/Python scenarios and obtain renewed human approval of the concrete candidate before merge. Installation and visible-device checks remain separate.

Device-only eviction is the accepted first version. Eviction across every device is deferred until an explicit shared-owner command is introduced; revisit when another consumer needs the control. Local eviction leaves the owner record present, so it still counts toward Nanoleaf #110's future Work/Free policy. No owner timer, forged SessionEnd, manual database deletion or Codex-state write is added.

This expansion adds a Nanoleaf wall control; the shared-owner API and Hub dashboard controls remain unchanged. Native idle/shutdown emission and subsequent reopen/live-resume qualification now belong to [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253), under the user-approved scope split. The temporary diagnostic hook was restored byte-for-byte. Ends observed during manual task cleanup do not establish normal-shutdown acceptance. The user accepted installed retention and Evict at Nanoleaf `0865a73` and approved the combined UI at `f1fc8e8`. Final head `f4ae77e` changes specifications only; the approval remains applicable. The final integrated source has not been installed.

## Delivered

Delivered through [Hub #238](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/238) and [Nanoleaf #116](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/116). Both repairs are test-only.

Matching PR checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, guarded squash merges and exact resulting-tree readbacks are recorded. Original implementation and consumer validation, specification sync/archive, installed archive/presentation acceptance and explicit UI approval remain complete.

Installed Hub remains 0.3.0 (source `6acc747`), with Nanoleaf `0865a73`; the final integrated source has not been installed. No additional runtime change or database restore occurred. Native idle/shutdown, reopen-without-prompt and live-resume qualification remains open in #253. No automatic cleanup on quit or after thirty minutes is claimed.

title: Refresh work-guide priorities, new issues and defects, and reorganize topic guides
body:
## Outcome

Replace stale milestone-led opening cards with current work, newly added issues, all open defects, useful next steps, blockers and decisions, and later work. ## Accepted design

The owner approved this design in the planning conversation and requested definition and implementation.

- Open defects: every open issue labeled `bug`, including blocked and deferred defects. Show the issue, affected feature/problem, status, owning guide, and a recorded workaround where available. title: Push hub change notifications when state commits
body:
## Outcome

Readers of the hub's change stream learn about a new revision as soon as it commits, instead of up to a second later. The dashboard updates right after a hook event. Nanoleaf can later replace its once-a-second poll with this stream.

## Current behavior

`GET /api/monitor/v1/changes` is a Server-Sent Events stream. Each open stream runs its own 1-second timer. The timer reads the owner snapshot, compares a small fingerprint (revision, collector, loss count, rejected admissions, uncertain count) and writes a `state` event or a heartbeat ([server.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L262-L292)). A commit reaches readers 0 to 1 s later. The first stream whose timer fires also advances the shared feed state (fingerprint, sequence and 32-entry history) for all streams.

The agent-state core already signals every commit with `feeds.publish(revision)`, in `commit` and in `replaceSessions` ([index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L134), [index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L147)), but the hub doesn't listen. `owner.subscribe` doesn't fit: it takes a configured consumer ID and allows one subscription per ID, and the consumer list is part of durable state, so adding a hub consumer would make existing stores fail with `incompatible-state`.

Both call sites run inside `queue`'s try/catch ([index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/d85b8b3381f4e9a7e2e0b410d3f4ab9be74e5793/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L118-L121)). An error thrown there after the write is durable marks the collector `faulted` and stops ingest until restart.

Commits come from more than the events route:

- hook ingest
- the Codex Desktop read-state reader from #219, which calls `owner.ingest` in-process
- label, acknowledge and recovery commands
- maintenance: journal pruning, 24-hour session expiry and approval settlement

## Scope

- [ ] Give the hub a commit notification from the owner that needs no consumer ID. The core raises it at both `feeds.publish` call sites, after the in-memory state update. Hooking the core covers every commit source, including future ones, without wrapping each hub call. A listener on the owner API is one option. Another is an anonymous subscription that reuses the bounded channel in `subscriptions.ts`, which already delivers asynchronously.
- [ ] Keep the commit path isolated. The core catches listener errors. The hub schedules its fan-out outside the commit call, for example with `setImmediate`, instead of reading a snapshot for every stream synchronously inside the commit.
- [ ] Split the per-stream publish step. On each notification or timer tick, advance the shared feed state once, then flush each open stream. Coalesce a burst of commits into at most one write per stream.
- [ ] Keep the 1-second timer for heartbeats, the per-stream auth recheck and changes that don't commit (collector state, quiesce, loss count, rejected admissions, sessions turning uncertain).
- [ ] Add a test-only option for the timer interval, which is hard-coded at 1000 ms. Keep it out of the configuration file that `cli.ts` validates.
- [ ] Keep the wire format and limits as they are: event IDs, the 32-entry replay window, resync on an unknown cursor, the 16-stream cap and disconnecting a reader stalled for more than 5 s. Bursts now produce more events, so the window covers fewer seconds and a reconnecting reader gets `resync` more often. Both current clients refetch the snapshot on `resync`.
- [ ] A slow or paused reader must not delay ingest, commits or other readers.
- [ ] Add the issue-linked OpenSpec change `gh-222-<slug>` that docs/sdlc.md requires for a changed contract with timing and concurrency effects. Update `agent-state-core`, which currently allows subscriptions only for registered consumers, and `standalone-hub-host` for push on commit. The design covers commit-path isolation and the shorter replay horizon.
- [ ] Update the owner API table in the agent-state README and the `/changes` row in the hub README. Publish agent-state 3.1.0.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A hub test shows a committed event reaching an open stream without waiting for the timer, using a long test-only timer interval.
- [ ] Tests cover a burst of commits, a commit from the in-process read-state reader, a maintenance commit and a paused reader that doesn't delay ingest.
- [ ] An agent-state test shows a throwing listener leaves the collector `running` and the commit's outcome successful.
- [ ] The existing feed tests pass unchanged: hub HTTP, dashboard matrix and the performance stalled-reader check.
- [ ] The agent-state, standalone hub and workflow checks listed in AGENTS.md pass. The OpenSpec change is synced and archived on the delivery branch.
- [ ] Live, after the installed monitor is updated separately: watch `/changes` with `curl -N`, submit a Codex prompt and confirm the `state` event arrives within 250 ms of the hook's ingest. One comment records the result and how it was timed.

## Not included

- Nanoleaf reading the stream instead of polling. That is [codex-nanoleaf#90](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/90), which this issue blocks.
- Tidbyt's 30-second poll. Its writes are at least 15 s apart, so earlier notice doesn't help it.
- Session data in the stream, and any message broker.

## Readiness

Complexity low. Uncertainty low. Impact medium: the notification runs on the commit path every consumer depends on, and an unisolated listener error would stop ingest until restart. No blockers. The owner API addition is a minor agent-state version (3.1.0). Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md, including the OpenSpec change above.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment for [agent-device-hub#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252) on 2026-09-25, from this story's text, comments and recorded dependencies. It adds only ratings the story did not already record; readiness, labels and status are unchanged.

- **Complexity: low.** The story calls it small: one listener on the existing feeds.publish signal.
- **Impact: medium.** Runs on the state owner's commit path that every consumer reads; listener errors must stay isolated.

title: Add optional shared playback artwork from the Sony source
body:
## Outcome

Add optional artwork to the shared playback service from [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), beginning with the Sony HT-A9 source. Acquire it once through the owning source/service so the BUNNY UI and display integrations can reuse it. Keep text-only now-playing and controls usable when artwork is missing.

Owner request, September 24, 2026: track artwork as a separate backlog story. This extracts the acquisition work previously described inside [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) and [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38); it is not a new requirement for the initial playback delivery.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] **AC1.** Define an optional source-scoped artwork reference/result in the shared contract. Sony-specific retrieval remains in the Sony module; shared consumers receive no private receiver URL. Keep the interface usable by future adapters and make unsupported/missing artwork explicit.
- [ ] **AC2.** Fetch only from the configured receiver under a documented size/time bound; validate the returned image bytes. The qualification observed JPEG bytes with `text/plain` and transient missing artwork, so do not require a correct MIME header or block metadata on artwork arrival.
- [ ] **AC3.** Keep only the current artwork or a small bounded cache. Do not attach delayed artwork from an earlier observation/source to the current track. Cover missing, delayed, invalid and oversized data and source/track changes with fake responses; no persistent artwork library is needed.
- [ ] **AC4.** Expose artwork through the existing authenticated playback boundary for UI/display consumers. title: Make BUNNY device settings apply in one step and simplify command status
body:
## Problem

During the #154 and #155 hardware checks on September 24, 2026, the owner found the BUNNY device controls awkward to use:

- **Extra click after every setting.** After a brightness or power change is applied successfully, the form stays locked and keeps the old draft. The owner has to press **Discard edit / load current** before changing the setting again, and that label reads as if it undoes the change.
- **Hard-to-read status text.** Messages such as "Previous: queued. Physical result is not confirmed." and the **Load current / unlock** button are hard to read.
- **Frequent `stale-generation` failures.** Pixoo playback advances the controller generation on every item, so Pause or Next often fails with `stale-generation`. It happened three times in one short session. Nothing runs, but the owner has to click again.
- **No same-mode reapply.** BUNNY does not resend the active mode. After a Nanoleaf brightness override, the only way to reapply Work's brightness policy is to switch to another mode and back.

## Outcome

Changing a supported setting takes one deliberate action, and the status text says plainly what happened.

## Scope

- After an apply settles with a non-uncertain outcome, clear the draft and unlock once the refreshed snapshot arrives, as the one-click commands already do. Uncertain results keep the lock.
- Reword the pending, sent, queued, uncertain and failed states and the unlock action. Keep the rule that transport success is not a physical result.
- Reduce `stale-generation` friction, for example by reading fresh guards immediately before submitting, or by offering one click to try again with current values. A `stale-generation` failure has no effects. Never retry automatically.
- Decide whether re-selecting the active mode should send an explicit mode command that reapplies that mode's policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A successful brightness or power change leaves the form ready for the next change without an extra click.
- [ ] Uncertain results still lock and require an explicit reload.
- [ ] The owner reviews the new status and button wording.
- [ ] `stale-generation` handling never resubmits automatically. Browser fixtures cover a generation advance between read and submit.
- [ ] The same-mode reapply decision is recorded, and implemented if accepted.
- [ ] Existing dashboard, browser and accessibility checks pass. The PR records human approval of the UI candidate under the SDLC UI approval scope.

## Context

Found during #154 and #155. The change affects the shared controls from #151 and #153 in `apps/dashboard`. No device or controller change is expected. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. This issue grants no permission for installation or device operations.

## Background

The coordinator worked out the steps from source and the device repositories.

## Scope

Add a "Connect device controllers for BUNNY" section to `apps/hub/SETUP.md` covering:

- **Prerequisites.** The device controller must be running and expose `/controller/v1` on numeric loopback. For Pixoo that means device mode and `PIXOO_CONTROLLER_ENABLED=1`. For Nanoleaf it means the controller service.

- **Back up, then restart the hub service,** and verify: health lists each device, native snapshots validate, and the launcher session shows the controls.
- **Rollback:** restore the config, revoke each principal, restart.
- **Troubleshooting:**
  - A registered device shows `unknown` health until its first request.

  - A controller stopped mid-session reports unavailable until it returns.

body:
## Outcome

When the iPhone plays Apple Music to the Sonos Move over AirPlay, BUNNY shows what is playing and can send pause, next and previous, the same as for the Sony HT-A9 today. Today the hub sees nothing while the Move is playing; the HT-A9 reports AirPlay as `inactive`.

title: Retire ended monitoring sessions consistently across Codex and Claude
body:
## Outcome

Apply one shared-owner retirement rule to every currently supported provider/client: Codex Desktop (`codex`/`desktop`), Codex CLI (`codex`/`cli`) and Claude Code (`claude`/`code`). An accepted `runtime.ended` removes the known session and its known descendants in one durable update. Consumers reconcile the resulting snapshot.

User-approved planning, September 24, 2026. This extends [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218), whose completed delivery covers Codex Desktop. It removes the policy exception that would otherwise let an ended Claude or CLI record hold [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) in Work until expiry.

## Owner policy

- Reuse #218's atomic retirement, bounded delayed-event guards, fresh record generations and known-descendant handling. The shared owner interprets provider lifecycle evidence once; devices do not add their own end filters or timers.
- An accepted end retires monitoring even when notices or attention remain. This may discard task labels, task-project overrides, Line placement and animation state, as already accepted in #218. It does not acknowledge, mark read, report success, cancel work or terminate agents. Preserve unrelated sessions, global settings and device reservations.
- Ordinary `Stop`/`turn.ended`, `SubagentStop`, interruption, waiting, completed/read status and five-minute freshness uncertainty do not become session ends. Completed and waiting records remain until an accepted runtime end or their existing evidence expiry.
- Preserve the 24-hour fallback for absent/lost ends, using each record's evidence clock. Turn duration alone does not imply an end; add no universal 30-minute timer. A real run with no accepted lifecycle evidence for 24 hours can still expire.
- Qualify the end/start mappings for each supported path, including provider-specific exit, clear/switch and resume behavior where applicable. Missing or unqualified end evidence is a coverage gap, not an invented end. Keep hooks bounded, metadata-only and fail-open.
- An eligible new start after retirement creates a fresh record without old-effect replay. Preserve known identity/order protections across restart and missed consumer snapshots, and document their existing limits. Read evidence alone cannot recreate a record. Keep the Codex Desktop archive admission safeguard specific to that client.

## Bounded implementation

Generalize the owner path delivered by #218 and reuse its fixtures and consumer checks. Change a consumer only for a demonstrated gap. No new service, policy registry, provider watcher, historical event replay, cleanup UI or per-device cleanup command. Do not add new provider families or change native modes here.

Assess compatibility and the upgrade behavior of already-retained records using stored evidence; never infer an old end from idle/unknown activity or scan transcripts. Records without sufficient end evidence retain the existing expiry fallback. Document this transition without resetting evidence clocks or live databases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Parameterized owner/provider checks cover Codex Desktop, Codex CLI and Claude Code. An accepted known end atomically removes the record and known descendants, releases capacity and publishes one revision; unknown/repeated ends create nothing.
- [x] Mixed-provider checks preserve unrelated records. Ending one provider's last session cannot remove another provider's session, and no ended record survives merely because it is Claude or CLI.
- [x] Completion, waiting, interruption, read/acknowledgment, child turn completion, freshness uncertainty and turns over 30 minutes retain their existing semantics. Fake-clock checks preserve the separate 24-hour fallback.
- [x] Reuse focused delayed-event, fresh resume, recognizable old-end, restart, child-admission and missed-retirement checks for the newly covered paths; preserve #218's unknown-ordering and bounded-history limits.
- [x] Existing Nanoleaf, Tidbyt, Pixoo and dashboard checks confirm snapshot removal/fresh recreation without provider-specific cleanup. Preserve unavailable-feed handling, queues, native modes and each display's cadence.
- [x] Record provider mapping evidence and remaining installed-path gaps. Update the issue-linked OpenSpec change, lifecycle/state requirements, affected package/provider/setup guidance, compatibility assessment and applicable validation during implementation.
- [x] Document upgrade treatment of previously retained records and verify it with a legacy-state fixture; no fabricated end, acknowledgment, clock reset or old-effect replay.

## Verification and delivery target

Source-only. Extend existing fake-clock, provider, owner, persistence and consumer fixtures; run applicable repository checks. Synthetic events establish source behavior, not delivery from an installed client. Separately authorized installed qualification should observe a normal end and resume for each newly adopted CLI/Claude path, recording emitted events and owner removal/recreation. Named-device permission is required for any visible-light check; repeating every device's full hardware qualification is unnecessary.

#218 completed its accepted-end retirement and approved installed archive/presentation scope. Native Desktop idle/shutdown emission, reopen-without-prompt and live-resume qualification now belong to [Hub #253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253). That investigation does not block this source-level generalization of accepted ends. This issue supplies owner removal to #110; it does not implement Work/Free automation or depend on #110.

## Dependencies and next action

- **Satisfied prerequisite: [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218)**, delivered through Hub #238 and Nanoleaf #116, with follow-up Hub #257 and successful merged-revision checks. Reuse its retirement contract, durable guards and consumer generation handling. The native dependency link remains as provenance; #218 is closed and no longer blocks readiness.
- [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) must validate the consistent owner policy before claiming automatic Work/Free behavior across supported providers.

Ready for source delivery. Prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec change and focused provider mapping/owner tests; no unfinished source prerequisite is recorded. Installed provider qualification still needs its separate authorization and evidence. This planning update authorizes tracker changes only, not implementation, installation, settings changes, agent launches or device operations.

Planned downstream caller: [Hub #262](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/262) reuses the provider-neutral retirement guards for explicit Evict everywhere. That future command is not a prerequisite or scope expansion for this issue.

## Planning assessment and execution recommendation

Refreshed September 25, 2026 after verified #218 completion; current Hub main `d4657fa9f4614e2a933e0afe365ea4ed8e10aded`. Complexity medium: provider mappings, durable owner transitions and consumer checks. Uncertainty medium: accepted-end policy is settled; actual installed emission coverage remains distinct. Impact high: incorrect identity/order handling could remove another live task's monitoring state. Ready for source work, with the existing criteria and protections retained. Reassess if provider qualification requires new collection mechanisms or changes accepted lifecycle meaning.

- **Codex:** Sol (`gpt-6-sol`), high reasoning; direct implementation. Offered by this host's collaboration tools on 2026-09-25; confirm starting-session account availability.
- **Why:** reuse an existing bounded path, with strong review of durable removal, delayed events and provider distinctions. No implementation workers proposed. title: Bound browser-session resources and centralize retirement cleanup
body:
## Outcome and real setup

Repeatedly opening and closing BUNNY on the single-operator Linux/WSL hub releases each retired browser session's resources. Existing launcher, dashboard, HTTP and MCP access continue to work.

Source inspection at main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17` found that monitor reads allocate a principal ledger, while browser expiry, eviction and logout remove credentials without retiring that ledger. The 16-session cap therefore does not bound ledger entries across launches. This is a source finding; retained bytes and real-world memory growth have not been measured. See [ledger creation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L100-L140) and [launch/logout](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L218-L238).

## Smallest useful implementation

Keep the change inside the hub. Give browser-session resources one local lifecycle owner, using the existing maps where practical. Expiry, oldest-session eviction, logout, credential replacement and shutdown use one idempotent retirement path for credentials, streams and replay accounting. Retired sessions cannot admit new work; already admitted work stays tracked until settlement and is then released. Do not create a new service or persistent session store.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. The launcher from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/179 is delivered. Coordinate overlapping stream/server edits with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222; that is shared-file coordination, not a blocker. General memory profiling remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (session, stream and replay lifetimes); uncertainty **low** for the retention path, with exact cleanup scheduling to establish in focused tests; impact **high** because authorization and replay must remain correct. **Ready for a separately requested delivery.** Refresh this assessment if authentication, admission or stream ownership changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep current browser scope/alias limits, configured machine credentials, Host/Origin checks, authentication before replay, request identities, restart epochs, byte/entry limits and the rule that pending work cannot be evicted to admit more work. Retiring a browser session does not undo a submitted command, retry it, quiesce agent state or change a device writer. No credentials or private state enter test receipts.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**.

- [ ] A focused regression covers repeated launch -> monitor read -> logout, expiry and oldest-session eviction. Session/ledger counts and replay accounting return to a documented bound after cleanup; no public diagnostics endpoint is needed. The existing repeat-launch test alone is insufficient because it does not read monitor sessions.
- [ ] Retirement closes that browser principal's streams and rejects its token and cached requests. Another browser session and configured HTTP/MCP principal remain usable. Logging out of a dashboard opened with a manually entered configured credential must not revoke that credential or reset its replay identity: reconnecting with it cannot execute an old request again. Verify both credential kinds with disposable-host authentication, replay and stream tests.
- [ ] A controlled pending command survives retirement without another execution or false cancellation. Its accounting remains charged until settlement and is then released; repeated retirement cannot double-release it. Verify with a deferred fake operation, including rejection and timeout paths.
- [ ] Preserve launcher, replay/revocation and restart tests. On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:hub:mcp` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus the shared suites required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] Prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec lifecycle/concurrency design at pickup. Follow docs/sdlc.md for independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI and merged-revision readback. The PR walkthrough explains resource ownership, duplicate/restart behavior and the pending-retirement test; review explicitly covers authorization and replay.

Process-wide profiling and performance-budget changes stay in #123; this issue proves bounded resource ownership, not an RSS improvement. body:
## Outcome and real setup

BUNNY's existing forms and one-click actions use one command lifecycle, so fixes to receipt handling, uncertainty and refresh ordering apply consistently. Preserve the current single-operator dashboard and its configured Pixoo/Nanoleaf controls, session labels and acknowledgments.

At main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17`, [useCommand and EditForm](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L47-L98) separately maintain submission, receipt tracking, busy/locked state and refresh ordering. Both changed in [PR #239](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/239). This is maintenance work that preserves that delivered behavior.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use one dashboard-local hook or reducer for the shared lifecycle, reusing `resultMessage`, `failureMessage`, `observedResult` and the focus helper. Forms retain draft values and configuration-revision conflicts; action buttons retain command preparation. Keep device-specific request construction and availability rules with their callers. Remove the duplicated orchestration after both callers use the common implementation; moving functions to separate files alone does not satisfy the outcome.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/231 is delivered behavior to preserve. Coordinate `apps/dashboard` edits with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182; skin work is independent and is not a blocker. Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (two interaction models and asynchronous observations); uncertainty **low** (existing implementations and browser scenarios define the behavior); impact **high** because a lifecycle mistake could allow a duplicate or incorrectly guarded device command. **Ready for a separately requested delivery.** Reassess after command-policy or dashboard changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve fresh guards immediately before device submission, configuration-revision draft conflicts, generation-only advances, one explicit submission, no automatic retry, accepted-ticket-only receipt tracking, editable rejected drafts, and locks for uncertain/partial results until explicit reload. Keep mode-specific controls, memory-only credentials, scope checks, focus restoration and no-write inspection. Transport acceptance never establishes physical output. Keep existing wording and layout unless an additional change is explicitly scoped.

body:
## Outcome and real setup

Reduce the places that must change when an existing Pixoo or Nanoleaf integration contract changes, while retaining both native protocols. The affected consumers are the single-operator hub's controller client, MCP tool definitions and dashboard. No new controller or wire version is requested.

At main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17`, protocol facts recur in [MCP schemas](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/mcp.ts#L69-L83), hub validators, and [dashboard types/builders](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L8-L25). [The pinned Nanoleaf contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/vendor/nanoleaf-integration.ts#L1-L13) already exports reusable types. Duplication is established; a current compatibility failure has not been demonstrated.

## Smallest useful implementation

Start with a short contract/caller map in this issue: list duplicated declarations, their authoritative owner, intentional transport projections and actual imports. Identify the declarations that can be removed and the checks that show callers still accept/reject the same inputs. Use that map to settle the smallest browser-safe local module arrangement before implementation.

Then reuse owner-supplied types and consolidate shared facts per extension for the hub validators, MCP schema projections and dashboard request builders. Keep protocol-specific projections explicit and preserve validation at each trust boundary. Use existing packaging and build facilities; do not add a plugin system, schema framework, new distributable package or cross-repository migration merely for this refactor. Preserve the reviewed vendor bytes and provenance rather than editing an upstream-owned copy in place.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. Coordinate overlapping dashboard command work and any owner-contract revision at pickup. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/25 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/26 own deferred source migrations and do not block local reuse. Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (three consumers and two protocols); uncertainty **medium** (the reusable declarations and browser/package boundary need the map above); impact **high** because validation or guard drift can change admitted device commands. **Backlog.** Next action: complete the bounded map and update this assessment to ready when it shows a concrete reduction without changing accepted contracts. If a candidate declaration must differ by boundary, retain it and explain why. Reassess on upstream pin, wire or packaging changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Retain native API versions, different string/object request tickets, revision/generation meanings, configured target binding, strict unknown-field rejection, limits, mode semantics and configuration-versus-physical outcomes. Preserve HTTP/MCP authorization and ambiguous-write handling. Browser imports must not pull in Node transport, credential access or private configuration. Pixoo and Nanoleaf keep source and device-writer ownership.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**; readiness mapping comes before implementation. If the map finds no worthwhile consolidation that preserves the native boundaries, record the evidence and recommend closing without implementation. Do not force an abstraction to satisfy this issue. The implementation criteria below apply only when the map establishes a useful change.

- [ ] The map names each shared declaration's owner, callers, removed duplicate and any intentional projection. Review shows fewer independently maintained protocol facts, with no new wire acceptance or capability claim.
- [ ] The selected local definitions serve the current hub, MCP and dashboard callers. Type/build checks cover browser compatibility and installed hub packaging; source inspection confirms no dependency on device-application internals or Node-only code in the browser.
- [ ] Preserve vendor checksums and native fixture coverage. Feed relevant valid and invalid native requests through the MCP projection and owning validator, accounting for documented projections. Cover tickets, bounds, unknown/private fields, target binding and differing native receipt semantics; keep semantic validation that a schema cannot express.
- [ ] Preserve dashboard request guards and HTTP/MCP outcomes. On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:mcp`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:dashboard` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus shared contract/MCP/workflow checks required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. Use the documented pinned owning-service checks for affected native boundaries. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] At pickup, record the issue-linked OpenSpec treatment for this intended behavior-preserving refactor. Any necessary wire or capability change requires reassessment before implementation. Follow docs/sdlc.md for independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI, conditional UI approval and merged-revision readback; review explicitly covers protocol compatibility and package contents.

## Meaningful deferrals

title: Prevent dashboard component aliases from colliding with built-in navigation
body:
## Outcome

Give built-in dashboard pages and registered components distinct navigation identities. A component alias of `activity` or `connections` must open only that component while the Activity and Connections pages remain independently accessible.

## Problem and source evidence

[Dashboard PR #127](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/127) deferred **P3 F-STD-2** to hub frontend maintenance. The current [dashboard source at `28f7599`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L228-L258) still stores a built-in page name or component ID in the same `view` string. The navigation buttons, `aria-current` checks and visible sections compare against that shared string. An alias matching a built-in key selects both targets. Ordinary aliases are unaffected. The original review classified this as a nonblocking navigation defect, with no permission bypass or automatic device writes.

Reproduce with synthetic components whose IDs are `activity` and `connections`, alongside an ordinary component. Select each component and its similarly named built-in page. The selected navigation item and visible view must identify only the chosen target.

## Scope

Own this in `apps/dashboard`. Use a discriminated navigation value, or an equivalently unambiguous representation, that separates built-in page identity from component identity. Preserve registered aliases, display labels, API paths, credentials, capability gates, drafts and the existing component view. Coordinate with any active dashboard owner, including the separate styling work in [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Model navigation so every supported component alias remains distinct from built-in pages, including exactly `activity` and `connections`. Do not fix the collision by banning or renaming otherwise valid aliases.
- [ ] Each click or keyboard activation selects one navigation item with the correct `aria-current` and displays only its intended page or component. Both built-in pages remain reachable when both conflicting aliases exist together.
- [ ] Retain ordinary component navigation, read-only/unknown component views, drafts, focus and selection across normal snapshot refresh/reconnect. Component IDs sent to the owning APIs remain unchanged.
- [ ] Add a failing regression case before the fix, then cover both conflicting aliases, an ordinary alias and transitions to/from the built-in pages with synthetic browser fixtures. Assert selected navigation, visible sections and inspection without command requests.
- [ ] Run the dashboard and shared checks required by the current [development guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/development.md#dashboard-checks). Deliver through the [repository SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), including independent reviews, applicable current-head CI, required approval of the actual UI candidate and merged-main readback. Record the OpenSpec disposition for this bounded repair.

## Readiness and delivery boundary

This tracker publication does not implement the fix. Use fake components and isolated test state; installation, live device operations, new controls, source migration and public guide publication are outside this issue.
