title: Show starting model and thinking-level recommendations for each story in the work guide
body:
Owner: Hub guide source and story metadata. Policy: [agent-skills#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/56), merged in [PR #57](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/pull/57) as [`3e009e6`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/blob/3e009e6f71451bb8f6577d2250e6a0697d38528a/skills/plan-work/references/execution-recommendations.md).

## Outcome and real setup

A reader opens a story in the [work guide](https://jimmie-potts.github.io/agent-device-guide/) and sees, next to its complexity, uncertainty and impact, which model and thinking level to start with in Claude Code and in Codex, and whether that session implements bounded work, investigates, or orchestrates workers. The reader picks the model and effort in their host. The guide shows the saved recommendation; it never claims to launch or switch a model.

Each recommendation lives in its GitHub story as one `## Execution recommendation` section written under the policy above, together with the Implement prompts that carry it: one per host, plus a cheaper start when one exists. The saved backlog reproduces the section; the guide renders it and copies its prompts verbatim. Where the evidence is insufficient, the story and the guide say what is missing.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories (agent-device-hub, codex-nanoleaf, divoom-app-upgrade), the existing generator, checks and brief dialog. Stories stay authoritative in GitHub.

Excluded: implementing any assessed story; changing its scope, readiness, labels or status; installing skills; changing runtime model settings; operating devices; public publication, which #87 owns.

## Smallest useful implementation

Three internal tasks, one coordinator, one issue.

**A. Section convention and guide rendering**, all under `docs/work-guide/`.

- Document the section in `docs/work-guide/README.md` as the shape the installed plan-work policy defines once [agent-skills#58](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/58) lands; until then this issue's own section is the interim reference. The README documents the parser's strictness, the guide-specific fingerprint and the rendering; it does not restate the policy. The interim shape: heading `## Execution recommendation`, then a `**Start with:**` line giving the one answer: which session type to open, on which model and thinking level in each host, and which prompt to paste. Then a two-host table with the rows `Model`, `Thinking level`, `Session type`, `Subagents` and `Availability` (evidence source and date per host, verified or provisional), plus an optional `Checkpoints` row naming decisions where a one-shot session stops to ask. Session type comes from a fixed vocabulary that maps one-to-one onto the policy's session roles: `One-shot` (one session implements directly, no subagents), `Pair` (one session delegates implementation to a single worker and advises it at approach, blockers and final review), `Orchestrate` (a stronger session breaks the story down, delegates bounded pieces to subagents and owns every write and review) and `Investigate first` (no implementation yet; a read-only session answers the named question, then the story is reassessed). Then `**Why:**`, `**Reassess when:**` and `**Assessed:**` (date, policy revision, evidence links, fingerprint) lines. After the table come the prompt blocks: `**Prompt (Claude Code):**` and `**Prompt (Codex):**`, each followed by one fenced `text` block, and optionally `**Cheaper start:**` (one line naming what it covers, its session type and each host's model and thinking level) followed by `**Cheaper prompt (Claude Code):**` and `**Cheaper prompt (Codex):**` blocks. Every prompt names the live issue URL, states the model and thinking level the reader selected, asks the agent to confirm the model and stop if it differs, tells it to take the thinking level as stated rather than guess it (Claude Code does not expose the effort level to the agent reliably: on 2026-09-24 an Opus session set to high reported low), states the session type and any subagent settings, points at the story's Execution recommendation with its assessment date, asks the agent to say so before changing strategy, and keeps the existing "if deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop" ending. `Investigate first` replaces the Implement prompts with read-only prompts that name the question. An insufficient story replaces the answer, table and prompts with `**Status:** insufficient` and `**Missing:**` (the exact input and the next question or evidence). One section per story. The parser is strict and never guesses. The vocabulary is a presentation label, not a second copy of the selection table.
- Add a parser and renderer module, for example `work/recommendations.py`, that `build_guide.py` feeds from the story bodies already saved in `work/backlogs/*-issues.json`. No new backlog file, tracker field, model registry or background assessor.
- Freshness. `Assessed` records a short SHA-256 fingerprint of the normalized story body with this section removed. The build recomputes it from the saved body; a mismatch renders "needs reassessment (story text changed after <date>)". Labels, state and dependencies never enter the fingerprint, so a status refresh can neither confirm nor stale a recommendation. Live GitHub reads in `guide_overview.js` keep each story's snapshot recommendation state and date. They may downgrade (a story absent from the snapshot shows "not yet assessed") and never upgrade. If the live path also checks the fingerprint, it shares fixtures with the Python check.
- Display. A compact text label per story in topic rows and opening cards, session type first, for example "Orchestrate · Opus high / Sol high", "One-shot · Sonnet medium / Luna medium" or "Investigate first · Sonnet medium / Luna medium", in both the snapshot renderer and the live renderer. In the brief dialog, a "Start with" block above the prompt actions shows the answer line, the two-host table with explicit model, thinking-level, session-type and subagent labels, the state, the assessment date and policy revision, and a `<details>` with why, availability and the reassessment trigger. One sentence tells the reader to choose the model and effort in their host before pasting, because the agent can confirm the model but not the thinking level. The Implement action gains two text toggles: host (Claude Code or Codex, remembered per viewer in browser storage with a safe fallback) and start (Recommended or Cheaper; Cheaper is disabled with a note when none is recorded). While the recommendation is current, Implement copies the story's saved prompt for that host and start. A stale, insufficient, unassessed or unreadable story gets the generic Implement prompt with its state notice, never a custom prompt. Explain, Plan and Review keep their current text. Every prompt names the live issue URL.
- States, in text rather than color: recommended, with date and provenance and a verified or provisional availability label per host; needs reassessment; insufficient information, with the missing input; not yet assessed; assessment unavailable, when a section is present but unreadable. Never a guessed default.
- An idempotent upsert helper, for example `work/recommendations.py upsert --dry-run`. It re-reads the live body, replaces only this section, writes nothing when the normalized section is unchanged, keeps the assessment date when the fingerprint and ratings are unchanged, and reads the result back. It renders the prompt blocks from the section's fields with one template per session type and host, so every story's prompts read the same way; a hand edit to a prompt in the issue wins on the next refresh, because the guide copies the saved text. The assessor's input stays outside Git in `.local/evidence/`. The helper writes what it is given; it does not assess.

**B. Initial assessment pass** over every open story in the three repositories. On 2026-09-24 that is 116 stories: Hub 66, Nanoleaf 30, Pixoo 20. The saved snapshot still lists 118; Nanoleaf #131, #132 and #135 have closed, and Pixoo #83 needs a primary guide.

- For each story, read the body, relevant comments, linked specification and dependencies.
- Reuse an existing `Work assessment` rating when its evidence is current. Derive a missing rating only when the sources support it, and record the rationale in that story's assessment section. Unknown stays unknown.
- Write both host recommendations for a sufficiently defined story, or `insufficient` with the exact missing input. Keep any blocker, deferral, readiness and status as they are.
- Assess children separately from parents. A high-impact story keeps the stronger capability floor even for a tiny diff.
- Re-read each body before writing. Coordinate with the owners of stories in progress or in review. Report permission failures and conflicting existing assessments as pending.

**C. Snapshot and guide revision.** After the tracker writes, run `refresh_backlogs.py`, reconcile primary coverage for new stories, rebuild, run the checks and deliver a Hub PR. Account for every inventoried story as recommended (new, updated or unchanged), insufficient, or pending, with links and reasons.

Dependencies: [agent-skills#58](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/issues/58) is a required input for the assessment pass (part B), so the 116 sections are written once in the canonical shape. Part A may proceed now against this issue's interim shape and adopts the merged revision. Shared-file coordination with [PR #251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251) for #85, which changes `build_guide.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `test_maintenance.py`, `guide_brief.css` and the README: rebase onto main after it merges, or coordinate with its coordinator if it stalls on the atlas approval. [#240](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/240) may change guide-only CI handling; confirm the policy at merge time. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the resulting guide revision later.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Stories remain authoritative; the guide is a dated projection. The three ratings stay model-neutral and are never averaged or derived from a title, label, file count or model choice. A recommendation grants no permission or readiness to start.
- Tracker writes touch only the `Execution recommendation` section and, where a rating is newly derived, the story's assessment section. Acceptance criteria, labels, status, assignees, priority, dependencies and other owners' text are preserved. No closing, reopening, native dependency edits or custom fields. Re-running the pass on unchanged evidence changes nothing.
- The existing brief actions (Explain, Plan, Implement, Review), their live issue URLs, focus handling, clipboard fallback, no-script GitHub link, keyboard access, phone-width fit, print and the anonymous GitHub read limits. This issue amends one rule from #196, "prompts embed no snapshot context": a custom Implement prompt embeds the model and strategy from a current recommendation, and only then. Every prompt still names the live URL and tells the agent to re-read the story. The prompt blocks sit inside the section and stay out of the freshness fingerprint.
- Generated HTML is never hand-edited. Architecture receipts and diagrams stay untouched. No credentials, private paths or transcripts enter the tracker or the guide.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, meaning the Hub PR plus the authorized story metadata edits. No installation, device or publication step.

1. `test_maintenance.py` covers the parser and renderer with fixtures: both hosts extracted and rendered; a missing host, duplicate section or unknown key rendering "assessment unavailable"; provisional availability rendered as unverified; a high-impact story whose ratings render unchanged beside its recommendation; a parent story typed Orchestrate and a child typed One-shot rendered independently; an unknown session type rendering "assessment unavailable"; a fingerprint mismatch rendering "needs reassessment"; a story without a section rendering "not yet assessed"; hostile text in every field and inside a prompt block rendered literally; prompts extracted per host and per start, with a missing cheaper start reported as absent rather than invented; two consecutive builds producing identical HTML.
2. The upsert helper is tested offline: unchanged content writes nothing and keeps the date; changed content replaces only the section; a body without a section gains exactly one; generated prompts follow one template per session type and host and survive a round trip through the parser.
3. `check_guide.cjs` shows the brief block with the answer line, both hosts and the session-type label as text at 390 px and 1440 px; a live status refresh that leaves the recommendation state and date unchanged; a live-only issue showing "not yet assessed"; one insufficient story showing its missing input; Implement copying the saved Claude Code and Codex prompts and the cheaper variant, the host choice persisting where storage allows, Cheaper disabled with a note where none is recorded, and a story mocked stale falling back to the generic prompt with its notice; print with the details expanded; the details control reachable by keyboard; no overflow.
4. The PR's assessment report lists every open story with its state and link, counts per state, the policy revision used, the stories left insufficient with their missing input, and any pending writes. The saved backlog reproduces every written section, and each story's readback matches.
5. The guide procedure's commands pass at the candidate with Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`): `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, then a rebuild with no drift in `docs/work-guide/outputs`. Screenshots (both hosts, a missing-information case, phone width and print), the HTML hash and the check receipt go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/gh-<this issue>-<slug>/`.
6. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same fixed comparison, then a guarded squash merge under [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). If every changed path stays under `docs/work-guide/`, record the guide-only CI exception evidence; otherwise normal CI applies. Guide UI needs no human approval. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling and story metadata with no product behavior delta.

Limitations: recommendations are planning heuristics under the linked policy, not benchmarks. Codex availability cannot be inspected from a Claude Code session, nor the reverse, so the other host's choices carry a provisional label until a session on that host records evidence.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Live recomputation of the fingerprint in the browser: optional. Without it, a story edited after the snapshot keeps its snapshot state and date until the next guide refresh, and the dated label makes that visible. Revisit if a reader acts on a stale recommendation.
- Closed stories and other repositories: not assessed. No history backfill.
- Public publication: pending under #87 after this guide revision merges. A Hub merge alone does not update the website.
- Custom Explain, Plan and Review prompts: not done; they stay generic. Revisit if a story's planning session needs the recommendation in its prompt.
- A CI or scheduled reassessment: never. Reassessment happens at planning or delivery pickup under the existing policy.
- Policy enforcement in the helper, such as refusing Sonnet on a high-impact story: not built, to avoid a second maintained copy of the policy. The assessor applies it and the review checks it.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24, against Hub `main` [`73166b2`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/commit/73166b2c6bc9b69a43650798684d73228483474d) and the policy revision above.

- **Uncertainty: medium.** The section syntax and the freshness mechanism are proposed here and settled in delivery. How many stories have enough evidence is unknown until the pass runs. Codex availability is not inspectable from this host.

title: Add a trading-card skin to the guide and atlas, with art shared by issue label
body:
Owner: Hub guide and atlas source.

## Outcome and real setup

Add a second, just-for-fun skin to the cross-project work guide and the B.U.N.N.Y. atlas. It draws on trading card games like Magic: The Gathering. Each issue appears as a card, and each card's art comes from its issue's type label, so every `bug` shares one piece of art, every `enhancement` another, and so on, the way basic lands share art. Atlas component pages get the same card treatment, with art chosen by component category. Readers pick Neon or Cards with a skin picker, and the page remembers the choice.

This is the alternate skin and skin picker that [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) postponed "to a separate issue". Neon Geometry Wars stays the default.

Real setup: the generated guide (`docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html`) and atlas (`docs/system-design/`), read on a phone and a desktop. The guide covers Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo issues. No other hosts or services.

## Smallest useful implementation

**Required input: [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85)** (PR [#251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251), in review). The card skin uses its role tokens, skin template, pause control and "how to add a skin" section. If that PR changes before merge, re-plan from the version that actually merges.

- **Art mapping.** One small data file maps art keys to images and gives the precedence order. Issues are keyed by type label. The starting set covers every type label in the three repos' current snapshots, and the owner can rename or reassign any of it:

  | Label | Card "land" | Color |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `enhancement` | Forest | green |
  | `bug` | Mountain | red |
  | `documentation` | Island | blue |
  | `maintenance` | Swamp | black |
  | `accessibility` | Plains | white |
  | `hardware` | Artifact | colorless |

  Workflow labels (`status:*`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `priority:*`) never pick art. An issue with several type labels uses the first in precedence order. An issue with no mapped label gets a default card art. Atlas components are keyed by their category prefix (`API`, `CORE`, `DB`, `DEV`, `DEP`, `CH`, `ADR`, ...), and an unmapped prefix also gets the default.
- **One markup, two skins.** The generators (`docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py`) write the art key into each issue link, brief and component panel, for example as a `data-art` attribute. The skins differ only in CSS, tokens and assets. Neon ignores the art key. Live GitHub status updates (#197) also update the art key when an issue's labels change.
- **Card anatomy.** In the Cards skin, the task brief dialog (#196) becomes a full card:
  - **Name line:** the issue title.
  - **Art box:** the label art.
  - **Type line:** type label and repository, for example "Enhancement - Hub".
  - **Set symbol:** a repository glyph. `priority:high` gets a "rare" treatment.
  - **Text box:** the existing brief content and copy buttons.

  Issue links in the guide tables become small mini-cards, using a type-colored frame and an art thumbnail or glyph. Atlas component panels use the card frame and category art. The table and page structure stays the same.
- **Art.** Original art made for this project and bundled in the repository, one piece per art key plus the default. Agent-drawn SVG is the default, and the owner can swap in raster images through the mapping later. Use no Wizards of the Coast art, card frames, mana symbols or logos, and do not use the Magic: The Gathering name in the UI. Record where each piece came from, and its license, in a short credits file beside the art. Keep all art to about 1 MB or less and make no remote requests.
- **Skin picker.** A small control in the guide and atlas headers switches between Neon and Cards. It stores the choice in `localStorage` (wrapped in try/catch) and applies it in the head script before first paint. If storage is unavailable, the page falls back to Neon.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Status stays readable as text in both skins. Art and frame color never replace the status label, the blocked qualifier or the issue number. Text always sits on a solid panel, never directly on art.
- Fixed-meaning colors (the Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo repository colors and the status colors) come from #85's non-overridable token set. The card "land" colors are skin decoration only.
- Pause and `prefers-reduced-motion` stop all decorative motion in the Cards skin too. Decoration stays out of the tab order and never covers controls. Print shows no decoration.
- The guide's issue totals, links, brief prompts, live GitHub status and existing checks behave as they do now. Change the generators and assets, not the generated output.
- The public guide carries only public issue data. Art and credits contain nothing private.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

1. **Cards render.** In the Cards skin at 390 and 1440 px, in dark and light, the guide's issue mini-cards, the brief card and the atlas component cards show the mapped art, type line, repository symbol and readable status text. Evidence: screenshots in the PR. The owner approves the atlas candidate, as [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md#ui-approval-scope) requires. The guide needs no approval.
2. **Art is shared by label.** Two issues with the same type label use the same art. An issue with several type labels follows the precedence order. An unmapped label or category falls back to the default art. When a live status update changes an issue's labels, the art changes with them. Evidence: a guide check that every type label in the current snapshots, and every atlas category prefix, maps to art or explicitly to the default. The check must also cover a fixture issue with several labels and one with an unknown label.
3. **Picker works.** Switching skins changes the whole page without a reload and saves the choice. A seeded preference applies before first paint, and when storage is unavailable the page renders Neon. Evidence: browser check assertions. Seed the stored choice with `addInitScript`; do not assert storage across `page.reload()` (see the #85 CI lesson).
4. **Protections hold.** Status stays identifiable without color or art. With pause and reduced motion on, nothing moves. Text contrast is checked on the card text panels. Nothing in the Cards skin adds a remote request. The color-literal check from #85 covers the new skin's files. Evidence: extended `check_guide.cjs` and `docs/system-design/check.cjs` assertions.
5. **Docs and credits.** The guide README's skin section lists the Cards skin, the mapping file and how to add or reassign art. The credits file lists each art piece's source and license.
6. **Existing checks pass:** `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`, `python3 docs/system-design/build.py` and its `--check` mode, `python3 docs/system-design/check.py`, `node docs/system-design/check.cjs`.

Delivery: follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The atlas is outside `docs/work-guide/`, so normal CI applies. There are no product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change is needed. Public publication follows the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md) and is separate from source delivery.

## Meaningful deferrals

- **B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard, Nanoleaf and Pixoo apps.** They keep Neon only. Revisit after [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182) lands the dashboard token layer.
- **Markdown documents rendered by GitHub** (READMEs, docs/*.md) and the nine Archify architecture viewers. These can't be skinned from our generators and stay as they are.
- **Deck view** (a card grid in place of each guide table), a rotated "tapped" look for blocked issues, gold frames for issues with several type labels, and flavor text. Revisit if the owner wants them after seeing the first candidate.
- **Per-issue custom art** (art keyed by issue rather than label). Revisit if the owner asks for it; the mapping file can grow an issue-key column.

## Assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24. Hub `main` is at `73166b2c6bc9b69a43650798684d73228483474d`, and #85's PR #251 head is at `92423ae4970d4fc3c94bd9c288bea939abc9907b` (open, in review).

- **Operating assumptions:** a personal project with one owner, the public guide and atlas as the only consumers, and reversible styling. The owner chose guide plus atlas and original bundled art on 2026-09-24.
- **Complexity: medium.** Two generators, one mapping, a picker with pre-paint application, live-status art updates and the art itself.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** #85's final token names and skin template haven't merged yet. Whether mini-cards read well at 390 px, and whether the art looks good, are for the owner to judge on the candidate. The label set and generator paths are known.
- **Impact: low.** Reversible, per-viewer styling on documentation pages. Neon stays the default. No device, state or credential effects.
- **Readiness: blocked** on #85 merging. The requirements are otherwise settled. At pickup, refresh the token and template names from the merged #85, and refresh the label set from the current snapshots.
- **Reviews:** independent Standards and Specification reviews and applicable CI, per sdlc. The owner approves the atlas candidate. No specialist review is needed beyond the accessibility checks in AC4.
- **Reassess if** #85 merges with a different skin mechanism, if the owner wants the dashboard included, or if the art source changes to supplied or licensed images.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Opus (`opus`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `high` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below. Refresh the token and template names from the merged #85 at pickup, as the story asks.

| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

State the model you are running and stop if it is not Opus; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. title: Report documentation drift against pinned sources in CI
body:
Owner: Hub documentation tooling and CI.

## Outcome and real setup

Every non-guide PR and main push reports where documentation has fallen behind the code it describes, so staleness is visible instead of unknown. Three checks:

1. **Pinned sources.** For each diagram, atlas document and API or database reference, list the pinned source files that changed between the recorded pin and the current head. Hub files come from the checkout; Nanoleaf and Pixoo files come from the public GitHub compare API.
2. **Documented commands.** Every `npm run <script>`, `python3 <path>` and `node <path>` named in AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/development.md, docs/sdlc.md and docs/work-guide/README.md exists in `package.json` scripts or on disk.
3. **Atlas reference.** `python3 docs/system-design/build.py --check` and `python3 docs/system-design/reference/check_reference.py` run in CI, so the generated API and database reference cannot drift silently.
4. **Documented paths.** Every repository path cited in code spans in AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/development.md, docs/sdlc.md, docs/work-guide/README.md and docs/application-ui-style-guide.md exists on disk. ## Smallest useful implementation

- `docs/check_docs_drift.py`, standard library only. It reads the diagram receipts under `docs/work-guide/work/architecture/` (`sourceRevisions`, `viewRevisions`, each diagram's `sources` and `revisions`), `docs/system-design/design.json` source baselines and `docs/system-design/reference/sources.json`, then prints one Markdown report: per diagram or document, the pin revision, the count of pinned files changed since, and the file list. - Job identities, timeouts, matrices and the guide-only path filters stay as they are; `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` still pass.
- Reads are GET only. A failed compare read reports "not checked" for that repository instead of failing the job.

Delivery target: source-only.

1. Unit tests for the script with fixtures: a pin with changed files reports them; an unchanged pin reports none; a documented command missing from `package.json` fails with the file and line; a missing path fails; a failed compare read reports not checked; the report is deterministic.

The workflow and docs paths sit outside the guide folder, so normal CI applies. No OpenSpec change: tooling with no product behavior delta.

- Failing CI on drift: not done. Lag is intentional and documented. Revisit if reviewers keep missing drift shown in the summary.
- Checking prose claims beyond commands and pins, such as statements in docs/architecture.md: not done; there is no reliable mechanical check. Revisit when one claim goes stale twice.
- A PR comment: not done, because it needs `pull-requests: write`. The job summary and annotations are enough. Revisit if they prove too hidden.

title: Move guide topic assignments and notes into the stories and read them live
body:
Owner: Hub guide source and story metadata. Blocked by [#252](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/252), which supplies the section parser and the upsert helper this issue reuses.

## Outcome and real setup

A story carries its own guide placement: the topic guide that owns it, a one-line reading note, an optional workaround, and whether the owner highlights it as a next step, a decision or later work. The guide reads those from the story instead of from `guide-coverage.json`, `guide_details.py` and the curated lists in `guide_paths.py`. When the page opens, the browser reads current story bodies, so a story created or edited after the snapshot appears in its topic with its current note, and a story without a placement shows "topic assignment pending". Refreshing the guide then needs no manual coverage reconciliation.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories, the existing generator, live-read script and checks. The eleven topic names, their outcomes, aliases and track groupings stay in the repository; they are the guide's structure, not story facts.

Excluded: history, roadmap and diagram inputs, which stay dated ([#258](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258) reports their drift); automatic refresh PRs; publication; changing any story's scope or status.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **One `## Guide` section per story**, in the #252 style: `- **Topic:** <topic id>` (required, one of the eleven), `- **Note:** ...` (optional, replaces the per-issue reading note), `- **Workaround:** ...` (optional, defects only) and `- **Highlight:** next step | decision | later, with the reason` (optional, replaces the curated next-step, decision and owner-later lists). Reuse #252's parser and upsert helper by adding keys; do not write a second parser.
- **Generator.** `build_guide.py` derives coverage, notes, workarounds and highlights from the saved bodies. Retire `guide-coverage.json`, the `DETAILS` table and the `NEXT_STEPS`, `DECISIONS`, `OWNER_LATER` and `WORKAROUNDS` tables. The snapshot build still fails, naming the story, when an open story lacks a valid topic.
- **Live path.** `guide_overview.js` and the topic sections read the `Guide` section from live bodies with the shared parser. A story unknown to the snapshot but carrying a topic is placed in that topic with its note and gate; one without a topic stays under "Issues awaiting topic assignment". A note edited after the snapshot shows live. The freshness line names which parts are live and which stay dated.
- **Migration.** One idempotent pass writes the `Guide` section into every open story from the current files (116 stories on 2026-09-24): dry run first, read back each story, and a rerun on unchanged input writes nothing.
- **Templates.** Add the `Guide` block with the topic list to the feature and bug templates in all three repositories, so a new story carries its topic from creation. One small PR in each device repository.
- **Docs.** The guide README and the "dated publication" sentence in docs/sdlc.md say which parts are live and which stay dated.

Dependencies: required input #252 (parser, upsert helper, live-path conventions). Shared-file coordination with [#251](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/251) on the generator and checks. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result later.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Every open story has exactly one topic in the snapshot build. Counts, reference links and the archive rules are unchanged. Live placement never counts a story twice or moves a closed one.
- Tracker writes touch only the `Guide` section. Everything else in a story is preserved: no label, status, assignee or closure changes. Reruns on unchanged input write nothing.
- The live read keeps its anonymous GET requests to the existing endpoint within the 60-per-hour limit; no new endpoints. A failed read keeps the snapshot, as today.
- Diagram, history and roadmap inputs and their receipts are untouched.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, meaning the hub PR, the migration edits and two template PRs.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: the `Guide` section parses from fixtures with each key; a missing or unknown topic fails the snapshot build naming the story; each highlight renders in its opening list; a story without a section is excluded from topic tables and listed as pending; hostile text renders literally; repeated builds produce identical HTML; the retired inputs are gone.
2. `check_guide.cjs`: with a mocked live body, a snapshot-unknown story appears in its topic with its note and the topic count updates; one without a section stays pending; a mocked note edit shows live; a failed read keeps the snapshot; the freshness line names the live parts; no page overflow at 390 px and 1440 px.
3. The migration report in the PR lists every open story with its topic and link, confirms each readback, and shows a second dry run writing nothing.
4. The guide procedure's commands pass with Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`), then a rebuild with no drift in `docs/work-guide/outputs`. Screenshots and the HTML hash go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`.
5. Independent Standards and Specification reviews and a guarded squash merge under [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The hub PR touches `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and docs/sdlc.md, so normal CI applies. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling and story metadata with no product behavior delta.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Topic labels (`guide:<topic>`) instead of a body section: not chosen, to avoid 33 new labels and a second mechanism. Revisit if filtering stories by topic inside GitHub becomes a need.
- A generator for `github-history.json`, which is still refreshed by hand: separate small task when the manual refresh next hurts.
- Automatic refresh PRs and publication on merge: separate decisions after #240.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24, against Hub `main` [`73166b2`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/commit/73166b2c6bc9b69a43650798684d73228483474d).

- **Complexity: medium.** A section parser shared by Python and JavaScript, a generator that drops four hand-maintained inputs, live placement of new stories, templates in three repositories and a 116-story migration.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** Whether live placement changes topic counts or only lists the story is settled at the first checkpoint; the rest is observed in the current generator.
- **Impact: medium.** 116 body edits, reversible through GitHub edit history. A parser fault fails the build loudly through the exact-cover assertion rather than dropping stories silently.

title: Evict a task across devices through the shared owner
body:
## Outcome and real setup

For one operator and the selected shared Hub owner, provide an explicit **Evict everywhere** action that removes a selected task's shared monitoring record and its known descendants. Every connected consumer reconciles the resulting owner snapshot, removing its row, status and task effects through its existing queue and cadence. Codex/Claude conversations and agent execution are untouched. Offline consumers reconcile on recovery; this is not a promise of simultaneous physical output.

The user requested eventual eviction across devices during [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218), accepted device-only eviction as the first version, and on September 25 explicitly chose shared-record removal rather than presentation-only hiding. This is distinct from [Hub #138](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/138), which resets an activity indicator while preserving the session.

## Smallest useful implementation

Build on #218's durable atomic retirement and fresh-generation behavior after [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) provides the same retirement/late-event rules for all supported provider/client paths. Add a deliberate guarded owner command through the existing monitor command boundary. Record manual eviction as a user command, never as a fabricated provider `SessionEnd`.

The existing Nanoleaf wall task control is the first caller. Add an explicitly named Evict everywhere action alongside the current device-only eviction, using a protected server-side call to the selected Hub. The local action retains its existing meaning. Do not silently broaden a saved device-only request or fall back to local-only removal after a failed global command. Reuse the existing private provisioning path for an appropriately authorized Hub credential; a read-only feed credential gains no control rights automatically and no credential reaches the browser.

Keep one coordinating writer across the Hub change and a linked Nanoleaf companion PR under this issue. Sequence owner command/contract tests, independent review of that shared boundary, then Nanoleaf adoption and end-to-end consumer checks. These are tasks within one delivered behavior, not unrelated layer tickets. No new daemon, event bus, device broadcast or direct controller-database access.

Required input: #241's accepted provider-neutral retirement and delayed-event contract. #218 is delivered. Native end qualification in [#253](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/253) and Work/Free automation in [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) are related independent work, not prerequisites. #110 must not depend on this feature: it already consumes owner presence.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Use exact owner/session identity and observed revision/generation/turn guards so an old click cannot evict a fresh incarnation or a different selected source. Reuse bounded replay, authentication and Host/Origin protections. Repeated matching commands are idempotent; a timeout or lost response does not authorize a new request identity or optimistic success.

Like accepted retirement, eviction may discard that task tree's labels, notices, attention, task-project overrides, placement and animation state. Preserve unrelated sessions, global projects/colors/reservations/scenes/settings and all conversations. It is not acknowledgment, readership, completion, cancellation or approval. Keep one authoritative state owner and one existing writer per physical device.

An eligible new start may create a fresh generation with defaults, without old-effect replay. Recognizable late events and current-turn noise must not immediately resurrect the evicted record. Retain documented unknown-ordering and bounded-history limits rather than promising permanent suppression.

Evicting the last record produces a healthy empty owner snapshot. That allows #110's future explicitly enabled automation to select Free. Eviction itself sends no mode command; disabled automation, manual precedence and unavailable-feed hold behavior remain #110's responsibility. Device-only eviction keeps owner presence and therefore does not produce this result.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: coordinated source delivery in Hub and Nanoleaf; installation and physical qualification remain separately authorized.

- [ ] A guarded command removes the exact known session tree atomically, releases capacity and publishes one owner revision. Unknown/duplicate targets do not create records. Core/storage tests cover unrelated records and preserved global state.
- [ ] API tests reject unauthorized, read-only, wrong-owner, stale revision/generation/turn and replay-conflict requests without removal. A lost-response/duplicate case does not remove a replacement task or execute twice. Persisted retirement guards survive restart.
- [ ] Lifecycle tests cover all supported providers, read/acknowledgment and known late/current-turn events after eviction, plus an eligible new start with fresh defaults and no old effects. Document limits when evidence cannot distinguish old and new work.
- [ ] Real owner snapshots drive focused dashboard, Nanoleaf, Pixoo and Tidbyt consumer tests: rows/allocations/effects disappear, disconnected consumers reconcile later, and a consumer that misses the absent interval still resets the recreated generation where supported. Preserve the documented snapshot1.0/1.1 compatibility limits and normal device queues/cadence.
- [ ] Nanoleaf browser/API tests distinguish device-only eviction from Evict everywhere, preserve selection/focus, reject stale controls, and show unavailable/uncertain outcomes without falsely reporting global removal. User approval covers the concrete changed UI before merge.
- [ ] A fake-owner/presence scenario shows the last global eviction produces zero records while a local eviction does not. If #110 is delivered, run its first/last presence and manual-override tests against the compatible owner; otherwise keep this assertion at the snapshot boundary and carry the integration example into #110.
- [ ] Prepare issue-linked OpenSpec changes at delivery pickup for the owner command, lifecycle state and Nanoleaf control. Assess package/contract compatibility; run required owner/Hub/contract/MCP/workflow checks and Nanoleaf Python/browser/workflow/MCP checks as applicable. Both repositories require independent Standards/Specification reviews, matching CI, guarded merges and merged-main readback. The PR walkthrough covers ownership, duplicate/stale/timeout behavior and recovery limits.

These are planned checks, not completed acceptance. Source work changes no installed credentials, service, hooks, live database or physical device.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Multi-owner/remote installations and multi-operator policy: no requirement in this setup; revisit before adding another owner/operator.
- Additional device-specific eviction UIs or a new Hub dashboard/MCP control: the existing Nanoleaf action is the first caller. Future callers reuse the same owner operation when requested; do not add a separate suppression system per device.
- Bulk clear, undo/restoration history and agent cancellation: excluded. Fresh eligible work can appear with defaults; previously discarded task presentation metadata is not restored.
- Native quit/idle end reliability remains #253; manual global eviction does not qualify it. Automatic Work/Free behavior remains #110.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `d4657fa9f4614e2a933e0afe365ea4ed8e10aded` and the delivered #218/Nanoleaf #116 contracts. Complexity medium: one owner command, durable state transition and one existing cross-repository UI caller. Uncertainty medium: product behavior is settled; command schema, credential provisioning and compatibility need bounded design at pickup. Impact high: an authorized action deliberately discards shared monitoring metadata across consumers, so stale-target, authorization and durable no-replay coverage are mandatory. Deferred/backlog, blocked on #241. Reassess after #241 lands or if support expands beyond the selected owner and existing clients.

title: Make the slow-device browser isolation check deterministic
body:
## Outcome and real setup

Make the existing dashboard browser test for independent device progress reliable on Node 24 with Playwright and its fake controllers. During #218/#256 validation, the scenario “slow device serializes explicit commands while another device remains responsive” failed at `apps/dashboard/tests/matrix.mjs:27` with `429 !== 200`. One unchanged-head rerun and an independent matrix run passed. This is separate from the corrected Start Monitor assertion in #256; no production defect is established.

Evidence: [the observed failure recorded in #256](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/256), [the test at the delivered revision](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/49b29d06caee71be61dd8cee93bbca0c746ca7e7/apps/dashboard/tests/matrix.mjs#L24), and [the per-device capacity guard](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/49b29d06caee71be61dd8cee93bbca0c746ca7e7/apps/hub/src/controllers.ts#L26). The raw failure and successful rerun remain in the #218 delivery evidence. Priority: low; intermittent test maintenance, not a device incident.

## Smallest useful implementation

First reproduce the collision with controlled fake-controller/request ordering. The current test issues an extra wall read while browser polling can occupy that wall's single request slot. That is the leading explanation, not yet a deterministic diagnosis. Check `matrix.mjs`, `fixture.mjs` and the existing dashboard polling flow.

Then synchronize only the test/fixture so it measures a wall request admitted while the Pixoo request is still deliberately pending, without an unrelated wall poll consuming the slot. Prefer bounded observable barriers over fixed sleeps. Keep the fix within this test and the minimal supporting fixture. If the probe instead demonstrates a production defect, report it and obtain a scoped follow-up rather than relaxing the contract. Required source prerequisites: none. Coordinate if another delivery edits the matrix or fixture; shared files alone are not a dependency.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep one bounded request slot per device and independent progress between devices. Preserve the successful wall response, the existing less-than-700-ms wall-read assertion while Pixoo is delayed 800 ms, serial explicit command behavior, exact write checks, and absence of capacity errors on the tested UI action. No production queue change, extra retries, assertion removal, increased threshold or disabled scenario merely to obtain green.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only test maintenance.

- [ ] A bounded controlled probe reproduces the original HTTP 429 assertion and identifies the competing read. Retain red evidence; a passing rerun alone is insufficient.
- [ ] After correction, the wall request succeeds while the slow Pixoo operation remains pending. A negative control that makes wall progress depend on Pixoo still fails the isolation check.
- [ ] The original status, timing, command and no-retry assertions remain; run the focused scenario through a small documented set of deliberately ordered interleavings, then the complete `npm run test:dashboard:browser` suite.
- [ ] Follow the Dashboard checks in `docs/development.md`, applicable shared checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, all matching PR CI and merged-main CI. These are planned checks, not results from this planning task. Record any new failure separately rather than using blind reruns.

No product behavior delta is proposed, so an OpenSpec change is unnecessary unless diagnosis expands the scope. No application UI approval renewal is needed for a test-only correction; any actual UI change requires its normal approval.

## Meaningful deferrals

A general browser-flake framework, queue redesign, broad performance project and installed/hardware trial are excluded. They would add no evidence for this bounded scheduling defect. Reassess if the controlled probe implicates production routing or the required assertion itself is invalid.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `d4657fa9f4614e2a933e0afe365ea4ed8e10aded`. Complexity low: one scenario and its fixture. Uncertainty medium: the collision is observed but controlled reproduction remains the first task. Impact low: test-only correction; production scope expansion requires reassessment. Ready for bounded diagnosis followed by an evidenced test-only repair. No unfinished source dependency.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `medium` effort, or Codex on Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

title: Replace Pause motion with a one-shot circuit trace in the guide and atlas
body:
## Outcome and real setup

The owner found the Pause motion button confusing on a phone (#87's phone check): a second tap resumes only a slow top-bar streak, and the label never changes. The owner wants the button dropped from the work guide and the B.U.N.N.Y. atlas. The top-bar streak, which repeats every 25 s, becomes a single circuit trace that plays once on load. It runs down the screen through the page background as a branching, circuit-board pattern rather than one horizontal line.

Setup: the two generated documentation pages (guide and atlas) that share `docs/skins/`. They are read on desktop and phone, and published through agent-device-guide.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Skin template (`docs/skins/skin.py`):** stop supplying the `#motion-toggle` button, the stored `bunny-design-motion` preference and the `data-motion` attribute. Keep the theme toggle.
- **Neon skin (`docs/skins/neon-geometry-wars.css`):** replace the repeating streak with a one-shot circuit trace. It is CSS only, colored from existing tokens, sits behind content, runs top to bottom across the viewport width, and never repeats. The opening and the trace both finish within 5 s of load, so WCAG 2.2.2 needs no pause control.
- **Pages and checks:** remove the button from the guide and atlas generators, regenerate both, and update `check_skin.cjs`, `check_guide.cjs` and `docs/system-design/check.cjs`.
- **Docs:** update the style guide (`docs/application-ui-style-guide.md`) and `docs/work-guide/README.md` to drop the pause control from the skin rules.

No dependencies. The public republish follows the #87 procedure.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` still stops all decorative motion.
- Decoration stays out of the tab order, never covers text or controls, carries no meaning and prints as nothing.
- The token check still rejects color literals outside the token files.
- The theme toggle and its stored choice keep working across the guide and atlas.
- A stale stored `bunny-design-motion` value has no effect.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

1. Neither page has a Pause motion button, a `data-motion` attribute or motion storage.
2. On a fresh load, the circuit trace runs once, down and across the page background. The opening and the trace both finish within 5 s, with no infinite animation. Evidence: the browser checks assert that every animation is finite and ends by 5 s, plus screenshots mid-trace at 390 and 1440 px in dark and light.
3. Reduced motion runs no animation, the trace never intercepts pointer or keyboard input, and print has no decoration. Evidence: the extended skin check.
4. The guide and atlas builds, token check and browser checks pass, and full Depot CI passes.
5. The owner approves the atlas UI candidate, and the guide is published and hash-verified on Pages.

## Meaningful deferrals

- There is no user-facing way to stop the 5 s opening except the system Reduce Motion setting. That is acceptable under WCAG 2.2.2 for motion under 5 s. Revisit if a longer or repeating animation is proposed.
- #254 (Cards skin) and the style guide's skin template currently name the pause control. This issue updates the style guide and leaves a note on #254.

title: Coordinate modes, colors and scenes across all devices from the hub
body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

One operator controls all participating devices from B.U.N.N.Y. (the hub) as one system: the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, the Pixoo, LIFX bulbs and, once qualified, PC lighting.

- **Work:** every device shows the same colors for the same meaning. Each status (working, question, blocked, unread) uses the same color everywhere, and each project uses the same project color on every device.
- **Free:** the hub can start a coordinated look, so that every participating device plays something in the same colors, instead of each device being set separately in its own app.
- **Quiet** follows the same idea at low intensity.

### Smallest useful implementation

To be defined. Starting points:

- #67 already applies Work, Free or Quiet to Nanoleaf and Pixoo from one hub request. It deliberately uses fixed native mode mappings, no common color model and no hub-chosen scene. This issue would extend it or build on it.
- jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#139 delivered a configurable status palette for Nanoleaf. One palette is stored in the Nanoleaf installation and shared by the Lines and Panels, and only the Nanoleaf wall map edits it. Project colors are also stored and edited per installation there.
- #20 still has LIFX status colors as an open owner decision.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Each device keeps one light writer, through its owning controller service. The hub routes requests; it does not write to devices directly.
- Alert priority stays keyed by status, never by color.
- Manual control in vendor apps keeps working, with the existing ownership handoff.
- Credentials stay with their owning services.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

To be defined after clarification.

### Open questions for clarification

1. **Palette ownership:** does the hub own one shared palette that it pushes to every device, or a default that each device can override? Does the Nanoleaf wall map keep its own editor? jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#18 currently records palettes as per-device presentation preferences; this issue would revisit that.
2. **Project colors:** which system owns project identity colors across devices, and how is a project identified the same way everywhere?
3. **Free-mode looks:** what does "play things of the same color" mean on each device? For example: a Nanoleaf scene or effect, a LIFX color or effect, a Pixoo image or animation. Who owns restoring the previous content, and how does the hub hand control back to vendor apps?
4. **Participants:** which devices take part, and is participation configured per device?
5. **Color fidelity:** the same hex value looks different on a Line, a bulb and an LCD. Is per-device calibration needed?
6. **Relation to #67:** fold its fixed mode mappings into this, or deliver #67 first and extend it?

### Meaningful deferrals

None yet; decide during clarification.

Related: #67, #69, #20, #56, #45, jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#139, jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#18.

## Execution recommendation

**Status:** insufficient
**Missing:** The defined scope and acceptance criteria. The story is a backlog placeholder: the shared color model, the participating devices, how it extends #67 and the open LIFX color decision in #20 are still to be defined.

**Reassess when:** The owner refines the placeholder into a story with acceptance criteria.

title: Show and control every device from B.U.N.N.Y. device pages and a group page
body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It records a long-term direction until it is clarified and split into stories. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

One operator sees and controls every device from one B.U.N.N.Y. interface: the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, the Pixoo, LIFX bulbs and, once qualified, PC lighting. The owner set this direction on 2026-09-25:

- The device projects move into this repository under the B.U.N.N.Y. name ([#25](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/25), [#26](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/26)). The interface with controls for every device is the dashboard; the wall map's art moves into it and the wall map becomes Nanoleaf's advanced editor (ADR 0007, 2026-09-25; this line originally said the wall map grows into the interface).
- The interface has several pages. A device page covers one product, for example a Nanoleaf page with today's wall-map art. A group page shows every device together, using the same art alongside LIFX, Pixoo and other device graphics.
- Designs, graphics and images are shared components that any page reuses, not per-page copies.
- Each device runs its own mode. Some devices can be in Work while others are in Free, and in Free each device can be controlled differently.
- In Work, the operator chooses which devices show tasks. Devices can share one task pool ([#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272)) or be pulled out and shown on their own.

This is not needed for the first or second version. Near-term stories should avoid choices that block it.

### Smallest useful implementation

To be defined. Starting points:

- [codex-nanoleaf#44](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/44) adds a device selector to the wall map, giving the Lines and the Panels one view each. It is the first device page, and it draws each device through a reusable renderer.
- [codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113) makes the Panels a second controller device, so the hub and dashboard control each Nanoleaf device separately.
- `apps/dashboard` already lists devices and changes their modes. [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182) gives it the B.U.N.N.Y. name and Neon skin. Section 10 of the [application UI style guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/application-ui-style-guide.md) keeps the wall map a separate application for now.
- [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267) owns shared colors and coordinated Free looks across devices. [#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/56) puts PC lighting controls in the shared UI.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Each device keeps one light writer, through its owning controller service. Pages and the hub route requests; they never write to devices directly.
- Credentials stay with their owning services. The browser never receives device tokens.
- Alert priority stays keyed by status. No page layout or device mode hides a red or yellow alert on a device that shows tasks.
- Task placement, reservations, unread tracking, scenes and mode selections survive the move into this repository.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

To be defined after clarification.

### Open questions for clarification

1. **Codebase:** answered on 2026-09-25 by [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-bunny-shell.md). The dashboard in `apps/dashboard` is the shell. The wall map's Prism renderer becomes hub-owned shared device art (#355), Nanoleaf exposes geometry read-only (codex-nanoleaf#169) and its remaining edits move behind the integration extension (codex-nanoleaf#170), and the wall map stays Nanoleaf's advanced editor until it retires (codex-nanoleaf#171). Style guide section 10 was revised in the same change. Not decided: the final page split (question 2) and the group layout (question 4).
2. **Pages:** which pages exist (per product, per device, group), and how does the operator move between them?
3. **Shared art:** in what form are device graphics shared (SVG components, a sprite set, the Prism material), and who owns each device's art?
4. **Group layout:** are devices placed by their physical position in the room or by a chosen logical arrangement? The combined Nanoleaf layout in [codex-nanoleaf#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) needs the same decision, so make it once.
5. **Controls:** which controls appear on the group page, and which stay on each device's own page?

### Meaningful deferrals

None yet; decide during clarification.

Related: #25, #26, #56, #182, #267, #272, codex-nanoleaf#17, codex-nanoleaf#44, codex-nanoleaf#47, codex-nanoleaf#113.

title: Let devices join or leave one shared task pool
body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It records a long-term direction until it is clarified and split into stories. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome and real setup

In Work mode, the operator decides how tasks spread across devices. The owner set this direction on 2026-09-25:

- A device can show tasks on its own. That includes showing every task, as the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels each do today.
- Devices can join one shared pool, so each task is placed once across all pooled devices, like one extended display.
- The operator can pull a single device out of the pool, for example to put it in Free, and add it back later.
- Any device can take part: the Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, the Pixoo, LIFX bulbs and qualified PC lighting.

This is not needed for the first or second version. Near-term stories should avoid choices that block it. The B.U.N.N.Y. pages that show and control these devices are [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).

### Smallest useful implementation

To be defined. Starting points:

- [codex-nanoleaf#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/47) designs a combined Lines-and-Panels pool inside Nanoleaf. It is the natural first pool and should use the membership model decided here.
- Nanoleaf already stores a mode per device. A device in Free or Quiet shows no tasks, so "Lines only" or "Panels only" needs no pool.
- [#262](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/262) evicts a task across devices through the shared owner. Pooled devices must reconcile that the same way.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- The shared monitoring owner stays the single task source, and each device keeps one writer. A pool is a placement decision, not a new writer or a merged controller device.
- Each device keeps its own identity in the hub and controller APIs ([codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113)).
- Reservations, unread tracking, active comets and effect epochs survive a device joining or leaving the pool.
- Red and yellow alerts keep their priority on every pooled device.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

To be defined after clarification.

### Open questions for clarification

1. **Placement across different devices:** a Line has two zones, a triangle one, a Pixoo a screen and a LIFX bulb one color. Can a bulb or screen hold one task, several, or only a summary?
2. **Allocator:** does the hub owner allocate tasks across the pool, or does one device controller allocate for the whole pool?
3. **Leaving:** what happens to a device's placed tasks when it leaves the pool, goes offline or changes mode?
4. **Projects:** how project reservations and Shared overflow work across devices.
5. **Pools:** can several pools exist at once, or only one?

### Meaningful deferrals

None yet; decide during clarification.

Related: #271, #262, #267, codex-nanoleaf#44, codex-nanoleaf#47, codex-nanoleaf#113.
