title: Open B.U.N.N.Y. from a bookmark without a token or launcher step
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The owner opens B.U.N.N.Y. on the PC by clicking one bookmark or shortcut and lands on the dashboard signed in. No token is generated, copied or pasted, and a reload or a second tab stays signed in. This applies to the one installed hub (`codex-nanoleaf-monitor.service`, loopback port 8788) used from the Windows browser and from WSL. Phone or LAN access is excluded; the hub stays loopback-only.

What exists today, from [#179](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/179) (PR #180): `node apps/hub/dist/cli.js open <config>` asks the hub over the owner-only socket `bunny-launch.sock` for a 30-second code, opens `http://127.0.0.1:8788/#launch=<code>`, and the page exchanges the code for an 8-hour browser session held only in page memory. The installed hub already serves that socket. What still hurts:

- No shortcut or bookmark runs the command, so the owner falls back to the collapsed "Use a separately provisioned access token" form, whose token is created by hand (README "Credentials").
- A reload or a new tab loses the session and shows the login page again.
- `http://localhost:8788/` is refused (the Host check expects `127.0.0.1`).

### Smallest useful implementation

**Decision (owner, 2026-09-25): Option 1.** Option 2 is kept below only as the rejected alternative.

**Option 1 (chosen): trusted-loopback sign-in.** A new optional private configuration field, for example `browserAccess: "trusted-loopback"`, off by default. When set, the page calls a new same-origin route (for example `POST /api/dashboard/v1/session`) on load and receives the same bounded browser session the launcher issues today: `read` and `control` on configured controller aliases, no `ingest`, `admin`, playback or MCP, 8-hour expiry, 16-session cap, retirement through the existing `retireBrowser` path. The route enforces the existing Host, Origin, `Sec-Fetch-Site` and `X-Pixoo-Request` checks. No cookie and no storage: a reload simply asks again, and `pagehide` logs the previous session out. The login page disappears when the option is on; a failed request shows the current launcher and manual-token fallbacks. The launcher and manual token keep working for configurations without the option.

**Option 2 (rejected): keep the code exchange, make it sticky.** Store the launched session in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, loopback-scoped cookie with a longer lifetime, add a Windows shortcut and a WSL alias for the `open` command, and accept `localhost` as a Host alias. The owner still runs the launcher after each expiry and on any machine reboot.

Also: accept `localhost:<port>` as well as `127.0.0.1:<port>` in the Host check, and document the bookmark URL in the hub README and `apps/hub/SETUP.md`. Blocked by nothing. Related independent work: [#232](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/232) (setup guide), [#203](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203) (owner sign-in for the future remote workspace, which this does not touch).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Loopback-only listener, exact Host and Origin checks, the `Sec-Fetch-Site` rule and the `X-Pixoo-Request` header on every write. These already stop cross-site pages and DNS rebinding and must stay.
- Machine credentials for ingest, admin, playback and MCP stay digest-only in the configuration; the browser session never gains them.
- Browser-session retirement from [#244](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244): expiry, eviction, logout and shutdown retire tickets, streams and replay entries.
- One state owner, one writer per device; the page only routes through the hub.

Assurance lost with Option 1, stated plainly: today a local program that is not the owner's browser needs a configured token or the owner-only socket to command devices. With the option on, any program on the PC that can send a same-origin-looking loopback request with the custom header can issue the same read and control commands. That matches the Nanoleaf wall map on port 8765, which has no sign-in and labels itself "Local to this PC". The devices are lights and displays. Reassess before any LAN, phone or second-operator exposure, as docs/sdlc.md already requires.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source first, then the owner's installation on explicit request.

- Source: with the option on, opening `/` from a fresh browser context shows the dashboard with controls enabled, and a reload keeps it working. With the option off, behavior is unchanged. Hub unit tests cover: the route refused without the option, refused on a bad Host, Origin or missing header, sessions capped and retired, and MCP still refusing browser sessions. Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass, and `retirement.mjs` still passes.
- Acceptance examples for this credential change are written in the OpenSpec proposal before implementation, per docs/sdlc.md scope defaults, and the PR carries the short walkthrough (session ownership, expiry, reload, duplicate tab, failure case, recovery).
- Installation gate: a named owner adds the field to the installed `host.json`, updates the hub package under the existing backup and receipt procedure, and confirms the bookmark opens signed in. Source merge alone does not claim this.
- UI change: the login page and shell change, so the current candidate needs explicit owner approval before merge.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Phone or LAN access: excluded. Owning issues [#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/47) and [#203](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203).
- Windows-side shortcut for the launcher and a sticky cookie session (Option 2): not needed, since a bookmark suffices under Option 1. Revisit only if the trusted-loopback option is ever turned off on the installed hub.
- Removing the manual-token form entirely: keep it for configurations without the option. Remove it when no configuration uses it.

Related stories filed together on 2026-09-25: [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) (dashboard layout) and [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278) (shared places navigation). Neither blocks this one.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Open B.U.N.N.Y. from a bookmark with no token, code or launcher step, and stay signed in across reloads.

title: Make the dashboard a dense control surface instead of long single-column pages
body:
### Outcome and real setup

Once signed in, the owner sees a dense control surface instead of a long column of forms. On the installed hub with the wall (Nanoleaf) and pixel (Pixoo) components, at 1440 px wide, a component page shows its status and every control without scrolling past about two screens, and the Activity page shows the sessions that matter in the first screen. The 390 px phone layout stays usable. Nothing about what the controls do changes.

What the pages look like today (full-page captures from the #245 candidate and the #182 approval set):

- The component page is one column: a 10-row fact list, then about twelve stacked forms (Mode, Reapply, Integration settings, Element, Task and Project mappings, Power, Brightness, Media, Scenes, Switch to Free), each with its own heading, one- to three-sentence hint, button and status line. The wall page is 3,827 px tall at 1280 wide and 4,933 px on a phone. Selects stop at half the column, so the right half is empty.
- The Activity page spends its first 400 px on a hero heading, a subtitle and a four-cell stats strip before any session appears. Each session is a full-width card with a six-item fact list, a label form and one form per notice.
- The Connections page is a hero, a six-item fact list and a few paragraphs.
- The login page is a two-line headline and two hint paragraphs.

Every hint is inline JSX in `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx`, and the application skin defines no spacing or type tokens, so the layout reads as raw pixel values (style guide §4.1).

### Smallest useful implementation

**Owner direction (2026-09-25):** a dense control surface built as a dashboard of components and widgets, keeping the futuristic Neon Geometry Wars look from style guide §3. Decoration stays within the guide's rule of a calm surface with no glow on every card; the density comes from layout, not from more chrome. Whether every component ends up on one page or keeps its own page is open; the owner chose on 2026-09-25 to build modular widgets first and settle that from the built candidate.

**Recommendation for the page split.** Build every control and status block as a widget with one interface (component alias, capability, current snapshot, command action) that any page can place. The home grid shows every component's everyday widgets (status, mode, power, brightness, scenes) together, so one page is enough for daily use. Each component keeps a page that composes the same widgets plus its rare, larger forms (Nanoleaf assignments and mappings, the Pixoo Monitor view, media). A widget renders identically wherever it is placed, so moving one between pages is a placement change, not a rewrite. Decide the final split after the candidate exists.

Graph widgets (velocity and live series) belong to [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283) and use this widget interface; their data comes from [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282).

Follow-on widget stories filed 2026-09-25: [#286](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/286) (wall miniature), [#287](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/287) (component inventory and widget ranking), [#288](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/288) (command palette and D-pad navigation). [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289) brings Tidbyt and LIFX into the same component and widget set.

Work in two steps so the owner approves a design before code moves.

1. **Design candidate.** A static HTML mock in the application skin for the four views (login, Activity, component, Connections) at 1440 px and 390 px, using the Nanoleaf wall map's three-column density (rail, canvas, inspector) as the reference. Proposed changes:
   - Component page: a one-line status strip (health, mode, power, brightness, observation age, pending commands) replaces the fact list; the fact list moves into a "Details" disclosure. Controls become cards in a two- or three-column grid: Mode with Reapply, Power, Brightness, Scenes, Media. Nanoleaf mapping forms sit in one "Assignments" panel; the Pixoo Monitor form in one "Monitor" panel. Each card keeps one short label line; longer guidance moves behind a help control or a `title`.
   - Home: the Activity view becomes a widget grid. One widget per registered component shows its health, mode, power and brightness with its quick actions (apply mode, power, reapply), and links to the full component page. Sessions, attention and collector health are widgets in the same grid, so the first screen shows the whole installation at once.
   - Activity: drop the hero and subtitle for a page title and the stats strip in one row. Sessions become compact rows with the badge, identity and an inline label field; notices expand under their row.
   - Connections: fold into a compact status panel reachable from the sidebar footer, or a two-column card page.
   - Login: one line and one button (or nothing, once the sign-in story lands).
   - Spacing and type: add the `--space-*` and `--type-*` roles to the application skin and use them, so the dashboard and the documentation skin share one scale.
2. **Implementation.** Apply the approved candidate in `apps/dashboard`, add hash routes for the built-in views and components (`#/activity`, `#/component/<alias>`, `#/connections`) so pages have URLs and back-button history, and update the browser, matrix, retirement and lifecycle checks whose selectors and exact texts change.

Dependencies: land [#247](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/247) first or in the same change, because the routes need the discriminated navigation value it introduces. Related independent work: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) (device and group pages later) and [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267) (shared colors). Do not choose a layout that blocks a group page.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Every control keeps its accessible name, its explicit apply action and its pending, unavailable, uncertain, error and stale states from the shared command lifecycle (#245). No control becomes implicit or auto-applied.
- Keyboard order, skip link, focus restoration after refresh and reconnect (the `.edit` group lookup), reduced motion, axe WCAG 2.1 AA at desktop and 390 px, and no horizontal overflow.
- Fixed-meaning status colors and the skin layer boundary from the style guide (§4.2, §4.3): a skin changes values, not layout semantics or which control is primary.
- Exact status sentences from `client.ts` and `lifecycle.ts`; shortening a hint must not change a status.
- The hub serves only `/`, `dashboard.js` and `dashboard.css` with the current CSP; no inline styles.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

- The home view shows every registered component as a widget with its status and quick actions on the first screen at 1440 px.
- The owner approves the design candidate, then the implemented candidate (screenshots at 1440 px and 390 px for all four views and the wall and pixel components), renewed after any later UI change, recorded on the PR per docs/sdlc.md.
- Full-page height of the wall component page at 1280 px wide is under 2,000 px, down from 3,827 px, and no view has an empty right half at 1440 px.
- `npm run test:dashboard`, the browser and matrix checks, `retirement.mjs`, `style.test.mjs` (no raw colors outside `src/skins/`) and the hub dashboard test all pass. The style guide §7 and §12 checklists are updated with the new measurements.
- OpenSpec: the unified-dashboard spec gains the routing and layout requirements; the approval requirement is unchanged.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Device art, group page and wall-map merge: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).
- Light scheme and the Neon decoration layer for the dashboard (`data-skin`): deferred in #182; revisit after this layout lands.
- Glossary labels such as "Eyes" for freshness: the style guide §11 leaves these to the owning UI issue; not part of this change.

Related stories filed together on 2026-09-25: [#276](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/276) (sign-in without a token, which removes the login page this story would otherwise redesign) and [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278) (shared places navigation, which adds a sidebar group this layout must leave room for). [#279](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/279) clears documentation leftovers. None block this one.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Turn the long single-column pages into a dense control surface with status strips, control cards and page URLs.
**Highlight:** next step, The dense home is where ADR 0007 settles the page split; the widget stories build on it.

title: Reach every B.U.N.N.Y. surface from one shared places navigation
body:
### Outcome and real setup

Every B.U.N.N.Y. surface reaches every other surface with one click, through the same navigation in the same order with the same labels. The surfaces are:

| Place | What it is today | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work guide | `docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html` | Public at https://jimmie-potts.github.io/agent-device-guide/ |
| Architecture | The nine Archify viewers, including the A2 system map ("the system") and the S4 walkthrough | Public under `/architecture/` |
| Atlas | The system design atlas: overview, walkthrough, 26 component pages, the complete reading view, the state and actions viewer | Public under `/atlas/` |
| Reference | The atlas API and database reference | Public under `/atlas/reference/` |
| B.U.N.N.Y. | The hub dashboard | Local only, `http://127.0.0.1:8788/` |
| Wall | The Nanoleaf wall map, owned by codex-nanoleaf | Local only, `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` |

Today these sit on three islands with no shared navigation. The guide links to the atlas and the viewers, the atlas links back to the guide only in the public export, the viewers link nowhere, the dashboard links only to the optional advanced editor, and nothing links to the dashboard or the wall. Brand text differs on every surface ("AGENT DEVICE / WORK GUIDES", "B.U.N.N.Y. / SYSTEM DESIGN", "◈ B.U.N.N.Y. / LOCAL INTEGRATION", "Codex × Nanoleaf / Wall map").

Public surfaces stay public and keep working on the phone. Local surfaces stay loopback-only and appear in the navigation as local entries that open only on the PC.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **One places manifest.** A small committed file under `docs/skins/` (for example `places.json`) lists each place with its label, public URL, local URL and group (Public or Local). Every generator reads it; nothing hand-edits generated HTML.
2. **One shared strip on the documentation surfaces.** `build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py` and the reference build render the same "Places" strip in the shared documentation skin: the B.U.N.N.Y. wordmark, the current place name, and links to the other places. `architecture_diagrams.py` injects the same strip into each rendered viewer after Archify renders, since the viewers keep their own CSS. `export_public.py` uses the public URLs and keeps the local entries tagged "Local", so the phone sees them but knows they open on the PC. The existing local atlas gets its guide link, not only the public export.
3. **The same places in the dashboard.** The sidebar gains a "Places" group built from the manifest at bundle time: Wall on loopback, and the public guide, architecture, atlas and reference URLs. Links to public pages are ordinary anchors; local links keep the numeric-loopback rule the advanced editor link already enforces.
4. **One brand line.** Every surface shows the B.U.N.N.Y. wordmark and its place name, following style guide §10, with the wall keeping its own title until it merges under [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).
5. **Wall link back.** codex-nanoleaf adds a "B.U.N.N.Y." link in the wall map header to `http://127.0.0.1:8788/`. This needs an issue in that repository; file it when this story is picked up.

Dependencies: none required. Related independent work: [#276](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/276) (so the dashboard link lands signed in), [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) (hash routes make deep links to a component possible later), [#254](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/254) (skin picker, which would read the same manifest), and [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Public pages never need a token, a local service or a private path. No local URL, credential or private runtime data enters the public export beyond the two loopback addresses, which carry nothing secret.
- The hub keeps serving only its three assets with the current CSP; the dashboard is not framed or embedded anywhere.
- The wall map's own CSRF token and loopback rule are untouched.
- The docs skin token check (`docs/skins/check_tokens.py`), the guide checks and the atlas checks keep passing. The viewer and reference styling exemption in the guide README stays; the injected strip uses the shared skin's fixed tokens only.
- Guide revisions still follow the guide maintenance procedure, and public publication still needs the owner's finish line and Pages receipts.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source, one guide revision, then public publication on the owner's request.

- From each of the six places, every other place is one click away, in the same order and with the same label. Checked by a browser script over the built local outputs and by hand on the running dashboard.
- On a phone over the public site, the guide, viewers, atlas and reference open and their strip fits at 390 px without horizontal overflow; local entries show the "Local" tag.
- `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `docs/system-design/check.py` and `check.cjs`, and `check_tokens.py` pass. `export_public.py` produces a manifest with the strip present in every exported page.
- Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass with the new sidebar group; axe passes at desktop and 390 px.
- UI approval: the guide strip is exempt under the guide UI exception. The atlas, viewer and dashboard changes need explicit owner approval of the current candidate, renewed after changes.
- Publication: after the guide-only or mixed PR merges, the public edition is copied under the existing procedure with Pages receipts. Source merge alone does not claim the site is live.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Serving the guide and atlas from the hub so they work offline on the PC: not needed while the PC has internet; revisit if the hub moves to a host without it ([#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/42)).
- Reaching the dashboard or wall from the phone: excluded; [#47](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/47) and [#203](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203).
- A shared dark and light toggle across origins: the `bunny-design-theme` key only works within one origin, and the dashboard is dark only. Revisit with [#254](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/254).
- Merging the wall map into the dashboard: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271).

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** One places navigation across the guide, architecture viewers, atlas, reference, dashboard and wall.

title: Clear the visual-alignment leftovers in the style guide, atlas and system map
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The visual-alignment work from #85, #86, #181, #182 and #269 is done, but a check on 2026-09-25 found leftovers that make the surfaces read as unfinished. Fixing them keeps the documentation truthful before the places navigation in [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278) lands.

Found:

- `docs/application-ui-style-guide.md` §1 and §10 still describe the `BUNNY` spelling and wordmark as current, although PR #269 shipped `B.U.N.N.Y.` in the dashboard.
- The local atlas (`docs/system-design/build.py`) has no link back to the guide; only `export_public.py` injects one. The public atlas and the local atlas therefore differ.
- Issue #186 and older text call the hub repository private. All three source repositories are public (guide README "Publish the public edition").
- The dashboard bundle never sets `data-skin`, so the documentation skin's decoration layer and the dark/light toggle do not apply to it. #182 deferred this on purpose; the style guide should say so where it describes the skin layers, so a reader does not expect the toggle.

### Smallest useful implementation

- Add the guide link to the local atlas build so the exporter no longer injects it.
- Correct the "private repository" wording where it remains in repository docs. Issue text is left as history.
- Refresh the A2 system map labels for the installed hub and the Tidbyt, LIFX and playback additions. This changes the atlas build and needs atlas UI approval.

The viewer overflow stays with its existing note unless a viewer is re-rendered anyway.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Generated outputs are rebuilt through their generators; no hand edits to generated HTML.
- The documentation skin token check, guide checks and atlas checks keep passing.
- Public publication is a separate step with its own receipts.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, with one guide revision if generated pages change.

- The style guide no longer describes `BUNNY` as the current spelling and names the dashboard's skin scope.
- The local atlas overview shows the guide link, and `export_public.py` no longer needs to inject one.
- No repository doc calls the hub repository private.
- A2 labels match the installed topology; the atlas candidate is approved by the owner before merge.
- `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `docs/system-design/check.py`, `check.cjs` and `check_tokens.py` pass.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Dashboard light scheme and decoration layer: deferred by #182; revisit after [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277).
- Viewer vertical overflow: keep the guide README note; fix when a viewer is re-rendered for another reason.

title: Record a private local history of tasks, devices, music and hub health for graphs
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The hub keeps a private, timestamped history of what B.U.N.N.Y. sees and does, so dashboard widgets can draw graphs that move through the day: tasks seen and finished, attention raised and cleared, device modes and brightness over time, minutes of music played, hub health. Everything stays on the PC in the hub's private directory. Nothing enters Git, the public guide or any service.

What exists today: the hub stores current state only. The agent-state journal keeps 24 hours of change summaries in memory and on disk, no route exposes it, and retirement and expiry leave no journal row. Controller, integration and playback snapshots carry no wall-clock timestamps and nothing samples them. Playback holds only the latest title. Performance receipts are one-off runs. There is no time series anywhere in the hub.

### Data catalog (brainstorm, 2026-09-25)

Everything below is counts, states and durations with neutral IDs or user-chosen labels. No prompts, transcripts, tool content, automatically copied task titles or private paths, per AGENTS.md and the lifecycle contract.

| Area | Capture | Why it helps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent tasks | Session started, turn started and ended, attention raised (input, approval) and resolved, read observed, retired or expired; per provider (Codex, Claude) and per user-chosen label | Tasks seen and closed per hour and day, time waiting on the owner, time blocked, sessions alive at once |
| Lights and displays | Mode per device over time (Work, Quiet, Free), power and brightness samples, commands issued with outcome, external-control takeovers, observation freshness gaps, wall Line occupancy (Lines assigned, free, held by stale tasks), scene activations, Pixoo playlist generation advances | Time in each mode, how often a manual change overrides B.U.N.N.Y., how full the wall is, which scenes get used |
| Music | Playing, paused and stopped minutes per day, play and pause commands, track changes; optionally artist and album counts when the owner turns on `history.playbackTitles` | Listening time through the day, top artists; titles are private listening data and stay opt-in and local |
| Hub health | Collector state, loss count, admission rejections, feed clients, browser sessions, process RSS, uptime and restarts, hook receipt latency samples | Spot leaks and outages before they show on the wall; compare with the performance budgets |
| Development | Issues opened and closed per day, PRs merged, issue cycle time, PR open-to-merge time, commits per day, from a refreshed GitHub history snapshot | Velocity widgets; owned by the status screen story |
| Later | Tidbyt installation presence, LIFX per-bulb state once connected, PC lighting, room or desk presets, Sonos as a second source | Same series shapes; add when the device joins the hub |

### Smallest useful implementation

- **One private store.** `history.sqlite` beside `state.sqlite`, owner-only, single writer (the hub process), two append-only tables: `events(at_ms, kind, subject, label, value)` and `samples(at_ms, series, subject, value)`. Raw rows kept 30 days; hourly and daily rollups kept indefinitely in a third table. Bounded size with oldest-first pruning.
- **One recorder in the hub.** It mirrors every journal commit, retirement and expiry into `events`; samples each configured controller snapshot, the Nanoleaf and Pixoo integration snapshots and the playback snapshot every 30 seconds, stamping hub wall-clock time and writing only when a value changes; and records each command outcome. Playback titles are stored only when `history.playbackTitles` is true in the private configuration; otherwise only status and counts.
- **One read route.** `GET /api/history/v1/series?series=<name>&from=<ms>&to=<ms>&bucket=<minute|hour|day>` with `read` scope, returning buckets for one or more series, plus `GET /api/history/v1/catalog` listing available series and their subjects. No write route; no MCP tool yet.
- **One export.** `cli.js history-export <config> --csv <dir>` for the owner's own analysis, written outside Git.

Dependencies: none required. Related independent work: [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/139) (reliable event history, which this does not claim to be), [#123](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123) (performance), [#222](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222) (push notifications). [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283) (Status page) consumes the route.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- This is a metrics store, not an event archive. It is never presented as complete history, never feeds current-status calculation, and never replays anything to a device. The agent-state journal rules from the core spec stay as they are.
- One state owner and one writer per device are untouched; the recorder only reads snapshots the hub already fetches and the journal the hub already writes.
- Privacy allowlist enforced in the recorder with a test: no field outside the allowlist reaches the store; playback titles absent unless opted in. The store, exports and rollups stay out of Git and out of the public edition.
- Bounded resources: sampling adds no controller polling beyond what the dashboard already causes; the recorder writes in batches; the store has a size cap and the hub keeps serving when the store is unavailable.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source first, then the owner's installation on explicit request.

- Fake-controller and fake-playback tests show events and samples appear with wall-clock stamps, change-only sampling, rollups, pruning at the cap and the 30-day boundary, and route buckets that match the raw rows.
- A privacy test injects a title, a prompt-like field and a private path into every source and shows none reaches the store without the opt-in, and only the title with it.
- The hub serves normally with the store read-only or missing, with a health flag in the context route.
- Memory and hook latency stay within `docs/performance/linux-budgets.json` in the standalone measurement.
- Installation gate: a named owner updates the hub package and confirms series accumulate on the installed hub for a day.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Reliable, ordered, gap-aware event history: [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/139). Consequence: counts here can miss events the journal missed.
- Read versus unread transitions per chat: the journal does not record the direction, so waiting-to-be-read time stays approximate until [#139](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/139) or a journal change.
- Tidbyt, LIFX and PC lighting series: when those devices join the hub ([#16](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/16), [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/17), [#53](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/53)).
- MCP access to history: add when an agent needs it.

**Coordination with the moments work (checked 2026-09-25):** [#296](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/296)'s moment log is a bounded local log "alongside" this store. Prefer one file: moments become `events` rows with kind `moment.*` (trigger, target device, receipt, pre-empted) so the Status page and the moment-log widget read one route. Events from [#293](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/293) (GitHub) and [#298](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/298) (calendar) enter the same table deduplicated by their stable event IDs, and a restart never re-emits them. Commands that moments send through the hub are already covered by the command-outcome rows.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Private local history store with a data catalog: agent tasks, lights, music, hub health, sampled by the hub and read through one series route.
**Highlight:** idea, A private local history so widgets can graph the day.

title: Add a Status page with velocity and live graph widgets to the dashboard
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The dashboard gets a Status page and a set of graph widgets. The owner sees development velocity for the three repositories (issues opened and closed per day, PRs merged per week, median issue cycle time, median PR open-to-merge time, commits per day) and live graphs that move through the day: tasks seen and finished, attention waiting on the owner, device mode timelines, brightness, minutes of music, hub memory and health. The widgets use the same widget system as the dense dashboard, so any of them can sit on the home grid.

This is the owner's own view of the owner's own work. It shows counts and trends, never scores, streaks or comparisons, which [#198](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/198) already excludes for the guide timeline.

What exists today: `docs/work-guide/work/history/github-history.json` already holds merged PRs, closed issues with created and closed times, commits and issues created per day for the Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo repositories, refreshed by hand. The guide draws one static SVG of merge dots from it. The dashboard has four count tiles and no charts. The hub records no time series.

### Smallest useful implementation

Two phases. The first needs no new data capture.

1. **Velocity from the saved GitHub history.**
   - Add `scripts/refresh-github-history.mjs`, a read-only paginated `gh api` fetcher that reproduces the saved file byte-for-byte for unchanged entries (the guide refresh needs the same script; today there is none). Extend the entries with PR closed-without-merge and issue label snapshots only if cheap.
   - The hub reads an optional private configuration field `githubHistory: <absolute path>` and serves it at `GET /api/status/v1/velocity` with `read` scope, computing per-day and per-week buckets, medians and the snapshot age. A stale or missing file shows its date, never a guess.
   - Velocity widgets: issues opened versus closed per day (line), PRs merged per week (bar), cycle-time distribution (small multiples per repo), commits per day (sparkline), with the snapshot time visible.
2. **Live graphs from the history store.** Once the [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282) route lands, add widgets for tasks seen and finished today (line, updated with the 5-second poll), attention waiting (step line), per-device mode timeline (horizontal bands), brightness (line), music minutes (bar per hour), RSS and collector state (sparkline with the budget line).

Charts are hand-drawn inline SVG React components (line, bar, step, band, sparkline) with a shared axis and scale helper, drawn from the application skin's tokens with the fixed status colors for status series. No charting library, because the CSP allows only `'self'` scripts and many chart libraries need `eval`. Each chart has a text alternative (a table toggle) and honors reduced motion.

Dependencies: phase 1 needs [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277)'s widget interface or lands as the first widgets of it. Phase 2 needs [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282). Related independent work: [#198](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/198) (guide timeline scrubber over the same history file), [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Opening or refreshing the Status page sends no device command and marks nothing read.
- The velocity route reads a file the owner configured; it never calls GitHub from the hub, and the refresh script stays read-only and outside the hub process.
- No private data on the page: labels come from user-chosen session labels and repository issue titles, which are already public; playback titles appear only with the store's opt-in.
- Style guide §9: text cues as well as color, reduced motion, no decorative motion beyond 5 seconds, 390 px layouts without overflow, axe WCAG 2.1 AA.
- The dashboard CSP and the three-asset rule stay as they are.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only for phase 1; phase 2 after [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282) is installed.

- Phase 1: with the saved history file configured, the Status page shows the five velocity widgets with the snapshot time; with no file, it says so. Unit tests cover bucket math on a fixture with month boundaries and a day with zero activity; the refresh script reproduces the checked-in file for unchanged entries.
- Phase 2: with fake series, each live widget renders, updates on poll, and shows its table alternative; a day with a gap draws the gap, not a line across it.
- Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass with the new page; axe passes at desktop and 390 px.
- The owner approves the design candidate and then the implemented candidate, renewed after later UI changes.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Review timing, label transitions and in-progress start times: not in the saved history; add to the fetcher only when a widget needs them.
- Achievement scores, streaks and productivity comparisons: excluded on purpose, as in [#198](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/198).
- Showing velocity in the public guide: the guide keeps its own timeline; revisit if the owner wants the same widgets there.

**Coordination with [#293](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/293) (checked 2026-09-25):** the two GitHub readers serve different needs and stay separate. This story's read-only snapshot refresh gives history back to each repository's creation, which a poller that starts today cannot. #293's bounded poller gives live PR and CI events for rules and moments. Once #293 emits into [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282), phase 2 adds a "merged today" live widget from those events, and the snapshot refresh may reuse #293's repository allowlist and credential so there is one GitHub configuration.

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Status page with velocity widgets from the saved GitHub history first, then live graphs from the history store.
**Highlight:** idea, A Status page with velocity and live graph widgets.

title: Render playback artwork on the Pixoo and Tidbyt now-playing cards
body:
Follow-up from [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38), which delivered text-only now-playing cards:

- Tidbyt: [#280](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/280).
- Pixoo: [divoom-app-upgrade#90](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/90).

#38 required this open follow-up for artwork rendering before it closed, and [#229](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) (AC6) links it.

## Outcome and real setup

Once #229 exposes optional, source-scoped artwork through the authenticated playback boundary, each display's owning controller sizes and renders it on its card:

- the Tidbyt runner in `controllers/tidbyt`;
- the Pixoo app in divoom-app-upgrade.

The setup is the same as #38: one operator, the installed hub with the HT-A9 source, and the installed Tidbyt runner and Pixoo service.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Read the artwork reference that #229 defines, with the displays' existing credentials and read cadence.
- Scale artwork to each display (64×32 Tidbyt, 64×64 Pixoo) inside the owning renderer, next to the existing text layout.
- Keep writes on each device's existing queue and presentation gates.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep everything #38 settled:

- the Tidbyt rotation tile;
- the Pixoo Monitor pop-up and the Media Off, Pop-up and Whole song setting;
- the 15 s Tidbyt gate and the 2 s Pixoo poll;
- the stale and removal rules;
- one writer per device.

The text-only card stays the fallback. Artwork from an earlier track or source is never shown on the current one.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Each renderer shows correctly sized, readable artwork for the current track: golden or exact-pixel tests with fake artwork.
- Artwork updates after a track change and after a source change, and delayed artwork from an earlier track is discarded: fake-feed tests.
- The text fallback appears when artwork is missing, invalid or unavailable: fake-feed tests.
- Renderer checks are recorded separately from physical display acceptance. Physical checks need a separately authorized trial on each device.
- Delivery target: source merged in both repositories.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Scrolling, rotation slots and foreground Tidbyt takeover stay out of scope, as in #38.

Blocked by #229.

## Guide

**Topic:** controls-music
**Note:** Playback artwork on the Pixoo and Tidbyt now-playing cards, after the text cards.

title: Show a read-only wall miniature widget on the dashboard home
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The dashboard home shows a read-only miniature of the Nanoleaf wall: which Lines are lit, in which project color, and why (working, question, blocked, unread, free, held by a stale task). The owner reads the wall's state without opening the wall map on port 8765, and one click opens the full wall map or the wall component page. This runs on the installed hub with the registered `nanoleaf-wall` controller. It sends no commands.

What exists today: the hub's Nanoleaf integration snapshot already carries `mode`, `projects[{id, color}]`, `tasks[]`, `elements[{id, projectId, signature}]` (the Line assignments) and `wallPending`. The wall map draws the physical layout from geometry that lives only in codex-nanoleaf (`layout.json`, the Prism material scripts). The style guide §10 keeps that imagery Nanoleaf's, and [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) leaves shared device art as an open question.

### Smallest useful implementation

Two phases.

1. **Schematic wall widget from the existing snapshot.** A widget in the [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) widget interface draws one cell per Line in a fixed 15-cell strip: fill from the project color, a status mark from the task's state, dimmed for free, hatched for a stale holder. A legend and counts (assigned, free, waiting for a Line) sit under the strip, matching the wall map's "Tasks" summary. Hover or focus on a cell names the Line, project and task label. Clicking the widget opens the wall component page; a secondary link opens the wall map at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through the numeric-loopback link rule the advanced editor already uses. The widget refreshes with the existing 5-second poll and shows the snapshot's freshness.
2. **Physical layout.** codex-nanoleaf exposes the wall's element geometry read-only on its integration route (an issue in that repository), the hub passes it through the integration snapshot, and the widget draws the real shape with the same cells. Until then the strip stays schematic and says so.

Dependencies: [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) for the widget interface. Phase 2 needs a codex-nanoleaf issue for geometry. Related independent work: [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) (device pages and shared art), [#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Read-only: the widget issues no controller command, reservation, assignment or read acknowledgment. Opening it changes nothing on the wall.
- Fixed-meaning status colors from the shared skin; project colors come from the snapshot, never guessed. A stale or unavailable snapshot shows as stale, not as an empty wall.
- Task labels are user-chosen labels or neutral IDs, as the snapshot already provides.
- The Nanoleaf controller remains the wall's only writer. [ADR 0007](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-bunny-shell.md) (2026-09-25) decided the shell question: the dashboard is the shell and the wall map is Nanoleaf's advanced editor until it retires; this widget is the first user of the shared device art in #355.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only.

- With the fake Nanoleaf controller fixtures, the widget shows the assigned Lines in project colors with correct status marks, free Lines dimmed, and counts matching the snapshot; a stale snapshot shows the stale state.
- Keyboard: cells are reachable and announced; axe passes at desktop and 390 px, where the strip wraps.
- Dashboard browser and matrix checks pass with the widget on the home grid.
- The owner approves the candidate before merge, renewed after changes.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Physical layout: phase 2, after the codex-nanoleaf geometry route exists (codex-nanoleaf#169), drawn through the shared device art of #355.
- Controls on the widget (assign, clear, locate): stay on the wall map and the component page; ADR 0007 routes them through the integration extension (codex-nanoleaf#170) before the shell offers them, and #271 still decides the group page.
- The Panels device: add a second strip when the Panels register as a controller ([codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113)).

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Read-only wall miniature on the dashboard home from the existing Nanoleaf integration snapshot; physical layout later.
**Highlight:** idea, A read-only wall miniature on the dashboard home.
**Extends:** H277

title: Inventory every UI component and rank what becomes a widget next
body:
> Investigate first. This issue produces a ranked widget list and follow-up stories; it authorizes no implementation.

### Outcome and real setup

One inventory of every UI component that exists across the B.U.N.N.Y. surfaces, with a decision for each: becomes a widget next, stays a page-level form, or stays where it is. The result is a ranked list on this issue and one story per widget group, so [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) builds the right widgets first.

Starting inventory from the 2026-09-25 planning pass:

| Surface | Component today | First read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard Activity | Stats strip (sessions, attention, components, collector) | Widget: four stat tiles |
| Dashboard Activity | Session card with facts, label form, notice acknowledgments | Widgets: compact session row; attention inbox across sessions |
| Dashboard Activity | Search and provider filter | Stays page-level |
| Dashboard component | Fact list (mode, pending, outcome, external control, observation age, snapshot age) | Widget: status strip per component |
| Dashboard component | Mode form with Reapply and switch block | Widget: mode card |
| Dashboard component | Power, Brightness | Widgets: one card each, or one combined |
| Dashboard component | Scenes, Media | Widgets: scene picker; media card |
| Dashboard component (Nanoleaf) | Integration settings, element, task and project mappings | Page-level assignments panel |
| Dashboard component (Pixoo) | Monitor view form | Page-level monitor panel |
| Dashboard Connections | Observed sources and feed facts | Widget: connections status tile |
| Wall map | Projects rail with reserved and in-use Lines | Widget candidate after the wall widget |
| Wall map | Wall canvas | Wall widget story [#286](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/286) |
| Wall map | Tasks list with status and Line | Widget: tasks by status |
| Wall map | Line inspector, task detail with project override | Stay on the wall map |
| Wall map | Mode toggles Work, Quiet, Free; status filter; Options menu; context card | Mode toggle joins the mode card; others stay |
| Pixoo advanced editor | Playlist editor | Stays; linked |
| Guide, atlas | Roadmap, timeline, system map | Stay documentation; velocity moves to [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283) |

External sources the owner asked about, each as a candidate widget with counts or state only, read-only credentials kept in the private configuration, and per-widget opt-in:

- Productivity: email unread count and oldest-unanswered age (Gmail API, counts only, no subjects stored), next calendar event countdown (Google Calendar), GitHub review requests and failing checks (`gh`, read-only), Jira sprint burndown (Atlassian API), a Work-mode timer tied to the mode card, weather (Open-Meteo, no key).
- Entertainment: now playing and minutes today (already from the Sony source), Sonos when [#233](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/233) lands, Plex or Jellyfin now playing, Twitch or YouTube live status for followed channels, Steam friends and now playing, sports scores, an RSS headline ticker.
- Machine and room: PC CPU, GPU and temperature (LibreHardwareMonitor's local JSON), network speed, hub memory against budget (from [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282)), Tidbyt and LIFX state once they reach the hub ([#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289)).

### Smallest useful implementation

- Walk the dashboard, the wall map and the Pixoo editor in the browser and complete the table above with the data each component needs, its commands, and its update cadence.
- Rank widgets by daily use and by data already available through the hub; mark those that need a new route, a new controller registration or an external credential.
- For each external source, record the API, its auth model, the read-only scope, what is stored (counts and states only) and the revisit trigger.
- Write one follow-up story per widget group in the feature form, and link them here.

Dependencies: none. Related: [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277), [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271), [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Read-only investigation: no code, installation or device change.
- Privacy: no widget proposal stores message bodies, subjects, prompts, transcripts or private paths; email and calendar widgets carry counts and times only. Credentials stay in the private configuration, never in Git.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: documentation and tracker only.

- The completed table and the ranked list are posted on this issue, and the follow-up stories exist with their dependencies linked.
- The style guide §11 glossary gains any new component names the ranking introduces.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Implementing any widget: its own story.
- External-source widgets: each needs its own credential decision by the owner before a story becomes ready.

**Coordination with the moments work (checked 2026-09-25):** the GitHub and calendar widgets listed above read the event sources [#293](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/293) and [#298](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/298) rather than adding their own integrations, and keep those sources' privacy rule (opaque IDs and times, no titles). Add to the inventory the dashboard controls the moments decision needs: the global flourish switch and quiet-hours schedule ([#291](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/291)), persona defaults and per-persona opt-out ([#294](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/294)), the interrupting-event list, and the moment-log widget ([#296](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/296)).

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Inventory every UI component across the dashboard, wall map and editors, rank what becomes a widget next, and list external sources.

title: Add a command palette and D-pad widget navigation with the N30 as B.U.N.N.Y. controller
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The owner drives the dashboard without touching the everyday mouse: a command palette opens with one shortcut and jumps to any component, mode, scene or page, and the widget grid is navigable with up, down, left and right. The 8BitDo N30 mouse becomes a dedicated B.U.N.N.Y. controller: its D-pad moves between widgets, a press enters one, another press backs out. The everyday mouse and its driver stay untouched. This runs on the Windows PC with the dashboard open in the browser.

What exists today: the dashboard has keyboard order, focus restoration and ArrowDown, Tab and Enter behavior inside forms, all covered by tests. The N30 emits PageUp, PageDown, Back and Forward from its D-pad, as the [N30 qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/desktop-input-qualification.md) recorded, and [#65](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/65) plans an app-scoped AutoHotkey mapper that binds those outputs to Codex actions while Codex is in the foreground. Nothing routes them to B.U.N.N.Y.

**Owner direction (2026-09-25):** the N30 is the dedicated widget controller for the hub. #65's Codex mapping is not withdrawn; the two coexist as foreground-scoped profiles, which is what [#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/70) already intends.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **Widget focus model in the dashboard.** Widgets form a roving-focus grid: one widget holds focus at a time, arrow keys and PageUp or PageDown move by grid position, Enter enters the widget and focuses its primary control, Escape returns to the widget level, Home and End jump. Inside a widget, the existing form keyboard behavior is unchanged. Focus is visible and announced. Hash routes from [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) let the palette and the grid deep-link.
2. **Command palette.** `Ctrl+K` opens a palette listing pages, components, modes per component, scenes, saved playlists and the Places links from [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278). Selecting a control action fills and focuses the matching widget's control; it does not apply it. Applying stays an explicit press, so the palette never sends a command by itself.
3. **N30 as controller.** The browser already receives PageUp and PageDown, so up and down work with no extra software once the dashboard maps them. Back and Forward arrive as browser history buttons, which Chromium may act on before the page can cancel; the first spike checks that. If the page cannot cancel them, the app-scoped mapper from #65 gains a second profile, active only while the B.U.N.N.Y. browser window is in the foreground, that turns Back and Forward into Left and Right and one chosen button into Enter and Escape. No mapping applies outside that window, and unassigned controls keep their normal behavior.

Dependencies: [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) for the widget grid. Part 3's mapper profile depends on #65's mapper existing; until then up and down work and left and right wait. Related: [#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/70) (profiles), [#66](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/66) (installed verification pattern).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- No input ever applies a device command by itself. The palette and the grid move focus and fill controls; a separate explicit press applies, as today.
- The everyday mouse, its driver and the keyboard A/B and Super Buttons stay outside B.U.N.N.Y., as [docs/desktop-controls.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/desktop-controls.md) records.
- Mapper rules from #65: foreground scope, no duplicate dispatch from held input, no replay of input received while the window was not in front, explicit enable and disable, and normal behavior on unassigned controls.
- Existing keyboard tests: Tab order, focus restoration after refresh and reconnect, ArrowDown inside forms, and reduced motion.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only for parts 1 and 2; part 3's mapper profile is installed only on explicit request with a named owner, following #66's pattern.

- Browser tests: arrow and PageUp or PageDown keys move focus across a fake widget grid in grid order and wrap at edges as decided; Enter and Escape enter and leave a widget; the palette opens, filters, and focuses the right control without sending a command (a command spy stays at zero).
- Spike result recorded here: whether Chromium lets the page cancel the Back and Forward buttons.
- If the mapper profile is built: injected-input tests for foreground scope, held input and disable, and a short trial on the PC with the N30, recorded as installed acceptance.
- axe passes at desktop and 390 px; the owner approves the candidate before merge.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Custom button mappings and saved profiles: [#70](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/70).
- Desk preset cycling from a button: [#68](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/68).
- A dedicated gamepad or keypad instead of the N30: revisit if the N30's four directions and two buttons prove too few.

## Guide

**Topic:** desktop-controls
**Note:** Command palette and a roving widget grid in the dashboard, with the N30 D-pad as a dedicated B.U.N.N.Y. controller beside its Codex profile.
**Highlight:** idea, A command palette and N30 D-pad widget navigation.
**Extends:** H277, H65

title: Connect Tidbyt and LIFX to the hub through one local controller host
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The Tidbyt and the LIFX bulbs appear in B.U.N.N.Y. like the wall and the Pixoo do: a component page, home widgets, history series, and `hub_devices` over MCP. Today the hub routes only controllers of kind `pixoo` and `nanoleaf`, each a separate HTTP service on loopback. Tidbyt (`controllers/tidbyt`) and LIFX (`controllers/lifx`) are in-process libraries with no listener, so no dashboard, widget, history or MCP path can reach them. The Tidbyt runner already consumes the shared feed on the installed hub; LIFX status is still open in [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20) and [#22](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/22). No backlog issue covers connecting either to the hub; [#232](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/232) only documents connecting controllers that already speak the contract, and [#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/56) does this for PC lighting later.

### Smallest useful implementation

- **One local controller host.** A small Node process in this repository, `apps/local-controllers` or similar, that loads the Tidbyt and LIFX libraries in-process and serves the existing controller v1 contract (`snapshot`, `commands`) for each on one loopback port with a bearer token, exactly as the Pixoo and Nanoleaf services do. It runs as one user service beside the hub and is the single writer for those devices. The Tidbyt runner's feed consumption moves into this host so there is one process, not two.
- **Two new kinds in the hub.** `ControllerConfig.kind` accepts `tidbyt` and `lifx`; the hub validates their capabilities from the snapshot (Tidbyt: power off is unsupported, status only; LIFX: power, brightness, color) and rejects unsupported commands with the owner's rejection, as the contract already requires. No integration route for either at first.
- **Registration.** `host.json` gains the two controller entries with their own `bunny-hub` principals, following the #154 and #155 pattern. The dashboard then shows both components with the generic controls, and [#277](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/277) widgets, [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282) series and MCP discovery follow without further work.

Read `docs/controller-contract.md` before touching wire values; this adds kinds and a service, not contract fields.

Dependencies: none for Tidbyt. LIFX control through the hub needs [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20)'s behavior decisions for automatic status, but manual power, brightness and color through the hub can land first. Related: [#232](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/232) (setup docs), [#56](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/56) (same pattern for PC lighting), [#23](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/23) (Tronbyt backend, unchanged by this).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer per device: the local host is the only Tidbyt and LIFX writer; the hub routes through it and never opens its state. The existing per-bulb queues, bounded retries and Tidbyt's classify-once results stay inside the libraries.
- Tidbyt credentials and bulb addresses stay in the host's private configuration, never in the hub's configuration or the browser.
- A manual change in the LIFX app is left alone until the next explicit command, as the LIFX README and #20 require. Nothing in this story adds automatic status painting.
- Contract rules: request tickets, configuration revisions, generations, typed outcomes, and unsupported capabilities reported rather than faked.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source first, then installation on explicit request with a named owner.

- Contract tests run against the local host with fake Tidbyt and LIFX transports: snapshot shape, supported and rejected commands, ticket and revision guards. `npm run test:contracts`, `test:contracts:python`, `test:tidbyt`, the LIFX suite, and the hub, MCP and dashboard suites pass with the two kinds registered in fixtures.
- With fakes, the dashboard shows a `tidbyt` and a `lifx` component with the right controls available and unavailable, and `hub_devices` lists both.
- Installation gate: the owner registers the host in `host.json`, and a bulb responds to a brightness change from the dashboard; Tidbyt shows the same status it shows today. Physical checks need the explicit device addresses and permission, as always.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Automatic LIFX agent status: [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20) and [#22](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/22).
- Tidbyt media or playlists: Tidbyt shows status only; nothing else is qualified.
- Integration routes (mappings, monitor settings) for these devices: add when a page needs more than the generic controls.
- Tronbyt: [#23](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/23) and [#24](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/24).

**Coordination with [#292](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/292) (checked 2026-09-25):** the host implements whichever controller contract version is current when it lands. If the moment command has shipped, the host declares the `moments` capability as unsupported for Tidbyt and LIFX until each has its own interlude story; v1 consumers stay unaffected either way.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`.

- **Complexity: medium.** A new loopback host, two hub kinds, a LIFX lighting profile route, MCP tools and dashboard controls. The per-device queues already exist in the Tidbyt and LIFX libraries.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Owner decision on 2026-09-25: LIFX color and temperature go through the hub now, over the existing `lifx-light` 1.0.0 profile on a typed route for `lifx` components. Controller v1 is unchanged. #292 agreed that this lands on API 1.0 first; #292 bumps the host's contract pin when it rebases.
- **Impact: medium.** A new authenticated listener takes device commands. Device effects are reversible. Tidbyt credentials and bulb addresses stay in private host configuration.
- **Readiness: ready.** Source delivery first. Installation and the physical check stay a separate, owner-authorized step.
- **Delivery choices.** The host reads the existing Tidbyt runner JSON as-is, so status, now-playing and the device lease carry over. The standalone runner stays available for rollback, and the shared lease prevents both from running. Each bulb gets a writer lease keyed by its address. The host never polls bulbs.

## Guide

**Topic:** nanoleaf-devices
**Note:** One local controller host serving the contract for the in-process Tidbyt and LIFX libraries, registered in the hub as two new kinds.
**Highlight:** idea, Tidbyt and LIFX reachable from the hub through one controller host.

title: Record the product direction and highest-leverage next work in the work guide
body:
Owner: Hub guide source (`docs/work-guide/`).

## Outcome and real setup

A reader of the cross-project work guide finds one dated **Direction** section beside the existing "Where we've been" and "Where we're going" panels. It answers, in the owner's words: where B.U.N.N.Y. stands on each surface, what it is becoming, what to build next and in what order, what to improve in what already exists, and which later ideas are worth keeping. Below the narrative, a computed **Least work, most unblocked** table ranks open stories by how many other open stories list them as a recorded prerequisite, so the owner can see which small items release the most work without re-deriving it each time.

Every intentional guide refresh re-validates the section. A story cited in the narrative that has since closed makes the maintenance check fail and name the story, so the direction text gets rewritten with the refresh rather than silently going stale, which is what happened to `docs/roadmap.md` before [#170](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/170) and to the "Useful next steps" list on 2026-09-25, when three of its four entries had merged that day. The leverage table is recomputed from the saved prerequisite records at every build and is never typed by hand.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories, the existing generator, snapshot inputs, checks and public edition. Excluded: live GitHub reads of the direction text (it stays dated), new story fields or labels, automatic refresh, publication, and any product behavior.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Saved input `work/guide_direction.py`**, the same pattern as `guide_paths.py`: `AS_OF` (date) and `REVISION` (the hub commit the text was written against); `STANDING`, one entry per surface (Nanoleaf Lines and Panels, Pixoo, Tidbyt, LIFX, PC lighting, playback, hub and dashboard, guide and atlas) with one or two sentences and the issue keys that evidence it; `BECOMING`, short paragraphs citing the direction placeholders [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267), [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271) and [#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272); `SEQUENCE`, an ordered list of (keys, why) for what to build next; `IMPROVEMENTS`, (text, keys) for changes to existing surfaces; `IDEAS`, later creative bets with keys; `DELIVERED_SINCE`, keys moved out of `SEQUENCE` at a refresh with the date, so the section can say what landed since the last direction rewrite. Text renders literally. Keys render through the existing `issue_link`, so they carry the same status icon and live GitHub relabel as every other link. First content: the 2026-09-25 assessment, pinned to hub `main` at `15c9c2a`.
- **Computed leverage** in `guide_status.py`: `leverage(issues, dependencies)` returns, for each open issue, the open issues whose native `blockedBy` records name it, direct and transitive, using the records `load_dependencies` already asserts complete. The renderer shows the top entries with at least one dependent: key, title, its existing scheduling state (candidate, active, blocked, deferred, later by owner), the direct and total counts, and the dependent keys. Stories in `DECISIONS` are marked "decision, no code". A `status:review` story is marked "in review" from its label; the PR snapshot is not parsed. The note states that counts come from recorded GitHub prerequisites only, that prose-only dependencies are not counted, and that a high count is not a priority.
- **Renderer** in `work/guide_direction.py`: one `<section id="direction">` inserted in `build_guide.py` after the timeline panels, with subsections "Where we stand", "What it is becoming", "Build next", "Least work, most unblocked", "Improve what exists" and "Later ideas". A dated line reads "Direction written <AS_OF> against hub <REVISION>; leverage computed from the <snapshot> prerequisite records." The section joins search, Expand all and print. It uses role tokens only, no decoration and no motion.
- **Refresh check** in `work/test_maintenance.py`: against the committed snapshot, every key in `STANDING`, `SEQUENCE`, `IMPROVEMENTS` and `IDEAS` must exist, and every `SEQUENCE` key must be open or listed in `DELIVERED_SINCE`; a violation fails naming the key. The same check covers `NEXT_STEPS` and `DECISIONS` in `guide_paths.py` until [#259](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/259) retires them.
- **Procedure**: `docs/work-guide/README.md` documents the section and its input, and step 1 of "Refresh and validate a guide revision" adds "review `work/guide_direction.py`; move delivered keys to `DELIVERED_SINCE` and rewrite the sequence". `docs/roadmap.md` gains one sentence pointing at the guide's Direction section as the dated narrative.

Dependencies: none required. Coordinate with #259, which moves curated per-story lists into story bodies: the direction narrative and the leverage table are guide structure and computed data, not story facts, so they stay in the repository. [#258](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258) may later fold this input check into its CI drift report. [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201) can reuse `leverage()` for the mission map.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- GitHub issues stay authoritative for scope and status. The narrative is dated editorial text and never claims live state; the table is derived only from saved native records; nothing in it promotes a blocked, deferred or owner-later story, and the existing conservative scheduling rules are reused unchanged.
- Topic totals, primary coverage, the archive, history, roadmap and diagram inputs are untouched. The new section adds nothing to issue counts.
- No tracker writes, no new endpoints, no new JavaScript reads. The public export includes the section; the input holds only public issue keys and owner prose.
- Two consecutive builds produce identical HTML. Hostile text in the input renders literally.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, one hub PR entirely under `docs/work-guide/` plus the one-sentence pointer in `docs/roadmap.md`. Guide UI needs no human approval under the SDLC UI approval scope.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: leverage counts from a fixture prerequisite graph (direct, transitive, a cycle, a deferred blocker and a decision entry); an unknown cited key fails the build naming it; a closed `SEQUENCE` key fails unless recorded in `DELIVERED_SINCE`; the check also catches a closed `NEXT_STEPS` key; hostile text is literal; identical repeated builds.
2. `check_guide.cjs`: the section renders at 390 px and 1440 px without overflow, appears in search results and Expand all, prints, and its issue links receive live status labels with the mocked read.
3. Guide commands pass under Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`), the regenerated HTML is committed, and screenshots plus the HTML hash go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`.
4. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the fixed candidate and a guarded squash merge under `docs/sdlc.md`, with the guide-only CI receipt if the filter applies. Publication of the public edition is a separate authorized step.
5. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling with no product behavior delta.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Reading the direction text live from an issue or discussion: not now. The text changes only when the owner rewrites it, and the refresh check already forces that review. Revisit with #259.
- Generating the narrative automatically at refresh: not chosen, to keep the owner's voice. The check makes a human rewrite the stale parts instead.
- Counting prose dependencies ("required input", "after #n") that are not recorded as native prerequisites: not now; record them natively in the tracker instead. Consequence: an unrecorded dependency is invisible to the table.
- A leverage view inside the mission map: later, with #201.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `15c9c2a`.

- **Complexity: low to medium.** One input module, one render function, one graph computation over records the build already loads, tests and a README step.
- **Uncertainty: low.** Native prerequisite records, the PR snapshot, `issue_link` and the timeline panels all exist; nothing new is fetched.
