title: Decide how hub moments and interludes work across devices
body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome

One decision record defines how events become coordinated device "moments". The principle is **the hub decides, devices guarantee**:
- Rules, events and agent personality live in the hub.
- Rendering, safety, precedence at execution and restore live in each device controller.

The owner agreed this direction on 2026-09-25, during jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#92's follow-up planning.

### Proposed ADR 0006 outline (number confirmed at filing)

**Context.**
- Hooks and the shared monitor already feed the hub.
- Controller contract v1 is a closed command set, so jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#92 added a Nanoleaf-only `animation.play` extension.
- ADR 0005 keeps content Free/Media-only and forbids automatic restore.
- #45 (rules), #40 (interruption), #267 (coordinated looks) and #139 (event history) each touch part of this.

**Decision (draft).**
1. **Hub owns policy:**
   - event sources and normalization with stable event IDs;
   - rules (#45);
   - agent personas and flourish budgets;
   - quiet hours, rate limits, a global "no flourishes" switch;
   - cross-device choreography;
   - an explainable moment log.
2. **Devices own mechanism:**
   - translating a semantic intent (mood, palette, duration) into device output;
   - one writer per device, bounds and validation;
   - final precedence at execution (alerts > interludes > ambient);
   - saving and restoring the *current* base presentation;
   - truthful receipts and external-control reporting;
   - continuing status presentation when the hub is down.
3. **Contract:**
   - A shared `moment` command in a new controller contract version: intent, mood, palette, duration, priority class, idempotency key from the triggering event, start time.
   - Each device declares the moods and limits it supports.
   - It comes with conformance fixtures for precedence, restore, expiry, replay and duplicate events.
4. **Interludes:**
   - A moment may briefly take over Work/Monitor presentation only as a time-boxed interlude.
   - The device returns to the current base, a red or yellow alert always pre-empts it, and it is skipped in Quiet or do-not-disturb.
   - This revises ADR 0005's "nothing restores automatically" for interludes only.
5. **Agents propose, the hub disposes:** agents call a propose tool, and never command devices directly for flourishes.
6. **No replay:** historical replay (#139) and restarts never re-trigger moments.

**Consequences.** Contract release and conformance work; one interlude story per device; hub-side moment log and persona storage.

### Open questions for the owner

- Which events may interrupt Work: PR merged, CI failed, meetings, or none by default?
- Quiet hours and the default flourish budget per agent.
- Whether choreography needs synchronized start times, or best-effort is enough.

### Related

- #45, #40, #267, #139, #246.
- jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#146 and #158.
- jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade playback.

### Owner decisions (2026-09-25)

1. **Interrupting events.**
   - Default set: PR merged, CI failed, and meeting reminders (the calendar source is #298).
   - The set is owner-editable: events can be added or removed later without a code change.
   - Everything else plays only in Free or Media until the owner adds it.
2. **Quiet hours.**
   - Build them with an on/off switch and an editable schedule, defaulting to **off**.
   - The owner often works late at night. Revisit the default when their schedule settles.
3. **Flourish budget.**
   - Start conservative, test for a few days, then expand. Testing must not block other delivery.
   - Proposed starting defaults, all editable:
     - per agent: at most 1 flourish per completed task and 2 per hour;
     - across all agents: at most 6 per hour;
     - at least 5 minutes between flourishes on any one device.
4. **Timing.**
   - Best-effort start times are enough for now.
   - Revisit trigger: visible drift between devices during choreography, which would open a sync-qualification story.

**Readiness:** ready to draft the ADR.

title: Release a controller contract version with a moment command and conformance cases
body:
> Filed on 2026-09-25 as a backlog placeholder at the owner's request. The owner started delivery with `deliver-work` on 2026-09-25 and approved the decisions below the same day.

### Outcome

Controllers receive coordinated moments through one shared, typed command instead of per-device extensions.

### Starting points

- Add a `moment` (or `interlude`) command and a `moments` capability declaring moods, limits and interlude support. The contents follow #291's decision.
- Extend the shared fixture inventory, which has 220 cases today, with moment cases:
  - precedence against alerts;
  - restore to the current base;
  - expiry;
  - a duplicate idempotency key;
  - a mode change mid-interlude;
  - hub-down behavior.
- Follow the contract's compatibility rules: a new version, with v1 consumers unaffected.

### Protections

- Typed commands only; no raw protocol or frames from the hub.
- Existing request tickets, generations and receipts.

### Accepted decisions (owner, 2026-09-25)

These settle the requirements in [ADR 0006](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0006-hub-moments-and-interludes.md) and the review comments below.

1. **Start time.** `start` is required and uses the device's own clock: `{domain:"controller-monotonic", epoch, atMs, toleranceMs}`, with `toleranceMs` at most 60,000. The hub computes `atMs` from the device snapshot's `sampleClock` plus its own elapsed time. The device drops the moment with `moment-missed` when the clock epoch differs, when it would start more than `toleranceMs` late, or when `atMs` is more than 60 s ahead.
2. **Moods.** Moods are open neutral IDs that each device declares. Every device with `moments` supported must include the core set `celebrate` (PR merged), `setback` (CI failed) and `reminder` (meeting). An undeclared mood gets `unsupported-capability`.
3. **Priority class.** The classes are `event` and `flourish`. A newer moment replaces the scheduled or playing one when its class is the same or higher, and the replaced moment ends as `superseded`. A flourish that arrives during an event is dropped with a receipt. Only `event` moments may set `coversStatus:true`.
4. **Evidence.** Receipts keep their transmission-only meaning. Admission-time drops use the new 1.1 failure codes `moment-duplicate`, `moment-missed` and `moment-blocked`. The 1.1 snapshot adds `state.moment`, which holds the current moment and the last one that ended, with its reason: `completed`, `preempted`, `superseded` or `interrupted`.
5. **Duration.** The contract allows `durationMs` from 1,000 to 300,000. Each device declares a `maxDurationMs` within that range; a longer moment gets `unsupported-capability`.
6. **Release.** The artifact becomes 1.1.0 and serves API 1.0 and 1.1. The in-repo workspace pins move to 1.1.0 with no behavior change. The Device MCP 1.0.0 archive keeps bundling the released contracts 1.0.0. After merge and green main CI, the coordinator publishes the GitHub release `controller-contracts-v1.1.0` with the archive, its SHA-256 and a receipt, as was done for 1.0.0.

Accepted assumptions:

- Negotiation is opt-in. A client reads the snapshot at its highest version, and the controller answers with the highest version it supports. The client sends moments only after it has read a 1.1 snapshot. A 1.1 controller still accepts 1.0 requests on the same ticket sequence, and a 1.0-only controller rejects a 1.1 request before admission.
- `palette` is optional: 1 to 8 `#rrggbb` colors, which the device may approximate.
- 1.1 capabilities list `moments` explicitly.
- The device-neutral terms are presentation `status`, `content` or `quiet`, and alert `attention` or `failure`. Device mappings are examples: Nanoleaf Work, Free and Quiet with yellow and red alerts; Pixoo Monitor and Media.
- The device remembers at least the last 64 moment IDs for each controller epoch.
- A moment that is blocked when it is due to start is dropped, not deferred.
- Any explicit command or mode change ends an interlude, which ends as `interrupted`.

### Acceptance and planned evidence

- The 1.1 schema accepts the `moment` command, the `moments` capability, the new failure codes and `state.moment`, and rejects out-of-range, missing-core-mood, flourish-covering-status and raw-protocol payloads. Evidence: schema cases run in TypeScript and Python.
- The pure moment reference decides each of the following, as semantic cases run in both languages:
  - alert pre-emption on status, and no pre-emption over content;
  - return to the *current* base;
  - duration expiry;
  - a missed start window and a different clock epoch;
  - a duplicate moment ID;
  - a newer moment superseding, and a flourish dropped during an event;
  - a mode change or an explicit command mid-interlude;
  - skipping in Quiet;
  - hub-down behavior: the device ends its interlude on its own clock, and a late delivery is dropped;
  - a restart that does not replay.
- 1.0 is unaffected. All 220 existing cases pass unchanged, and 1.0 `validate`/`admit` reject a 1.1 request as before. The hub, MCP, Tidbyt and LIFX checks pass on the 1.1.0 workspace pin, and `npm run test:package` passes for the 1.1.0 archive.
- `docs/controller-contract.md` documents 1.1, and an OpenSpec change updates `controller-contracts`.
- After merge: main CI is green and the `controller-contracts-v1.1.0` release is published and read back.

### Deferred

- Device adoption: Nanoleaf [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/158) and Pixoo [#92](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/92).
- The Tidbyt and LIFX hosts stay on API 1.0 until their own interlude stories.
- Hub-side sending belongs to #293-#298.
- Moving the Device MCP to the 1.1.0 contract waits for an MCP moment tool.

### Work assessment (delivery pickup, 2026-09-25, base `b15890b`)

- **Complexity: medium.** A 1.1 schema, a small moment state machine in two languages, fixtures, and version pins across four consumers. No concurrency or migration.
- **Uncertainty: low** now that the decisions above are settled.
- **Impact: medium.** A shared wire contract with future Nanoleaf and Pixoo adopters. It can be reverted, and it involves no devices, data or credentials.
- **Readiness:** ready. #291 closed on 2026-09-25.

## Guide

**Topic:** assistant-access
**Highlight:** idea, One typed moment command in a new contract version.
**Extends:** H291

title: Dashboard browser job flakes in the keyboard-submit brightness scenario
body:
## Outcome and real setup

The Depot job "Checks / Dashboard browser and contracts on ubuntu-latest" passes on the first attempt for a change that does not touch the dashboard. Today it fails intermittently in one Playwright scenario and passes on retry, which blocks routine merges until someone reruns it.

## Evidence

- `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, scenario "accepted brightness and power changes leave their forms ready for the next change without another action" in `apps/dashboard/tests/matrix.mjs`. At line 189 the test sets the fake to uncertain, fills Brightness with 25, focuses the slider, presses Tab and Enter, then waits for the form's status "Result unknown: this may have reached the device (uncertain-result). Check the device, then reload current values before trying again." The wait times out after 12 seconds; the page log shows the Pixoo view rendered normally up to that point.
- Failed then passed on retry on 2026-09-25, all with `depot-code-access` check runs:
  - `main` at `5cdc7fd`: failure started 18:07:53Z, success 18:11:51Z.
  - `main` at `e4135fb`: failure 07:35:29Z, success 07:39:08Z.
  - PR #302 (docs only, two markdown files) at `354ab50`: failure 19:08:51Z (check 108212800527, Depot attempt `mk01pwk080`), success on `depot ci retry` at 19:14:28Z (check 108214705294). The same job passed first time on the identical tree at `43053e5`.
- The attempt 1 log excerpt is kept outside Git in the owner's `.local/evidence/gh-242-resume/pr302-depot-dashboard-flake-mk01pwk080.log`.

## Smallest useful implementation

Reproduce locally by looping `npm run test:dashboard:browser` on the scenario, then find why the keyboard submit sometimes does not produce the uncertain status: whether Tab lands on a different control, whether Enter submits before the fake's uncertain mode applies, or whether the status renders and is replaced before the locator sees it. Fix the cause in the dashboard or make the test drive the same behavior deterministically without weakening what it asserts. No new tooling.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

The assertion set stays: an uncertain result locks the form, nothing retries within 5.5 seconds, focus lands on "Reload current values", and reload restores the controller's desired value. A possibly related pre-existing focus gap was seen during #245: after an uncertain Resume in a busy Media group, focus can fall to the page body. It is not filed and may or may not share a cause.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- The scenario passes 20 consecutive local runs and the Dashboard job passes first time on the delivery PR and on the merged `main` revision.
- If a dashboard behavior changes, the existing UI approval scope applies.

## Meaningful deferrals

- A general retry policy for flaky jobs: none. The merge rules keep requiring a green run; this issue removes the cause.

## Guide

**Topic:** development-workflow
**Note:** Intermittent Dashboard browser failure in the keyboard-submit brightness scenario; it also fails on `main` and passes on retry.

title: Carry observed model and thinking level in shared agent state and show it in B.U.N.N.Y.
body:
## Outcome and real setup

The lifecycle envelope rejects every property outside its schema, so the model and level a host already reports never reach the hub. Claude Code's hook input carries `effort.level` as a documented common field on every event, which is exactly the value agents cannot self-report reliably. Add an optional, allowlisted `settings` field so the shared owner keeps the last observed model and level per session, and the B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard shows it on the session card. Real setup: the installed standalone hub with its Claude Code and Codex hooks, one operator.

## Smallest useful implementation

- `packages/lifecycle-contracts`: add optional `settings: {model?: string, level?: string, source: 'hook' | 'statusline' | 'rollout' | 'user'}` to the envelope in `src/index.ts` and `schemas/lifecycle-v1.schema.json`, bounded like `label`, with fixtures and both contract test suites. Keep `apiVersion` `1.0`; the field is optional and ignored by older readers.
- `packages/agent-state/src/providers.ts`: `normalizeHook` copies Claude Code's `effort.level` into `settings.level` with `source: 'hook'`; no model, since hook input does not document one. Codex hook input is unknown until the investigation in #306 answers it; pass nothing for Codex.
- `packages/agent-state`: `Session.settings` keeps the last observed value with its observation time; snapshot 1.1 exposes it; the README's privacy section lists model and level as allowlisted metadata. Format version stays 2.0 with the field optional; startup from a store that lacks it needs no migration.
- `apps/hub`: pass the field through the snapshot the dashboard reads; `bin/monitor-hook.mjs` needs no change beyond the normalizer.
- `apps/dashboard`: a small model and level chip on each session card, `unknown` when absent, provenance in its title. This is application UI and needs human approval of the candidate.
- The existing `setLabel` operation is the join to deliveries: the delivery record convention in agent-skills#60 asks the coordinator to label its session with the issue key. No new API.

Dependencies: none for source. Installed capture needs the hub upgrade and hook re-qualification as a separate installation task with a named owner.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Hooks still fail open within their time budget. Missing settings never imply anything. Transcripts and rollout files are not read by this story. One owner, one writer, unchanged retirement, attention, read and freshness semantics. No raw session ids, paths or prompts in the field or the dashboard.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. Installed and physical acceptance are separate.

- [ ] Contract tests in TypeScript and Python accept the field with each `source`, reject an unknown source, an oversized value or a second unknown property, and still accept envelopes without it.
- [ ] Agent-state tests show a session keeping its last observed settings across turns, surviving restart from a store without the field, and exposing it in snapshot 1.1 only.
- [ ] A fake Claude Code hook payload with `effort.level` reaches the snapshot as `level: high, source: hook`; a payload without it leaves settings absent.
- [ ] The dashboard browser test shows the chip for a session with settings and `unknown` without.
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:contracts`, `npm run test:contracts:python`, `npm run test:package`, `npm run test:agent-state`, `npm run test:agent-state:python`, `npm run test:agent-state:package`, `npm run test:mcp`, the Dashboard checks, the workflow checks, independent reviews, PR and merged-main CI.
- [ ] Human approval of the dashboard chip candidate, renewed after any change to it.

OpenSpec: the agent-state-core spec gains the settings requirement; sync and archive on the delivery branch.

## Meaningful deferrals

A model id for Claude Code sessions, Codex model and reasoning, and any status-line emitter wait for #306's answer. Usage or cost fields are excluded; no host exposes them to hooks. No history of settings changes within a session, only the last observed value.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `f94e1f4`. Complexity medium: contract, normalizer, reducer, snapshot, dashboard. Uncertainty medium: `effort.level` on every event is documented but unobserved on the installed Claude Code version. Impact medium: additive contract and agent-state change with no ownership change. Ready.

## Guide

**Topic:** shared-codex
**Note:** Carry the host-observed model and thinking level per session so the dashboard and delivery records stop guessing.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model | Sonnet (`sonnet`) | Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) |
| Thinking level | `high` | `medium` |
| Session type | One-shot | One-shot |
| Subagents | None | None |
| Reviewers | Two fresh read-only Sonnet (`sonnet`) reviewers, one for Standards and one for Specification | Two fresh read-only Luna (`gpt-6-luna`) reviewers at `high`, one for Standards and one for Specification |
| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |
| Checkpoints | the schema shape before the contract change, and the dashboard chip candidate before review | the schema shape before the contract change, and the dashboard chip candidate before review |

**Prompt (Claude Code):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/305. I started this session on Sonnet at high effort. State the model you are running and stop if it is not Sonnet; take the effort as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only Sonnet reviewers for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: the schema shape before the contract change, and the dashboard chip candidate before review. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Prompt (Codex):**

```text
Use the deliver-work skill to deliver https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/305. I started this session on gpt-6-sol at medium reasoning. State the model you are running and stop if it is not gpt-6-sol; take the reasoning level as stated rather than guessing it. Run as a one-shot session: implement it yourself without worker subagents, and use two fresh read-only gpt-6-luna reviewers at high reasoning for deliver-work's required Standards and Specification reviews. Stop to ask me at these checkpoints: the schema shape before the contract change, and the dashboard chip candidate before review. The issue's Execution recommendation (assessed 2026-09-25) is the basis; if what you find no longer fits it, say so before changing strategy. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.
```

**Cheaper start:** none recorded; the contract and agent-state suites are the reliable check, but the schema and reducer decisions should not be split from the dashboard change.

**Why:** Several interfaces in one bounded outcome: contract schema, normalizer, reducer, snapshot and a dashboard chip, all additive, with existing fake-tested suites. Policy row: several interfaces or meaningful design judgment within a bounded outcome.
**Reassess when:** #306 reports a Codex or model-id source that changes the settings shape, or the contract change turns out to need a new API version.
**Assessed:** 2026-09-25 · policy `agent-skills@3746fab` · evidence: story text and dependencies read at filing on 2026-09-25; ratings as recorded in the story · fingerprint: `ce415b5f3edc`

title: Investigate host-observed model sources for Codex and the Claude Code model id
body:
## Outcome and real setup

#305 captures Claude Code's thinking level from the hook's documented `effort.level` field. Two sources remain unqualified: the Codex hook input, whose documented fields do not mention model or reasoning, and a Claude Code model id, which the hook input does not document but the status line JSON does (`model.id`, `model.display_name`, `effort.level`). Codex rollout files record `model` and `effort` in every `turn_context` line and `cli_version` in `session_meta`, but the hub deliberately refuses to open rollout files (`apps/hub/src/codex-desktop.ts`, `docs/provider-qualification.md`). Answer, read-only, which host records can supply model and level for each provider without reading conversation content, and which of them the owner is willing to have the hub read. Real setup: the installed Codex CLI and Desktop and Claude Code on this host.

## Smallest useful implementation

None; this is an investigation. Question: for Codex CLI and Desktop and for Claude Code, which host-provided record gives the session's model and level, at what event, with what stability guarantee, and what does capturing it require: a hook field, a status-line emitter installed separately, or a bounded read of `turn_context` metadata lines from the rollout file?

Evidence to return:

- The documented Codex hook input fields at the current reference, with model and effort presence per event.
- The documented Claude Code status line input and the installation it needs, kept separate from the hub's hook installation.
- Whether reading only `session_meta` and `turn_context` lines from a rollout is compatible with the hub's transcript rule, and what bound it would need.
- A recommendation per provider and the decision the owner must make before #305's deferrals are picked up.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Read-only. No hook, setting or installation change. No transcript or prompt content quoted; field names only.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: a report on this issue, then reassessment of #305.

- [ ] Each provider has an answer with its source, event and stability, or an explicit "not exposed".
- [ ] The rollout-read question has a recommendation the owner can accept or reject.

## Meaningful deferrals

Implementing any source is a reassessment of #305 or a new story.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `f94e1f4`. Complexity low, uncertainty high, impact low. Ready as an investigation.

## Guide

**Topic:** shared-codex
**Note:** Find which host records can supply model and level for Codex and Claude Code without reading conversation content.

title: Read delivery execution records into the guide and show deliveries by model
body:
## Outcome and real setup

The guide's history chart shows one mark per merged PR with title and time only. After agent-skills#60 defines the `## Execution record` PR section, PR bodies carry the actual model, level and review effort per delivery with provenance. Read that into the saved history so the guide shows, per delivery, model, level and review effort, and per story the recommended-versus-actual drift, without anyone re-reading PR bodies. The owner uses this on the guide page; the comparison itself stays with agent-skills#44. Real setup: the maintainer's dated `gh api` history refresh and guide rebuild.

## Smallest useful implementation

- `docs/work-guide/work/execution_record.py`: a strict parser on `story_sections.py`, like `recommendations.py`, pinned to the agent-skills revision that merges agent-skills#60. A section that breaks the convention renders "record unavailable"; a PR without one renders "no record".
- The history refresh keeps the parsed record for each merged PR in `work/history/github-history.json`, not the PR body. Fix attribution comes only from the record's `Fixes delivery` line.
- `timeline.py`: each PR mark's tooltip adds model, level, provenance and review rounds when recorded.
- A "Deliveries by model" table in the timeline section: for each coordinator model and level, count of deliveries, median lines changed, review rounds, corrections and attributed post-merge fixes, with unknown shown as unknown and the record count as the denominator.
- Each task brief's Start with block adds one line: the last delivery for that story and whether it matched the recommendation.
- `docs/sdlc.md`: require the Execution record section in delivery PRs and the `Fixes delivery` line on repairs, pointing at the catalog reference rather than copying it.
- Tests in `test_maintenance.py` for the parser and the table; `check_guide.cjs` coverage for the tooltip and the table.

Dependencies: agent-skills#60 merged and its revision known; #304 merged so the recommended side is current.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

History remains a dated snapshot read with `gh api`; nothing is fetched live in the browser for records. No prompts, transcripts, private paths or raw session ids enter the snapshot. Existing chart marks, milestones and roadmap are unchanged. The table ranks nothing and states its denominators.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. The docs/sdlc.md change is outside docs/work-guide, so the guide-only CI filter exception does not apply; the full applicable CI runs.

- [ ] Parser tests cover a complete record, an unknown-heavy record, a broken record and a PR without one.
- [ ] After a history refresh, the deliveries recorded since agent-skills#60 show model and level in their tooltips and appear in the table with correct counts.
- [ ] A story with a recorded delivery shows the drift line in its brief; a story without one shows nothing.
- [ ] `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`, independent reviews, PR and merged-main CI.

No human UI approval: the change is guide UI. No OpenSpec change.

## Meaningful deferrals

Backfilling records for the existing merged PRs is excluded; their models are mostly unknown and the table says so. Cost or usage columns wait for a host that exposes them. The hub-to-PR join is story #305's session label plus this record's Session label row, not a new service.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `f94e1f4`. Complexity medium: parser, refresh, three widgets and a docs rule. Uncertainty low to medium: the shape is fixed by agent-skills#60; the table's value depends on how many records exist. Impact low: guide presentation and a documentation rule. Blocked until agent-skills#60 and #304 merge.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide
**Note:** Show each delivery's actual model, level and review effort beside the story's recommendation.

## Execution recommendation

**Start with:** One-shot: one session implements it directly after agent-skills#60 and #304 merge. Claude Code on Sonnet (`sonnet`) at `high` effort, or Codex on Sol (`gpt-6-sol`) at `medium` reasoning. Paste that host's prompt below.

| Availability | Provisional: aliases verified from this host's Agent tool on 2026-09-25; the agent cannot observe its effort level | Provisional: not inspected from Claude Code (2026-09-25); confirm the model and reasoning options in Codex first |

title: Show recommended creative and expansion stories in a guide Ideas section
body:
Owner: Hub guide source (`docs/work-guide/`).

## Outcome and real setup

A reader of the cross-project work guide finds one **Ideas** section beside the Timeline and Direction sections. It lists every open story that its owners have marked as a creative or expansion idea: a new capability, a generalization across devices or repositories, or a user-visible win that recent work made cheap. Each entry shows the story with its live status relabel, the one-line observation that prompted it, the stories it would build on, and its existing scheduling state (candidate, blocked, deferred). Entries are grouped by the topic each story already lives in, so a reader sees where the idea lands without leaving the guide's vocabulary.

The mark lives in the story, not in a curated file. A story says `**Highlight:** idea, <what prompted it>` in its `## Guide` section and may add `**Extends:** <story keys>`. The Direction section's "Later ideas" list is derived from those marks instead of the hand-written `IDEAS` list in `work/guide_direction.py`, following the same move [#259](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/259) made for topics and highlights. Today the expansion stories filed on 2026-09-25 ([#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267), [#271](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/271), [#272](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/272), [#292](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/292) to [#298](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/298), the Nanoleaf animation family and Pixoo #91 to #94) sit in their device topics with nothing that distinguishes a placeholder idea from a defect fix in the same table.

Setup: one maintainer, the three source repositories, the existing generator, snapshot inputs, checks and public edition. Excluded: a new GitHub label, tracker automation, changes to any session closeout prompt, ranking ideas by value, publication, and any product behavior.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **Grammar** in `work/guide_section.py`: a fourth `Highlight` kind, `idea`, with the same `<kind>, <reason>` shape; an optional `**Extends:** <keys>` line, valid only beside an `idea` highlight, whose keys use the guide's `H<n>`, `N<n>`, `P<n>` form and must exist in the snapshot. An `Extends` without `idea`, an unknown key, or a malformed line makes the section unreadable and fails the snapshot build naming the story, exactly like the existing rules. `work/story_sections.py` stays the shared engine. The three repositories' feature issue templates name `idea` and `Extends` in the Guide placement description (companion PRs in codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade, as #259 did).
- **Section** in `work/guide_ideas.py`, inserted by `build_guide.py` after Direction as `<details class="reference ideas" id="ideas">` with a sidebar entry "I · Ideas" whose count is the number of marked open stories. Entries group by topic in `guide_paths.TOPICS` order and, within a topic, by story key. Each entry renders the story through `issue_link`, the reason literally, the `Extends` keys through `issue_link`, and the scheduling state from the existing `guide_status.scheduling_state`. A note states that ideas are counted in their topics, not here, and that the mark is a placement, not a priority. The section joins search, Expand all and print, uses role tokens only, and has no decoration or motion.
- **Direction** in `work/guide_direction.py`: remove the curated `IDEAS` list; the "Later ideas" subsection renders the marked stories in compact form and links to the Ideas section. The existing `check()` also fails, naming the key, when a story in `SEQUENCE` carries an `idea` highlight, because "build next" and "later idea" are exclusive.
- **Live path** in `work/guide_overview.js`: the same grammar re-parses each successfully read repository's open bodies. A story newly marked or moved in since the snapshot lands in a "Newly added since the snapshot" block inside its topic group of the Ideas section; a story that closes live or loses its mark is removed; existing rows patch their reason and `Extends` in place. A repository whose read fails keeps the snapshot's rows. The freshness line names the Ideas section among the live parts.
- **Migration**, at an owner checkpoint: the delivery session reads the live tracker, proposes the exact list of stories to mark with a one-line reason drawn from each story's own text and its `Extends` keys from stated parents (for example #267 extends [#67](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67); #271 and #272 extend codex-nanoleaf#47; Nanoleaf #158 and Pixoo #92 extend #292), and stops for approval before writing. Candidates: the seven keys the current curated `IDEAS` list cites, the 2026-09-25 placeholders, [#282](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/282), [#283](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/283), [#286](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/286) to [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289), the Nanoleaf animation stories and Pixoo #91 to #94. Writes go through the existing section render helper with a dry run first and receipts outside Git, the way #259 migrated topics.
- **Procedure**: `docs/work-guide/README.md` documents the `idea` kind, `Extends`, the Ideas section and the derived Later ideas; the Direction paragraph drops `IDEAS` from the saved-input list.

Dependencies: none required. [#290](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/290) (Direction) and #259 (guide sections) are delivered and are the seams this builds on. [#278](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/278) edits the same sidebar; whichever lands second rebases. [#258](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/258) may later report an idea story that closed without its mark being reviewed.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- GitHub issues stay authoritative for scope and status. `idea` is a placement mark, not a status, a label or a priority. It never promotes a blocked, deferred or owner-later story, and the conservative scheduling rules are reused unchanged.
- Topic totals, exact-cover of topics, primary coverage, the archive, history, roadmap and diagram inputs are untouched. The Ideas section adds nothing to issue counts; the sidebar count is informational.
- No new labels, no tracker automation, no new endpoints. Migration writes are one-off, owner-approved edits to public issue bodies with receipts outside Git.
- Two consecutive builds produce identical HTML. Hostile text in a reason or `Extends` renders literally. The public export includes the section and holds only public keys and one-line prose.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only. One hub PR under `docs/work-guide/` plus the hub feature template under `.github/`, so full CI applies and the guide-only exception does not; two companion template PRs in codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade. Guide UI needs no human approval under the SDLC UI approval scope.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: an `idea` highlight parses and renders; `Extends` without `idea`, an unknown `Extends` key and a malformed line each fail naming the story; a `SEQUENCE` key marked `idea` fails the direction check naming it; entries group in topic order; the Direction's Later ideas equal the marked set; hostile text is literal; repeated builds are identical.
2. `check_guide.cjs`: the section renders at 390 px and 1440 px without overflow, appears in search, Expand all and print, its links receive live status labels, and with the mocked live read a newly marked story appears in the Newly added block while a closed one is removed.
3. Guide commands pass under Node 24 (`fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --`), the regenerated HTML is committed, and screenshots plus the HTML hash go to the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`.
4. Migration: the dry-run diff is reviewed and approved at the checkpoint, every write reads back equal to the rendered section, a rerun reports no change, and receipts are kept outside Git.
5. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of the fixed candidate, all applicable CI jobs green on the hub PR and on the merged revision, and green companion PRs. Publication of the public edition is a separate authorized step.
6. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling with no product behavior delta.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Ranking ideas by leverage, owner order or value: not now. Topic order and key order are enough for the current count; revisit when the section passes about forty entries.
- Filing ideas automatically from session closeouts: belongs to the closeout prompt, which is being revised separately; once it files placeholders with `Highlight: idea`, they appear here without a guide edit.
- An idea lifecycle or promotion state: not chosen. Promoting an idea means editing its story's highlight or adding it to the Direction sequence, and the new check keeps the two exclusive.
- Keeping a hand-written Later ideas list beside the derived one: rejected by the owner on 2026-09-25; derived only.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`.

- **Complexity: low to medium.** One grammar extension in an existing parser, one render module, one derived list replacing a curated one, live-path handling that mirrors the existing topic logic, tests, templates and a one-off migration.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The section engine, `issue_link`, scheduling state, the Direction check and the #259 migration pattern all exist; the owner has already settled derivation, migration approval and the `Extends` field.
- **Impact: low.** Documentation output and public issue-body edits; a fault fails the build loudly, and migration writes are reviewed before they happen.
- **Readiness: ready.** No open prerequisite.

## Guide

**Topic:** work-guide

title: Delete merged delivery branches on merge and prune the ones left behind
body:
Owner: repository settings (owner action) and `docs/sdlc.md`.

## Outcome and real setup

Merged delivery branches disappear on merge instead of accumulating. On 2026-09-25 the hub had 123 of 127 remote branches whose PR was already merged, codex-nanoleaf 55 of 56 and divoom-app-upgrade 36 of 37. Every session closeout reports "the merged branch remains; policy says I may not delete it", and nobody acts, because the SDLC cleanup step reserves branch deletion for the owner.

Setup: the three source repositories on GitHub, squash merges guarded by `--match-head-commit`. Excluded: the public `agent-device-guide` repository's `publish/*` branches (they are the publication record), and any change to worktree cleanup.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Enable "Automatically delete head branches" on agent-device-hub, codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade (owner action or `gh api -X PATCH repos/<r> -f delete_branch_on_merge=true`).
- One-off prune: list remote branches whose PR is merged and whose head is the merged PR's head, show the list for approval, then delete them. Keep any branch with an open PR, an unmerged commit, or a registered worktree.
- `docs/sdlc.md` cleanup step 4: replace "Do not delete the delivery branch yourself" with "GitHub deletes the head branch on merge; if it did not, report it". Drop the branch line from the session closeout checklist.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Squash merge, head guard, review gates and worktree rules are unchanged. Deleting a merged branch loses nothing: the squash commit is on `main` and the PR keeps the history.
- Branches with unmerged commits, open PRs or registered worktrees are never touched by the prune.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: repository settings plus one docs-only hub PR.

1. The setting reads back `true` on all three repositories.
2. The prune list was approved before deletion; the receipt (branch, merged PR, head SHA) is kept outside Git; a rerun finds nothing to prune.
3. The next merged PR in each repository leaves no head branch behind.
4. `docs/sdlc.md` step 4 updated; workflow checks pass.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Pruning `publish/*` branches in the public repository: not now; they are the publication record.
- A scheduled prune: unnecessary once the setting is on.

title: Produce a daily cross-session closeout digest
body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 at the owner's request and rewritten the same day for clarity. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### The problem

On 2026-09-25, 21 agent sessions each ended with their own archive sweep. Each sweep proposed follow-ups from what that one session saw. No session could see another's list, so the same Linux upgrade command was proposed three times, the same Pillow note twice, and two sessions filed overlapping stories (#282 and #283 beside #293 and #296) that a third session then had to reconcile by hand. The per-session closeout (agent-skills #61) fixes what one session loses; it cannot fix what only shows up across sessions.

This is separate from refreshing the guide. #315 refreshes the guide's data nightly by machine. This item reads what the day's sessions *decided and proposed* and consolidates it for the owner.

### Outcome and real setup

Once a day, one report covers every issue closed, opened or commented on and every PR merged across the three repositories in the last day, and answers: which follow-ups were proposed by more than one session; which newly filed stories overlap each other or an older story; which closing comments name a deployment gap or a learning that has no issue; and which placeholders filed that day still lack a topic or recommendation. The owner reads one page instead of 21 closeout tails.

### Smallest useful implementation

To be defined. Starting points:

- Reads only: issues and PRs updated in the window, their closing comments, and the closeout comments that agent-skills #61 will post.
- Output: one Markdown report posted as a comment on the day's nightly refresh PR (#315) when one exists, otherwise on a fixed tracking issue, listing duplicates with the sessions that raised them, overlaps with the stories they touch, and untracked gaps with the comment that named them.
- Attributes each proposal to the `**Session:**` label of the closeout record it came from (agent-skills#61, using agent-device-hub#305's label convention); comments without a record are grouped as unattributed rather than guessed.
- Files nothing itself. The owner approves items, and filing follows the closeout skill's rules.
- Host: a Claude scheduled routine or a Codex equivalent, because the dedupe and overlap judgment is what an agent is for; GitHub Actions stays the host for the mechanical refresh.

### Open questions

- Whether the digest replaces the per-session filing of P1 and P2 items or only catches what per-session filing misses.
- Whether overlap detection needs anything beyond shared issue links, labels and topic ids.

## Guide

title: Refresh the work guide nightly into one rolling pull request
body:
Owner: Hub `.github/workflows/` and guide source (`docs/work-guide/`).

## Outcome and real setup

Every night a scheduled workflow refreshes the work guide's saved GitHub data, rebuilds the guide, runs its checks, and, when the committed output changed, opens or updates one rolling pull request with a plain report of what moved: stories opened, closed or relabelled, topic counts, recommendation labels that went stale, and whether the Direction narrative still fits. Today every one of those steps is manual: an "intentional guide revision" happens only when a session decides to run `refresh_backlogs.py`, hand-edits `work/history/github-history.json`, rebuilds and opens a PR. On 2026-09-25 the published guide's "Useful next steps" named three stories that had merged that day, and #290 and today's merges were absent until the next hand refresh.

The nightly PR is the starting point for the human step, not a replacement for it. The Direction narrative in `work/guide_direction.py` stays owner-written: when a cited story closed, the refresh check fails as #290 designed, the PR says so, and the owner rewrites the text before it can merge. Nothing merges or publishes on its own; that is [#317](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/317) gated by #240.

Setup: the hub repository on GitHub Actions with its `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the three public source repositories, the existing generator and checks. Excluded: merging, publishing the public edition, editing issues, re-rendering diagrams, and any change to the guide-only CI exception.

## Smallest useful implementation

- **History generator** `work/refresh_history.py`: builds `work/history/github-history.json` from paginated read-only queries (merged PRs and closed issues per repository) in a deterministic order, replacing the hand edit that #259 deferred. First run must reproduce the current hand-maintained file or document each difference in the PR.
- **Report** `work/refresh_report.py`: diffs the previous and new snapshots and prints Markdown: per repository, opened, closed, retitled and relabelled stories; topic count changes; recommendation states that changed (recommended, stale, insufficient, not yet assessed); the Direction check result naming any closed cited key; the retired-term warnings if that check exists. The same text becomes the PR body and the job summary.
- **Workflow** `.github/workflows/guide-refresh.yml`: `schedule` (one nightly cron, owner picks the hour) plus `workflow_dispatch`; permissions `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` only; steps reuse `work-guide.yml`'s Python, Node and pinned Playwright setup, then `refresh_backlogs.py`, `refresh_history.py`, `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py`, `check_guide.cjs`. If `git diff --quiet -- docs/work-guide` passes, write "no change" to the summary and stop. Otherwise commit to the fixed branch `guide/nightly-refresh` (the workflow owns that branch and may reset it), then create the PR "Nightly guide refresh" if none is open or update its body, labelled with the existing `documentation` label. A refresh helper that fails midway fails the job before any commit, so a partial snapshot never reaches the branch.
- **Direction failure path**: when `test_maintenance.py` fails only on the Direction check, the job still pushes the branch and opens the PR, marks the report "needs owner rewrite of guide_direction.py", and the failed check stays red on the PR.
- **Procedure**: `docs/work-guide/README.md` gains a "Nightly refresh" paragraph and step 1 of "Refresh and validate a guide revision" starts from the rolling PR; `docs/development.md` lists the workflow beside `work-guide.yml`.

Dependencies: none required. Preferred order before #313 (installed revisions) and #308 (Ideas section), which add inputs the nightly report should cover once they exist; shared-file coordination with #278 on the README.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- No merge, no publication, no issue writes, no diagram render. The workflow touches only `guide/nightly-refresh` and its one PR.
- The Direction narrative is never generated; the check that forces a human rewrite is preserved unchanged.
- Snapshot dates stay honest: the report and the guide's freshness line carry the refresh time, and a failed repository read keeps the previous snapshot for that repository as the live path already does.
- Token scope is the minimum above; no personal token or secret is added. Reads are GET and GraphQL queries only.
- The rolling PR stays entirely under `docs/work-guide/`, so today's guide-only CI handling applies to it unchanged until #240 decides otherwise.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, one hub PR. Full CI applies because `.github/workflows/` and `docs/development.md` are outside the guide filter.

1. Unit tests in `test_maintenance.py` or a sibling: `refresh_history.py` reproduces the committed history file from recorded fixture responses; `refresh_report.py` produces the expected Markdown for a fixture pair with an opened story, a closed story, a relabel, a topic count change, a stale recommendation and a closed Direction key.
2. A `workflow_dispatch` run on the delivery branch: with a changed snapshot it opens the rolling PR with the report; a second run with no change writes "no change" and opens nothing; a run with a closed cited Direction key opens the PR with the failed check visible. Run logs and PR links recorded on the issue.
3. `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` exit zero; the guide commands pass under Node 24; a rebuild shows no drift.
4. Independent Standards and Specification reviews; all applicable CI jobs green on the PR head and on the merged revision.
5. No OpenSpec change: documentation tooling only.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Merging and publishing the nightly PR automatically: the follow-on story, blocked by #240's decision on review and check requirements for mechanical guide-only refreshes.
- A Claude or Codex scheduled routine instead of GitHub Actions: rejected for the mechanical refresh, which needs no judgment; a routine remains the candidate host for the closeout digest (#314), which does.
- A timer on the WSL host: rejected because the host is not always up (codex-nanoleaf #133) and the refresh needs the pinned browser toolchain that CI already has.
- Rewriting the Direction text automatically: rejected, as #290 decided, to keep the owner's voice.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`.

- **Complexity: medium.** A new workflow, a history generator replacing a hand-maintained file, a snapshot diff report, and a branch-and-PR update path with a failure branch.
- **Uncertainty: low to medium.** Whether `GITHUB_TOKEN` can run the existing `blockedBy` GraphQL query across the two other public repositories is a bounded question answered at the first dispatch; history parity is checked by the first run's diff.
- **Impact: medium.** The workflow writes a branch and a PR in the hub; nothing merges. A faulty report misleads the human step but cannot change the published guide.
- **Readiness: ready.** No open prerequisite.

## Guide

title: Warn at guide refresh when an open story names a retired term
body:
Owner: Hub guide source (`docs/work-guide/`).

## Outcome and real setup

A guide refresh warns, naming the story, when an open story's text still describes something the project retired: a removed UI control, a decommissioned runtime, a renamed surface. Two independent reviews missed that #254 still tests the Pause motion control #264 removed, and Nanoleaf #17, #19 and #20 still describe the Windows runtime #131 retired; a session closeout found both. #311 clears the current instances; this keeps new ones from hiding.

Setup: the guide's snapshot build and maintenance check, which already read every open story body. Excluded: editing stories, scanning closed stories, scanning repository docs (#258 owns documentation drift), and any fuzzy matching.

## Smallest useful implementation

- Saved input `work/guide_retired.py`: a list of `(term, retired_by_key, date, note)` entries, exact case-insensitive phrases, starting with `Pause motion` (H264), `tray.ps1`, `install-modes.ps1` and `PowerShell` (N131). The owner adds entries when a delivery retires something, in the same PR.
- `build_guide.py` or `test_maintenance.py`: for each open story in the snapshot, report every matching term as a warning line "story cites retired term <term> (retired by <key>)". A match inside the story's own `## Guide` note is an error, because the guide renders that text. A term whose `retired_by_key` is not in the snapshot fails the check naming the entry, matching the Direction input's rule.
- The nightly refresh report (#315) includes the warning lines when it exists; until then they appear in the build output and the job summary.
- One paragraph in `docs/work-guide/README.md` under Guide sections.

Dependencies: none required. Preferred order after #311, so the first run starts clean.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- Warnings never fail the snapshot build; only a retired term inside guide-rendered text or a dangling `retired_by_key` fails.
- No story is edited; the check reads the saved snapshot only.
- Two consecutive builds produce identical output; hostile text in a note renders literally.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source-only, one hub PR under `docs/work-guide/`.

1. `test_maintenance.py`: a fixture story matching a term produces the warning naming story and key; a term in a fixture `## Guide` note fails; a dangling `retired_by_key` fails naming the entry; a story without matches is silent; repeated builds identical.
2. Against the committed snapshot after #311, the check reports zero warnings, or each remaining warning is listed on this issue with its owner.
3. Guide commands pass under Node 24; regenerated output committed with no drift.
4. Independent Standards and Specification reviews; guide-only CI exception evidence if the filter applies.

## Meaningful deferrals

- Deriving retired terms automatically from merged PRs: not now; the list is short and the owner knows what was retired.
- Scanning repository documentation for the same terms: #258's documented-paths check covers moved files; a retired-term scan of docs can join it when one is needed.

title: Merge and publish the nightly guide refresh automatically
body:
Owner: Hub `.github/workflows/`, `docs/sdlc.md` and the guide publication procedure.

## Outcome and real setup

When the nightly guide refresh PR from #315 passes its checks and the Direction check, it merges on its own with the head guard, and the public edition at agent-device-guide is republished from that merged revision and verified live, so the published guide is never more than a day behind GitHub without anyone running the procedure. Today both steps are manual and the SDLC requires two independent reviews and an explicit publication request for every guide revision.

Setup: the hub and public repositories, the existing publish procedure and live hash check. Excluded: the Direction narrative, which stays owner-written and blocks the merge when stale; any guide revision that is not the mechanical nightly refresh.

## Smallest useful implementation

To be settled after #240, which decides what GitHub can enforce and how guide-only revisions are validated. Starting points:

- A merge step in the nightly workflow that merges the rolling PR with `--match-head-commit` when its own checks and the Direction check passed and no human commit is on the branch, with an explicit `--body` so nothing auto-closes.
- A publish job that runs the existing export, opens the public PR, merges it under the same guard, and performs the live hash verification the procedure already defines, posting the receipt on the hub PR.
- An SDLC sentence defining the mechanical nightly refresh as a class of guide revision whose review requirement is the workflow's checks rather than two agent reviews, if #240 decides so.

## Open decisions (owner, in #240 or here)

- Whether a mechanical refresh may merge without the two independent reviews, and what evidence replaces them.
- Whether publication follows every merged refresh or a daily window.
- What stops the automation: a failed live check, a Direction failure, a human commit on the branch.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

- The head guard, explicit merge body, live verification and rollback (revert the public PR) stay as the procedure defines them.
- Any revision touching files outside `docs/work-guide/` is never merged by this path.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

To be defined with the decisions above. At minimum: a dispatched run that merges and publishes a real refresh with the receipt posted, a run that stops on a Direction failure, and a run that stops on a human commit.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`. Complexity medium. Uncertainty high until #240 settles the review and check requirements. Impact medium to high: an unattended merge and publish path; the guards above bound it. Readiness blocked by #240 and #315.

title: Add the LIFX Beam to the LIFX controller and B.U.N.N.Y.
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The owner's LIFX Beam appears in B.U.N.N.Y. next to the LIFX bulbs, with power, brightness, color and temperature controls, and in `hub_devices` over MCP. Setup: one operator, the installed hub, and the Beam at an IP the owner supplies, owned by the same local controller host that [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289) adds for the bulbs.

Today `controllers/lifx` qualifies only vendor 1/product 27/firmware 2.90 (the A19 from [#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/17)). Any other model is reported unsupported. The [pinned product catalog](https://github.com/LIFX/products/blob/8adbe485db11621639f693f3a1510603f029c902/products.json) lists four Beam product IDs (38, 56, 119, 120). All are color and multizone, and their temperature range and extended-multizone support depend on product and firmware. The owner's Beam has not been identified yet.

### Smallest useful implementation

1. **Identify the Beam (read-only, at pickup).** With the owner's IP and permission, send only `GetVersion` (32), `GetHostFirmware` (14), `LightGet` (101) and `GetExtendedColorZones` (511) to UDP 56700, as in #17. Record product, firmware, zone count and catalog capabilities in a comment. No broadcast, no `Set` messages.
2. **Qualify that exact product and firmware** in the controller's qualification table. Keep the A19 entry unchanged. Report the temperature range the catalog gives for that firmware.
3. **Whole-Beam controls.** Power uses `DeviceSetPower`. Color and temperature set every zone to one HSBK, which is what "set the Beam to blue" means.
4. **Brightness keeps the zone pattern.** A plain `LightSetColor` sets all zones to one color, so today's brightness path would flatten a multi-color scene set in the LIFX app. For a multizone device, brightness reads the zones with `GetExtendedColorZones`, scales each zone's brightness, and writes them back in one `SetExtendedColorZones` (510), inside the same queue turn. If the qualified firmware lacks extended multizone, stop and ask the owner before using the legacy zone messages.
5. **Profile and snapshot.** Report zone count and whether the device is multizone in the `lighting` snapshot, and add them to the `lifx-light` profile with a minor version if the owner-facing view needs them. Controller v1 is unchanged. Read `docs/controller-contract.md` before changing any wire value.
6. **Hub and dashboard.** Nothing new beyond #289, since the Beam is another device in the same host configuration. Check that the LIFX component view renders it with the right controls available.

Dependencies: #289 for the hub, dashboard and MCP path. Steps 1-4 touch only `controllers/lifx` and can start before #289 merges. #289 is in progress in another worktree, so coordinate with its owner before editing `controllers/lifx` in parallel.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- One writer: the Beam is owned by the #289 host through the existing per-device queue. No second process talks to it, and nothing polls or scans the LAN.
- The A19's qualification, commands and tests stay unchanged.
- A brightness change never flattens the zone pattern. A zone read that fails before the write reports no write effects; an unacknowledged write stays `uncertain`, as it does today.
- Manual changes in the LIFX app are left alone until the next explicit command. Nothing here adds automatic status painting.
- The Beam's IP stays in private host configuration, never in Git, issues or the browser.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. Installation and the physical check are the companion hardware issue.

- The qualification comment records product, firmware, zone count and catalog capabilities, without the IP or serial.
- Fake-transport tests cover: the qualified Beam accepted and other Beam IDs or firmware rejected; power, color and temperature on all zones; brightness preserving a mixed zone pattern with an exact packet fixture; a failed zone read with no write; an unacknowledged zone write reported `uncertain`; the A19 unchanged.
- With fakes, the dashboard shows a Beam component with the right controls, and `hub_devices` lists it.
- `npm run build`, `typecheck`, `test:lifx`, the contract suites, and the hub, MCP and dashboard suites pass.
- Any dashboard change beyond #289's LIFX view needs the owner's UI approval under the SDLC UI scope.

### Meaningful deferrals

- **Per-zone gradients and scenes from B.U.N.N.Y.** Use the LIFX app for now; the controller leaves app scenes alone. Revisit when the owner asks for zone control or [#267](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/267) defines coordinated looks.
- **Firmware effects (move, etc.).** Stay off, as for the A19. Revisit with #267 or a moments story under [#292](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/292).
- **Agent status on the Beam.** Belongs to [#20](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/20)'s choice of which lights show status.
- **Other Beam product IDs or firmware.** Unsupported until qualified; a firmware update needs a new read-only check.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `b15890b`.

- **Complexity: medium.** Two new protocol messages and a multizone read-modify-write inside the existing queue, plus a profile addition.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The product ID, firmware and extended-multizone support are unknown until the read-only check.
- **Impact: medium.** Commands change a physical light. Effects are reversible, and a wrong brightness write could flatten an app scene the owner would have to reapply.

**Readiness:** blocked on the owner's Beam IP and read-only permission for step 1. Hub visibility also needs #289. This issue does not authorize installation or `Set` messages to the Beam.

## Guide

**Topic:** nanoleaf-devices
**Note:** Qualify the owner's LIFX Beam read-only, support it as one light whose brightness keeps its zone pattern, and show it in B.U.N.N.Y. through the #289 host.

title: Install and verify the LIFX Beam in B.U.N.N.Y.
body:
## Outcome

Control the owner's LIFX Beam from the installed B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard in one short session the owner watches, following the #155 pattern.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] **Prepare.** Name the installation owner and confirm the Beam's IP in the private host configuration. Get permission for the configuration change and lighting sequence. Record installed hub and local controller host versions with their source revisions. Confirm the #289 host is the only Beam writer.
- [ ] **Starting and final state.** Note the current power, color and whether an app scene is showing, plus the intended final state. Mark unknown values unknown.
- [ ] **Controls.** From the dashboard, try power off/on, brightness, one color and one temperature. Compare each receipt with what the owner sees.
- [ ] **Zone pattern.** Set a multi-color scene in the LIFX app, then change brightness from B.U.N.N.Y. The pattern should dim, not turn one color.
- [ ] **Manual control.** Make a change in the LIFX app. Confirm B.U.N.N.Y. leaves it alone until the next explicit command.
- [ ] **Record.** One checklist comment with versions, results, failures and the final state. Keep the IP and credentials out of it.

## Evidence and limits

Transport receipts are distinct from what the owner saw. Detailed logs only for failures. A defect needing code is a separate focused issue. This is a functional check of one Beam, not a reliability run.

## Dependencies and ownership

Owner: hub coordinator with the owner. Requires [#319](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/319) and [#289](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/289) delivered and the #289 host installed. This issue alone grants no permission to install software or operate devices. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md.

title: Show dashboard controls for a Nanoleaf device with a read-only integration snapshot
body:
### Outcome and real setup

Show the dashboard's general controls for the NL22 Light Panels. [codex-nanoleaf#113](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/113) ([PR #164](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/164)) makes the Panels a second Nanoleaf controller device. The Panels' `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` snapshot is read-only: it keeps the exact key set, but it marks `settings.set`, `elements.assign`, `task.assign` and `project.color` as `{supported: false, scope: "control"}` and lists no elements. Setup: one operator and the Linux Nanoleaf installation with the Lines (`wall`) and the Panels (`panels`) as two hub controller entries sharing one endpoint and credential.

Today two things block it:

- `validateIntegrationSnapshot` (`apps/hub/src/integration.ts:39`) requires `supported: true` for all four operations, so `integrationSnapshot()` throws `incompatible-controller` for the Panels.
- The dashboard (`apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx:270`) loads the v1 snapshot and the integration snapshot in one `try`. When the integration read fails, it never stores the v1 snapshot, so the Panels page shows "General controls unavailable: no controller snapshot". The hub's v1 routes work for the Panels.

### Smallest useful implementation

- Accept `supported: false` (with `scope: "control"`) for the four configuration operations in `validateIntegrationSnapshot`, and hide or disable the matching edit forms when an operation is unsupported.
- Optionally, keep the v1 snapshot and general controls when the integration snapshot fails.

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- The closed validation of every other key.
- The Lines' snapshot shape and editing.
- The hub browser never receives credentials.
- No new routes.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- A hub test fixture for a read-only Nanoleaf integration snapshot validates.
- The dashboard shows mode, power, brightness and scene controls for that component, with no configuration edit forms.
- Existing Nanoleaf and Pixoo fixtures still pass.

### Meaningful deferrals

Panels animations and configuration edits through the extension remain Nanoleaf-side work: the #92 follow-up and codex-nanoleaf#47.

### Guide placement

Nanoleaf devices: the Panels gain dashboard control once codex-nanoleaf#113 is installed.

title: Show real LIFX power in B.U.N.N.Y. and stop presenting controls a device cannot use
body:
### Outcome and real setup

These problems were found during #289's installed check on 2026-09-25. The setup was B.U.N.N.Y. on the installed hub 0.3.5, the LIFX A19 `pendant-1`, the LIFX Beam `beam` and the Tidbyt, all served by the local controller host.

- The bulb was off, but its Power control showed "On". Power was unknown, and the control starts at "On" as an unlabeled placeholder. Because the placeholder already read "On", turning the bulb on meant sending Off and then On. A brightness change does not turn a bulb on, so it had no visible effect until then.
- The Tidbyt page, and `beam`'s, shows four disabled general-control forms. They look clickable because disabled buttons are only drawn at half opacity.

Wanted: opening a LIFX bulb shows its actual on or off state within a few seconds. The Power control starts from what is known, or asks when nothing is. A device with no controls says so in one line. Disabled buttons look disabled everywhere in B.U.N.N.Y.

### Smallest useful implementation

- **Host, on-demand read.** When a qualified LIFX bulb's snapshot is read, through the v1 or the lighting route, and the bulb has no reading, or its last reading is 30 s old or more, the host queues one read-only `refresh()` (LightGet) through the bulb's queue. The snapshot answers at once from memory, and the next dashboard read, about 5 s later, shows the result. Reads are limited to one per bulb per 30 s, and happen only while something reads the snapshot. Unqualified bulbs such as `beam` are never read.
- **Dashboard Power control.** Start from desired power when known, otherwise from the observed power when known, otherwise from no selection, with a hint that current power is unknown. Show the last reading and its age in the hint.
- **Dashboard devices without controls.** General controls show a form only for each declared capability, plus one line naming the undeclared ones. A component that declares none of them, like the Tidbyt, shows one line only. This removes the same dead forms from the LIFX pages (media and scenes), the Pixoo (scenes) and the wall (media); it was refined during delivery on 2026-09-25. A LIFX bulb whose lighting capabilities declare neither color nor temperature gets one line for Lighting.
- **Disabled buttons,** across B.U.N.N.Y.: a clearly distinct disabled style from skin tokens, keeping contrast checks passing.

Dependencies: none. Related: #20 (automatic LIFX status, unchanged).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Reads only. The host sends no Set messages and never paints, and a manual change in the LIFX app stays until the next explicit command. Traffic goes only to configured, qualified bulbs, through each bulb's queue within `maxPending`. A read never reserves a request ID or changes a configuration revision or generation. A failed read keeps the last observation and its age.
- With no snapshot readers, the host sends no traffic.
- The Tidbyt stays status only. Pixoo and Nanoleaf controls are unchanged except for the Power starting rule and the disabled styling. A Nanoleaf whose power is unknown now also starts with no selection instead of "On".
- Command guards, receipts, locks and the shared command lifecycle are unchanged.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: source. Installation is a separate step, on the owner's explicit request.

- Host tests with fake transports:
  - A snapshot read of a bulb with no reading, or one 30 s old, queues exactly one LightGet.
  - Repeated reads inside 30 s, and reads while a read is queued, send nothing.
  - With no reads, there is no traffic, and an unqualified bulb is never read.
  - A failed read keeps the previous observation.
  - Request IDs are unchanged.
- Dashboard browser checks, with the real host and fakes:
  - With power unknown, both On and Off can be sent.
  - With an observed-off bulb, the control starts at Off and the hint shows the reading.
  - Tidbyt and `beam` each show one line and no forms.
  - LIFX, Pixoo and wall pages show no form for an undeclared capability.
  - Disabled buttons have a distinct computed style, and the accessibility scan passes.
- UI approval by the owner on the current candidate.
- After an authorized install: opening `pendant-1` shows its real power within a few seconds.

### Meaningful deferrals

- Beam support: multizone qualification of product 38 in the LIFX controller. Until then `beam` has no controls; manage it in the LIFX app. Revisit when the owner wants Beam controls.

## Work assessment

Delivery assessment, 2026-09-25, against hub `main` `9f13c08`.

- **Complexity: low to medium.** One bounded, read-triggered refresh in the host; the Power starting rule, a no-controls line and disabled styling in the dashboard. The existing command lifecycle is untouched.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The LIFX controller already has a read-only `refresh()`. The owner asked for the on-load read on 2026-09-25, knowing it relaxes #289's "never reads on its own".
- **Impact: low to medium.** It adds bulb reads while B.U.N.N.Y. is open, and changes shared UI for every device.
- **Readiness: ready.**

## Guide

**Topic:** bunny-controls
**Note:** Real LIFX power on page load, no dead controls for status-only devices, and clearly disabled buttons.

title: Keep the now-playing displays working when the selected playback source changes
body:
### Outcome and real setup

The Tidbyt now-playing tile and the Pixoo card from [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38) keep showing what is playing when the owner switches the hub's selected playback source. The trigger is [#301](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/301), which adds the Sonos Move as a selectable source.

Today both displays pin `sourceId: "ht-a9"`: the Tidbyt runner's `nowPlaying` block and the Pixoo's `agent-monitor/playback.json`. Both read with credentials whose `devices` list only `ht-a9`. Each display also rejects a snapshot for any other source ID as a failed read. So once the Move is selected, the hub answers 403 and the displays show nothing after 30 s, with no error the owner can see.

Setup: one operator, the installed hub, the Tidbyt runner inside the local controller host from #318, and the Pixoo user service.

### Smallest useful implementation

Pick one when this is defined:

- **(a)** Documented reconfiguration: when the selected source changes, update both display configurations and both credentials' `devices`, then restart the host and the Pixoo service.
- **(b)** Let each display follow the hub's selected source. It would accept whatever `sourceId` the snapshot names, with credentials listing every configured source.

(b) needs a decision, because the strict source check was deliberate: it stops a display from showing another source's music. An unavailable selected source must still show as unavailable (see the architecture's Shared playback section).

### Behavior and protections to preserve

- Read-only credentials, one per display.
- No playback commands from displays.
- The stale and removal rules.
- One writer per device.
- A display never shows a source the owner did not select.

### Observable acceptance and planned evidence

- Fake-feed tests in the Tidbyt and Pixoo suites for a selected-source change.
- A physical check after #301 is installed, if the owner authorizes one.
- Delivery target: source merged in the affected repositories.

### Meaningful deferrals

Two concurrently observed sources stay out of scope, as in #301.

**Note:** Keep the now-playing displays working when the selected playback source changes.

title: Send moments from the hub through controller contract 1.1
body:
> Backlog placeholder, filed on 2026-09-25 from the #292 closeout at the owner's request. It holds the idea until it is clarified and defined. It does not authorize implementation, installation or device changes.

### Outcome

The hub reads controllers at API 1.1 and sends them moments through one shared sender. Rules (#45, #293, #298), agent proposals (#295) and choreography (#297) then reuse it instead of each building their own. Today the hub's controller client only validates 1.0 snapshots and cannot send a moment.

### Starting points

- Read snapshots and feeds with the `apiVersion=1.1` query parameter, and validate them against `snapshotV1_1` and `feedV1_1` from [`controller-contracts-v1.1.0`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/controller-contracts-v1.1.0).
- A controller that serves only 1.0 answers a versioned read with `invalid-request`; the Nanoleaf controller and #318's local controller host do this today. In that case, read again without the parameter, treat the controller as 1.0-only and send it no moments. Decide when to probe again, for example when the controller's epoch changes.
- Build each moment request from the device's latest snapshot:
  - the ticket from `nextRequestId`;
  - the expected configuration revision and generation;
  - `start` computed from `sampleClock` plus the hub's elapsed monotonic time, as [the contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/controller-contract.md#moments-api-11) describes.
- Pass `capabilities.moments` and `state.moment` through to the dashboard and MCP reads.
- Fake-controller tests can come first. An end-to-end check needs one controller that serves 1.1: jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf#158 or jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade#92.

### Protections

- One writer per device. The hub goes through each controller's own queue.
- 1.0 controllers and 1.0 readers keep working unchanged.
- The hub never re-sends a moment after its start window, and never re-sends one after a hub restart.
- Reads and reconnects never send commands.

**Readiness:** backlog. It follows #292 and comes before the first story that sends a moment (#293, #295, #297 or #298).

body:

Every open story shows a current starting-session recommendation in the work guide. The #252 pass (PR #266) assessed the 121 stories open on the morning of 2026-09-25. ## Assessment and readiness

Planning, 2026-09-25, Hub main `4df92c5`. Complexity low: repeat of a delivered procedure. Uncertainty low. Impact low: guide presentation. Ready after #324's topic writes.

**Topic:** work-guide

body:

When the phone streams to the Sony HT-A9 alone, the hub can resume a paused song. Today it cannot: the #242 qualification showed the receiver's network API rejects every resume form, while Sony's [remote control guide](https://helpguide.sony.net/ht/a9/v1/en/contents/TP1000029196.html) documents the remote's Play/Pause button as "starts, pauses, or re-starts playback (resume play)".

- The command has no acknowledgment. The source already polls `getPlayingContentInfo`, so the existing uncertain-result rule confirms or reports the outcome the same way it does for pause.

### Open questions

- Whether the remote button resumes an AirPlay session at all.
- Which sender, and whether it lives beside the hub or inside a controller of its own with one writer.
- Whether this is still wanted once #233 gives play through the Move for grouped playback.

**Readiness:** backlog. It needs the remote-button check.
